problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.k_eq_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_one : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.k_eq_three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_three : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.k_eq_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_two : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.k_eq_zero)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_zero : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 5, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.prime_tuples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.prime_tuples {k : ℕ} (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hp : ∀ (a : Fin k → ℕ+) (b : Fin k → ℕ) (hab : ∀ p, p.Prime → ∃ n, ¬ p ∣ ∏ i, (a i * n + b i)), Set.Infinite {n | ∀ i : Fin k, (a i * n + b i).Prime} ) : Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252 (erdos_252.variants.schinzel)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_252.variants.schinzel (hs : ∀ (fs : Finset (Polynomial ℤ)), (∀ f ∈ fs, BunyakovskyCondition f) → SchinzelCondition fs → Infinite ↑{n | ∀ f ∈ fs, Prime (Polynomial.eval (↑n) f).natAbs}) : ∀ k, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 253 (erdos_253)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_253 : ¬ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, 0 < a 0 → RepresentsAPs a → (Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a <| n + 1 : ℝ) / a n) (𝓝 1)) → subsetSums (Set.range a) ∈ Filter.cofinite
problems.humanStatement:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dotsc$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that
$\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i} \to 1$. If every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many
integers which are the sum of distinct $a_i$ then every sufficiently large integer is
the sum of distinct $a_i$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 254 (erdos_254.variants.cassels)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_254.variants.cassels : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (((A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard : ℝ) - ((A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard : ℝ)) / Real.log (Real.log x)) atTop atTop) ∧ (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ (distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))^2)) → ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m
problems.humanStatement:
Cassels [Ca60] proved this under the alternative hypotheses $\lim \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert
-\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\log\log x}=\infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}^2=\infty$ for every
$\theta\in (0,1)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 257 (erdos_257)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_257 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → Irrational (∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 257 (erdos_257.variants.tsum_top)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_257.variants.tsum_top : Irrational <| ∑' n, n.divisors.card / (2 ^ n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n}
$$
is irrational.

[Er48] Erdős, P., _On arithmetical properties of Lambert series_. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 257 (erdos_257.variants.tsum_top_eq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_257.variants.tsum_top_eq : ∑' n, 1 / (2 ^ n - 1 : ℝ) = ∑' n, n.divisors.card / (2 ^ n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} = \sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n},
$$
where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 258 (erdos_258.variants.constant)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : answer(True) ↔ ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ), Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1)))
problems.humanStatement:
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 258 (erdos_258.variants.monotone)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a → Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 26 (erdos_26.variants.rusza)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_26.variants.rusza : ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧ ¬IsThick A ∧ ∀ k, ¬IsBehrend (A · + k)
problems.humanStatement: If we allow for $\sum_{a\in A} \frac{1}{a} < \infty$ then Rusza has found a counter-example.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 260 (erdos_260)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_260 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ s : ℝ, StrictMono a → Tendsto (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / n ) atTop atTop → HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / 2 ^ a n) s → Irrational s
problems.humanStatement:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $\frac{a_n}{n} \to \infty$.
Is the sum $\sum_{n}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}$ irrational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263 (erdos_263.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_263.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ 2 ^ n)
problems.humanStatement: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263 (erdos_263.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_263.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsIrrationalitySequence a → atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Must every irrationality sequence $a_n$ in the above sense
satisfy $a_n^{1/n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

Note: this was answered **false** for the *pre-correction* statement, which did not
require monotonicity — the counterexample sequence is not increasing. The problem
was corrected on erdosproblems.com on 2026-04-02 to require increasing sequences;
for the corrected statement this question is **open**. The earlier formal proof
(for the pre-correction definition) is preserved at
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c8cf651906abe91051cf835d4232ad5648412113/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/263.lean#L298

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263 (erdos_263.variants.doubly_exponential_all_but_countable)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_263.variants.doubly_exponential_all_but_countable : ∀ᶠ (α : ℝ) in .cocountable, α > 1 → IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n : ℕ => ⌊α ^ 2 ^ n⌋₊)
problems.humanStatement:
Koizumi [Ko25] showed that $a_n = \lfloor \alpha^{2^n} \rfloor$ is an irrationality sequence
for all but countably many $\alpha > 1$.

[Ko25] Koizumi, J., Irrationality of the reciprocal sum of doubly exponential sequences,
       arXiv:2504.05933 (2025).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263 (erdos_263.variants.folklore)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_263.variants.folklore (a : ℕ -> ℕ) (ha : atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (2 ^ n : ℝ))) atTop) : Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
A folklore result states that any $a_n$ satisfying $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n^{\frac{1}{2^n}} = \infty$
has $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converging to an irrational number.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263 (erdos_263.variants.sub_doubly_exponential)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_263.variants.sub_doubly_exponential (a: ℕ -> ℕ) (ha' : StrictMono a) (ha'' : Summable (fun n : ℕ => 1 / (a n : ℝ))) (ha''' : atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / a n ^ 2) (𝓝 0)) : ¬ IsIrrationalitySequence a
problems.humanStatement:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] proved that any strictly increasing sequence $a_n$ such that
$\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and $\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^2} = 0$ is not
an irrationality sequence in the above sense.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264 (erdos_264.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_264.parts.i : ¬IsIrrationalitySequence (2 ^ ·)
problems.humanStatement:
Is $2^n$ an example of an irrationality sequence? Kovač and Tao proved that it is not [KoTa24]

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264 (erdos_264.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_264.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ IsIrrationalitySequence Nat.factorial
problems.humanStatement: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264 (erdos_264.variants.example)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_264.variants.example : IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n ↦ 2 ^ (2 ^ n))
problems.humanStatement: One example is $2^{2^n}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264 (erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_neg)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_neg {a : ℕ → ℕ} (h₁ : StrictMono a) (h₂ : 0 ∉ Set.range a) (h₃ : Summable ((1 : ℝ) / a ·)) (h₄ : 0 < atTop.liminf fun n ↦ a n ^ 2 * ∑' k : Set.Ioi n, (1 : ℝ) / a k ^ 2) : ¬IsIrrationalitySequence a
problems.humanStatement:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] generally proved that any strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
$a_n$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and
$$
  \liminf_{n \to \infty} (a_n^2 \sum_{k > n} \frac{1}{a_k^2}) > 0
$$
is not an irrationality sequence.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264 (erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_pos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_pos {F : ℕ → ℕ} (hF : atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (F (n + 1) : ℝ) / F n) atTop) : ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsIrrationalitySequence a ∧ (fun n ↦ (a n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n ↦ (F n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
On the other hand, Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] do prove that for any function $F$ with
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{F(n + 1)}{F(n)} = \infty$ there exists such an irrationality sequence with $a_n \sim F(n)$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 266 (erdos_266)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_266 : ¬ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ((∀ n : ℕ, a n ≥ 1) ∧ Summable ((1 : ℝ) / a ·) → ∃ t ≥ (1 : ℕ), Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $a_n$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges.
There exists some integer $t \ge 1$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ is irrational.

This was disproven by Kovač and Tao in [KoTa24].

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 266 (erdos_266.variants.all_rationals)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_266.variants.all_rationals: ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ a 0 ≥ 1 ∧ (∀ t : ℚ, (¬ ∃ n : ℕ, t = -(a n)) → (∃ q : ℚ, HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))) q))
problems.humanStatement:
In fact, Kovač and Tao proved in [KoTa24] that there exists a strictly increasing
sequence $a_n$ of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ converges to a rational
number for all $t \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $t \ne -a_n$ for any $n$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 267 (erdos_267.variants.fibonacci_inverse_sum)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_267.variants.fibonacci_inverse_sum : Irrational <| ∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib k)
problems.humanStatement:
The sum $\sum_n \frac 1 {F_{n}}$ itself was proved to be irrational by André-Jeannin.

Ref: André-Jeannin, Richard, _Irrationalité de la somme des inverses de certaines suites récurrentes_.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 267 (erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (n (k+1) / k.succ : ℝ)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac {n_k}{k} \to \infty$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 269 (erdos_269.variants.infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_269.variants.infinite (P : Set ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_inf : P.Infinite) : Irrational (series P)
problems.humanStatement:
This theorem addresses the case where the set of primes $P$ is infinite. In this case the sum is
irrational.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 269 (erdos_269.variants.irrational)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_269.variants.irrational : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2), Irrational (series (P : Set ℕ))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
irrational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 269 (erdos_269.variants.rational)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_269.variants.rational : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2), ∃ (q : ℚ), q = (series (P : Set ℕ))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
rational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 272 (erdos_272)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_272 : (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 272 (erdos_272.variants.isBigO_sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_272.variants.isBigO_sq : (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ 2
problems.humanStatement: Simonovits and Sós have shown that $t\ll N^2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 272 (erdos_272.variants.szabo)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_272.variants.szabo : (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N - N ^ 2 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N : ℕ ↦ N ^ ((5 : ℝ) / 3) * (Real.log N) ^ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 272 (erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong : (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N - N ^ 2 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 273 (erdos_273)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_273 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)}
problems.humanStatement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 273 (erdos_273.variants.three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_273.variants.three : answer(True) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, ∀ i, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ p ∧ c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)}
problems.humanStatement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 274 (erdos_274)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], 1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι], ∀ (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j)
problems.humanStatement:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 276 (erdos_276)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_276 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ), IsLucasSequence a ∧ (∀ k, (a k).Composite) ∧ (∀ n > 1, ∃ k, Nat.gcd n (a k) = 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 277 (erdos_277)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_277 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧ ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 279 (erdos_279)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_279 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : Nat, k ≥ 3 → ∃ a : Nat → Nat, ∃ N : Nat, (∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → a p < p) ∧ ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p : Nat, ∃ t ≥ k, p.Prime ∧ n = a p + t * p
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 28 (erdos_28)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_28 (A : Set ℕ) (h : (A + A)ᶜ.Finite) : limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (sumRep A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = (⊤ : ℕ∞)
problems.humanStatement:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
 $\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282 (erdos_282)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_282 {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) (hx_den : Odd x.den) : greedyUnitFractionRem { n | Odd n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282 (erdos_282.variants.fibonacci)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_282.variants.fibonacci {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : greedyUnitFractionRem .univ x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282 (erdos_282.variants.general)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_282.variants.general (x : ℚ) (A : Set ℕ) : greedyUnitFractionRem A x =ᶠ[atTop] 0 ↔ (x, A) ∈ (answer(sorry) : Set (ℚ × Set ℕ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282 (erdos_282.variants.graham)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_282.variants.graham {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) {a d : ℕ} (hd : 1 < d) (h : (x.den / x.den.gcd (a.gcd d)).gcd (d / a.gcd d) = 1) : (greedyUnitFractionRem { n | n ≡ a [MOD d] } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0) ↔ answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Graham has shown that $\frac{m}{n}$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions
with denominators $\equiv a\pmod{d}$ if and only if
$$\left(\frac{n}{(n,a,d)},\frac{d}{(a,d)}\right)=1.$$
Does the greedy algorithm always
terminate in such cases?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282 (erdos_282.variants.sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_282.variants.sq : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ x : ℚ, (x : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ico 0 (π ^ 2 / 6 - 1) ∪ Set.Ico 1 (π ^ 2 / 6) → greedyUnitFractionRem { n | IsSquare n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0
problems.humanStatement:
Graham has also shown that $x$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions with
square denominators if and only if $x\in [0,\pi^2/6-1)\cup [1,\pi^2/6)$. Does the
greedy algorithm for this always terminate? Erdős and Graham believe not - indeed, perhaps it
fails to terminate almost always.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.alekseyev)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.alekseyev : ∀ (m : ℕ), m > 8542 → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧ (∑ n ∈ S, (1 / (n : ℚ))) = 1 ∧ (∑ n ∈ S, (n : ℤ)^2) = (m : ℤ)
problems.humanStatement: Alekseyev [Al19] has proved this when $p(x)=x^2$, for all $m>8542$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.burr)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.burr : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≥ 1 → ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ M : Multiset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ M, 1 ≤ n) ∧ (M.map (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℚ))).sum = 1 ∧ (M.map (fun n ↦ (n : ℤ)^k)).sum = (m : ℤ)
problems.humanStatement: Burr has proved this if $p(x)=x^k$ with $k\geq 1$ and if we allow $n_i=n_j$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.cassels)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.cassels : ∀ (p : ℤ[X]), 0 < p.leadingCoeff → (¬ ∃ (d : ℤ), d ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ (n : ℤ), n ≥ 1 → d ∣ p.eval n) → ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧ (∑ n ∈ S, p.eval (n : ℤ)) = (m : ℤ)
problems.humanStatement:
Cassels [Ca60] has proved that these conditions on the polynomial imply every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of $p(n_i)$ with distinct $n_i$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.graham)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.graham : Condition X
problems.humanStatement: Graham [Gr63] has proved this when $p(x)=x$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.graham_alpha)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.graham_alpha : ∀ (p : ℤ[X]) (α : ℚ), 0 < p.leadingCoeff → (¬ ∃ (d : ℤ), d ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ (n : ℤ), n ≥ 1 → d ∣ p.eval n) → α > 0 → ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧ (∑ n ∈ S, (1 / (n : ℚ))) = α ∧ (∑ n ∈ S, p.eval (n : ℤ)) = (m : ℤ)
problems.humanStatement:
Graham also conjectures that this remains true with $1$ replaced by an arbitrary rational $\alpha>0$
(provided $m$ is taken sufficiently large depending on $\alpha$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_linear)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_linear : ∀ b : ℤ, 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 5000 → Condition (X + C b)
problems.humanStatement:
van Doorn [vD25] has investigated the question of what 'sufficiently large' means for $p(x)=x$.
van Doorn has also proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 5000$, then the conjecture is true.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283 (erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_quadratic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_quadratic : ∀ b : ℤ, 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 800 → Condition (X^2 + C b)
problems.humanStatement:
van Doorn [vD25] has proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x^2 + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 800$, then the conjecture is true.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 285 (erdos_285)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_285 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ᵉ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧ 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i }) (h : ∀ k ∈ S, IsLeast { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n) (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) } (f k)), ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)), ∀ k ∈ S, f k = (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ with
$$
  1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
  f(k) = (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1} k ?
$$

Proved by Martin [Ma00].

[Ma00] Martin, Greg, _Denser Egyptian fractions_. Acta Arith. (2000), 231-260.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 285 (erdos_285.variants.lb)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_285.variants.lb (f : ℕ → ℕ) (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧ 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i }) (h : ∀ k ∈ S, IsLeast { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n) (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) } (f k)) : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)), ∀ k ∈ S, (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1) ≤ f k
problems.humanStatement: It is trivial that $f(k)\geq (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1}k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287 (erdos_287)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_287 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ → ∑ i : Fin k, 1/ (s i : ℝ) = 1 → 3 ≤ max_gap k s
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287 (erdos_287.test.best_possible)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_287.test.best_possible : let s : Fin 3 → ℕ
problems.humanStatement:
The example $1 = \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}$ shows that $3$ would be best possible here:
the sequence $(2, 3, 6)$ is a valid Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with
`max_gap = 3`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287 (erdos_287.variants.gap_at_least_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_287.variants.gap_at_least_two : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ → ∑ i : Fin k, 1 / (s i : ℝ) = 1 → 2 ≤ max_gap k s
problems.humanStatement:
The lower bound of $\geq 2$ is equivalent to saying that $1$ is not the sum of reciprocals of
consecutive integers, proved by Erdős [Er32].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287 (erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)
problems.humanStatement:
For all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$ is also prime.

This is an open conjecture. If true, it would imply `erdos_287` for all but at most finitely
many exceptions (see `erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies`).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287 (erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies : type_of% erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture → ∃ (k₀ : ℕ), ∀ᵉ (k : ℕ) (hk₀ : k₀ ≤ k) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ → ∑ i : Fin k, 1 / (s i : ℝ) = 1 → 3 ≤ max_gap k s
problems.humanStatement:
The conjecture `erdos_287` would follow for all but at most finitely many exceptions if it were
known that, for all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$
is also prime.

More precisely: if the prime conjecture holds, then there exists $k_0$ such that for all
$k \geq k_0$, any Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with $k$ terms and all terms $> 1$
must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 288 (erdos_288)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_288 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { I : Fin 2 → ℕ+ × ℕ+ | ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin 2, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n }
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 288 (erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k > 2, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ | ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n }
problems.humanStatement: Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 288 (erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { (I, n₂) : (ℕ+ × ℕ+) × ℕ+ | I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, ∑ n₁ ∈ Set.Icc I.1 I.2, (n₁⁻¹ : ℚ) + (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ) = n }
problems.humanStatement: This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 288 (erdos_288.variants.k_intervals)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_288.variants.k_intervals : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ | ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n }
problems.humanStatement: It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 289 (erdos_289)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_289 : answer(sorry) ↔ (∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ∃ I : Fin k → ℕ × ℕ, (∀ i, (I i).1 < (I i).2) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (I i).2 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 < (I i).1) ∧ ∑ i, ∑ n ∈ .Icc (I i).1 (I i).2, (n⁻¹ : ℚ) = 1)
problems.humanStatement:
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$ with $|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}.
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1 }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔ { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) > 1 }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

Steinerberger has observed that the answer to the second question is trivially yes: for example, any
$n$ which begins with a $2$ in base $3$ has $3\mid (a_n,L_n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic : Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop (fun x : ℕ ↦ ((((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ))) (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) / Real.log x)
problems.humanStatement:
This leads to a heuristic prediction (see for example a preprint of Shiu [Sh16]) of
$\asymp\frac{x}{\log x}$ for the number of $n\in [1,x]$ such that $(a_n,L_n)=1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ))) atTop (nhds 0)
problems.humanStatement:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.variants.steinerberger_generalization)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.variants.steinerberger_generalization (n p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hpn : p ≤ n) : let k
problems.humanStatement:
More generally, if the leading digit of $n$ in base $p$ is $p-1$ then $p\mid (a_n,L_n)$. There is
in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: a prime $p\leq n$ divides $(a_n,L_n)$ if and only if
$p$ divides the numerator of $1+\cdots+\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is the leading digit of $n$ in base
$p$. This can be seen by writing $a_n = \frac{L_n}{1}+\cdots+\frac{L_n}{n}$ and observing that the
right-hand side is congruent to $1+\cdots+1/k$ modulo $p$. (The previous claim about $p-1$ follows
immediately from Wolstenholme's theorem.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 (erdos_291.variants.wu_yan)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_291.variants.wu_yan (h_indep : LinearIndependent ℚ (fun p : {p : ℕ // p.Prime} ↦ 1 / Real.log (p : ℝ))) : atTop.limsup (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) > 1)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ) : EReal)) = 1
problems.humanStatement:
Wu and Yan [WuYa22] have proved, conditional on $\frac{1}{\log p}$ being linearly independent
over $\mathbb{Q}$ for any finite collection of primes $p$ (itself a consequence of Schanuel's
conjecture), that the set of $n$ for which $(a_n,L_n)>1$ has upper density $1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 295 (erdos_295)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_295 : answer(sorry) ↔ Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun N => k N - (rexp 1 - 1)*N) Filter.atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exists
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Is it true that $\lim_{N \to \infty} k(N) - (e - 1)N = \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 295 (erdos_295.variants.erdos_straus)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_295.variants.erdos_straus : ∃ᵉ (C > 0) (O > 0), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (k N - (rexp 1 - 1)*N) ∈ Set.Ioc (-C) (O * N / (N : ℝ).log)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Straus have proved the existence of some constant $c>0$
such that $-c < k(N)-(e-1)N \ll \frac N {\log N}$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 298 (erdos_298.variants.natural_density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_298.variants.natural_density : answer(True) ↔ (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → A.HasPosDensity → ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1)
problems.humanStatement: The literal natural-density interpretation of Erdős Problem 298 follows from [Bl21].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 299 (erdos_299.variants.density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_299.variants.density : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / n = 1
problems.humanStatement:
The corresponding question is also false if one replaces sequences such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$
with sets of positive density, as follows from [Bl21].

The statement is as follows:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density (and hence certainly if $A$ has positive
density) then there is a finite $S \subset A$ such that $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 3 (erdos_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_3 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ, (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) → ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k
problems.humanStatement:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N} has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 30 (erdos_30)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_30 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > 0), (fun N => h N - (N : Real).sqrt) =O[atTop] fun N => (N : ℝ)^(ε : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varespilon}(N^\varespilon)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302 (erdos_302.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_302.parts.i (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 answer(sorry))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that there are no
solutions to
$$\frac{1}{a}= \frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}$$
with distinct $a,b,c\in A$? Estimate $f(N)$.

The colouring version of this is [303], which was solved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302 (erdos_302.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_302.parts.ii (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) : ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 ((1 : ℝ) / 2))
problems.humanStatement:
In particular, is $f(N)=(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))N$?

This is false: it is contradicted by Cambie's lower bound of $(5/8+o(1))N$ recorded below,
since $5/8 > 1/2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302 (erdos_302.variants.lower_five_eighths)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_302.variants.lower_five_eighths (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ((5 : ℝ) / 8 - ε) * N ≤ f N
problems.humanStatement:
Stijn Cambie has observed that
$$f(N)\geq (5/8+o(1))N,$$
taking $A$ to be all odd integers $\leq N/4$ and all integers in $[N/2,N]$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302 (erdos_302.variants.lower_half)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_302.variants.lower_half (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε) * N ≤ f N
problems.humanStatement:
One can take either $A$ to be all odd integers in $[1,N]$ or all integers in $[N/2,N]$ to show
$f(N)\geq (1/2+o(1))N$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302 (erdos_302.variants.upper_nine_tenths)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_302.variants.upper_nine_tenths (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) ≤ ((9 : ℝ) / 10 + ε) * N
problems.humanStatement:
Wouter van Doorn has proved [va25] that
$$f(N) \leq (9/10+o(1))N.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 304 (erdos_304.variants.lower_1950)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_304.variants.lower_1950 : (fun b : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log b)) =O[atTop] (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
In 1950, Erdős [Er50c] proved the lower bound $$\log \log b \ll N(b)$$.
[Er50c] Erdős, P., Az ${1}/{x_1} + {1}/{x_2} + \ldots + {1}/{x_n} =A/B$ egyenlet eg\'{E}sz sz\'{A}m\'{u} megold\'{A}sairól. Mat. Lapok (1950), 192-210.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 304 (erdos_304.variants.upper_1950)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_304.variants.upper_1950 : (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun b => Real.log b / Real.log (Real.log b))
problems.humanStatement:
In 1950, Erdős [Er50c] proved the upper bound $$N(b) \ll \log b / \log \log b$$.
[Er50c] Erdős, P., Az ${1}/{x_1} + {1}/{x_2} + \ldots + {1}/{x_n} =A/B$ egyenlet eg\'{E}sz sz\'{A}m\'{u} megold\'{A}sairól. Mat. Lapok (1950), 192-210.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 304 (erdos_304.variants.upper_1985)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_304.variants.upper_1985 : (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun b => Real.sqrt (Real.log b))
problems.humanStatement:
In 1985 Vose [Vo85] proved the upper bound $$N(b) \ll \sqrt{\log b}$$.
[Vo85] Vose, Michael D., Egyptian fractions. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1985), 21-24.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 306 (erdos_306)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_306 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (q : ℚ), 0 < q → Squarefree q.den → ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ (n : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ), n 0 = 1 ∧ StrictMono n ∧ (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), ω (n i) = 2 ∧ Ω (n i) = 2) ∧ q = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), (1 : ℚ) / (n i)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\frac a b\in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ with $b$ squarefree. Are there integers $1 < n_1 < \dots < n_k$,
each the product of two distinct primes, such that $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 306 (erdos_306.variants.integer_three_primes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_306.variants.integer_three_primes (m : ℕ) (h : 0 < m) : ∃ k > (0 : ℕ), ∃ (n : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ), n 0 = 1 ∧ ∀ i, (hik : i < k) → n ⟨i, by omega⟩ < n ⟨(i + 1), by omega⟩ ∧ (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), ω (n i) = 3 ∧ Ω (n i) = 3) ∧ m = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), (1 : ℚ) / (n i)
problems.humanStatement:
Every positive integer can be expressed as an Egyptian fraction where each denominator is the
product of three distinct primes.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 307 (erdos_307)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_307 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P Q : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, q.Prime) ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (p : ℚ)⁻¹) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (q : ℚ)⁻¹)
problems.humanStatement:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

Asked by Barbeau [Ba76].

[Ba76] Barbeau, E. J., _Computer challenge corner: Problem 477: A brute force program._

problems.title: Erdős Problem 307 (erdos_307.variants.coprime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_307.variants.coprime : answer(True) ↔ ∃ P Q : Finset ℕ, 0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧ 1 < #P ∧ 1 < #Q ∧ Set.Pairwise P Nat.Coprime ∧ Set.Pairwise Q Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (p : ℚ)⁻¹) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (q : ℚ)⁻¹)
problems.humanStatement:
Instead of asking for sets of primes, ask only that all elements in the sets be relatively coprime.

Cambie has found several examples when this weakened version is true. For example,
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)
$$
and
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{41}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{7}\right).
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 307 (erdos_307.variants.coprime_one_notMem)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_307.variants.coprime_one_notMem : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P Q : Finset ℕ, 0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧ 1 ∉ P ∪ Q ∧ 1 < #P ∧ 1 < #Q ∧ Set.Pairwise P Nat.Coprime ∧ Set.Pairwise Q Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (p : ℚ)⁻¹) * (∑ q ∈ Q, (q : ℚ)⁻¹)
problems.humanStatement: There are no examples known of the weakened coprime version if we insist that $1\not\in P\cup Q$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 312 (erdos_312)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_312 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ ∀ (K : ℝ), 1 < K → ∃ (N₀ : ℕ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℕ), (n ≥ N₀ ∧ (∑ i : Fin n, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹) > K) → ∃ (S : Finset (Fin n)), 1 - Real.exp (-(c * K)) < (∑ i ∈ S, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹) ∧ ∑ i ∈ S, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ 1
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that, for any `K > 1`, whenever `A` is a sufficiently large
finite multiset of integers with $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n > K$ there exists some $S \subseteq A$ such that
$1 - \exp(-(c*K)) < \sum_{n \in S} 1/n \le 1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 313 (erdos_313)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_313 : answer(sorry) ↔ erdos313Solutions.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Are there infinitely many pairs `(m, P)` where `m ≥ 2` is an integer
and `P` is a set of distinct primes such that the following equation holds:
$\sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} = 1 - \frac{1}{m}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 313 (erdos_313.variants.exists_at_least_eight_primary_pseudoperfect)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_313.variants.exists_at_least_eight_primary_pseudoperfect : 8 ≤ (Set.encard {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n})
problems.humanStatement:
There are at least 8 primary pseudoperfect numbers. The first eight terms of
[A54377](https://oeis.org/A54377) are exhibited together with their explicit
prime decompositions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 313 (erdos_313.variants.primary_pseudoperfect_are_infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_313.variants.primary_pseudoperfect_are_infinite : Set.Infinite {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}
problems.humanStatement: It is conjectured that the set of primary pseudoperfect numbers is infinite.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 313 (erdos_313.variants.solution_42_2_3_7)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_42_2_3_7 : (42, {2, 3, 7}) ∈ erdos313Solutions

problems.title: Erdős Problem 313 (erdos_313.variants.solution_6_2_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_6_2_3 : (6, {2, 3}) ∈ erdos313Solutions

problems.title: Erdős Problem 316 (erdos_316.variants.generalized)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_316.variants.generalized (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A.Nonempty ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 ∉ A ∧ ∑ k ∈ A, (1 / k : ℚ) < n ∧ ∀ P : Finpartition A, P.parts.card = n → ∃ p ∈ P.parts, 1 ≤ ∑ n ∈ p, (1 / n : ℚ)
problems.humanStatement:
This is not true in general, as shown by Sándor [Sa97], who observed that the proper divisors of
$120$ form a counterexample. More generally, Sándor shows that for any $n\geq 2$ there exists a
finite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}\backslash\{1\}$ with $\sum_{k\in A}\frac{1}{k} < n$ and no
partition into $n$ parts each of which has $\sum_{k\in A_i}\frac{1}{k}<1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 316 (erdos_316.variants.multiset)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_316.variants.multiset : ∃ A : Multiset ℕ, 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 ∉ A ∧ (A.map ((1 : ℚ) / ·)).sum < 2 ∧ ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Multiset ℕ), A = A₁ + A₂ → 1 ≤ (A₁.map ((1 : ℚ) / ·)).sum ∨ 1 ≤ (A₂.map ((1 : ℚ) / ·)).sum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 317 (erdos_317)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_317 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ δ : Fin n → ℚ, Set.range δ ⊆ {-1, 0, 1} ∧ letI lhs : ℝ
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\geq 1$ there exists some $\delta_k\in \{-1,0,1\}$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ with
$$0< \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{\delta_k}{k}\right\rvert < \frac{c}{2^n}?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 317 (erdos_317.variants.claim2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_317.variants.claim2 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ δ : (Fin n) → ℚ, δ '' Set.univ ⊆ {-1,0,1} → letI lhs
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that for sufficiently large $n$, for any $\delta_k\in \{-1,0,1\}$,
$$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{\delta_k}{k}\right\rvert > \frac{1}{[1,\ldots,n]}$$
whenever the left-hand side is not zero?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 317 (erdos_317.variants.counterexample)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_317.variants.counterexample : ¬ (∀ δ : (Fin 4) → ℚ, δ '' Set.univ ⊆ {-1,0,1} → letI lhs
problems.humanStatement:
`erdos_317.variants.claim2` fails for small $n$, for example
$$\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}=-\frac{1}{12}.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 318 (erdos_318.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.parts.i : ∃ A : Set ℕ, HasPosDensity A ∧ ¬ P₁ A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 318 (erdos_318.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔ P₁ ({n | IsSquare n} \ {1})
problems.humanStatement:
Does the set of squares excluding 1 have property `P₁`?

Larsen [La26] proved that this set does have property `P₁`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 318 (erdos_318.variants.contain_single_even)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.variants.contain_single_even {A : Set ℕ} (hA : {n | n ∈ A ∧ Even n}.ncard = 1) : ¬ P₁ A

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.variants.infinite_AP {A : Set ℕ} (hA : A.IsAPOfLength ⊤) : P₁ A

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.variants.squares : ¬ P₁ ({n | IsSquare n})

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_318.variants.univ : P₁ univ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 (erdos_319)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_319 (N : ℕ) : IsGreatest { #A | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) } answer(sorry)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 (erdos_319.variants.isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_319.variants.isBigO (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ∀ N, IsGreatest { (#A : ℝ) | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) } (c N)) : c =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 (erdos_319.variants.isLittleO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_319.variants.isLittleO (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ∀ N, IsGreatest { (#A : ℝ) | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) } (c N)) : c =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 (erdos_319.variants.isTheta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_319.variants.isTheta (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ∀ N, IsGreatest { (#A : ℝ) | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) } (c N)) : c =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 (erdos_319.variants.lb)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_319.variants.lb : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), (o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (1 - 1 / rexp 1 + o N) * N ≤ sSup { (#A : ℝ) | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) }
problems.humanStatement:
$$
  |A| \geq (1 - \frac{1}{e} + o(1))N
$$
follows from the main result of Croot [Cr01].

[Cr01] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On unit fractions with denominators in short intervals_.
Acta Arith. (2001), 99-114.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32 (erdos_32)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_32 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧ (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun N => (Real.log N) ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = o((\log N)^2)$
and every sufficiently large integer can be written as $p + a$ for some prime $p$ and $a \in A$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32 (erdos_32.variants.liminf_gt_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_32.variants.liminf_gt_one : ∀ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A → (1 : EReal) < liminf (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card / Real.log N : EReal)) atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Must every additive complement $A$ to the primes satisfy
$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}|}{\log N} > 1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32 (erdos_32.variants.log_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_32.variants.log_bound : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧ (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => Real.log N
problems.humanStatement:
Can the bound $O(\log N)$ be achieved for an additive complement to the primes? [Guy04] writes
that Erdős offered \$50 for the solution.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32 (erdos_32.variants.log_squared)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_32.variants.log_squared : ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧ (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => (Real.log N) ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved in [Erd54] that there exists an additive complement $A$ to the primes with
$|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = O((\log N)^2)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32 (erdos_32.variants.ruzsa)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_32.variants.ruzsa : ∀ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A → (Real.exp Real.eulerMascheroniConstant : EReal) ≤ liminf (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card / Real.log N : EReal)) atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa proved that any additive complement $A$ to the primes must satisfy
$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}|}{\log N} \geq e^\gamma$,
where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321 (N : ℕ) : R N = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums
$\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$. What is $R(N)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321.variants.isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321.variants.isBigO : (fun N ↦ (R N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums $\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$. Find the simplest $g(N)$ such that $R(N) = O(g(N))$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321.variants.isLittleO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321.variants.isLittleO : (fun N ↦ (R N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums $\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$. Find the simplest $g(N)$ such that $R(N) = o(g(N))$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321.variants.isTheta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321.variants.isTheta : (fun N ↦ (R N : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums
$\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$. What is $\Theta(R(N))$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321.variants.lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321.variants.lower (N k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hkN : k ≤ log^[k] N) : N / log N * ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 3 k, (log^[i] N) ≤ R N
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
\frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{k} \log_i N \le R(N),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum \sb{1}\spN\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 (erdos_321.variants.upper)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_321.variants.upper (N r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrN : 1 ≤ log^[2 * r] N) : R N ≤ 1 / log 2 * log^[r] N * N / log N * ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 3 r, (log^[i] N)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
R(N) \le \frac{1}{\log 2} \log_r N \left( \frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{r} \log_i N \right),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum \sb{1}\spN\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 323 (erdos_323.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_323.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)) =O[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k k x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

This would have significant applications to Waring's problem. Erdős and Graham describe this as
'unattackable by the methods at our disposal'.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 323 (erdos_323.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_323.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → m < k → (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ ((m : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))) =O[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k m x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that if $m < k$ then $f_{k,m}(x) \gg x^{m/k}$ for sufficiently large $x$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 323 (erdos_323.variants.k_eq_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_323.variants.k_eq_2 : ∃ c > 0, (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f 2 2 x : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ c * (x : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (x : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
The case $k=2$ was resolved by Landau, who showed $f_{2,2}(x) \sim \frac{cx}{\sqrt{\log x}}$ for
some constant $c>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 323 (erdos_323.variants.k_gt_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_323.variants.k_gt_2 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k > 2, (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k k x : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: For $k>2$ it is not known if $f_{k,k}(x)=o(x)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 324 (erdos_324)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_324 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℤ[X], {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => f.eval (a : ℤ) + f.eval (b : ℤ)
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that all the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 324 (erdos_324.variants.quintic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_324.variants.quintic : {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => a ^ 5 + b ^ 5
problems.humanStatement:
Probably $f(x) = x^5$ has the property that the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 325 (erdos_325)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_325 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ (3 / k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg x ^ (3 / k)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 325 (erdos_325.variants.weaker)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_325.variants.weaker : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ ((3 / k : ℝ) - ε)) =O[atTop] (fun x => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow k x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it even true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg_{\epsilon} x ^ (3 / k - \epsilon)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 325 (erdos_325.variants.wooley)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_325.variants.wooley : (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ (0.917 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x => (cardIsSumThreePowerBelow 3 x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
For $k = 3$, the best known is due to Wooley [Wo15]
[Wo15] Wooley, Trevor D., Sums of three cubes, II. Acta Arith. (2015), 73-100.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 326 (erdos_326)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_326 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAddBasisOfOrder 2 → ∃ (b : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono b ∧ ∀ n, b n ∈ A ∧ (Set.range b).IsAddBasis ∧ ∀ (x : ℝ), ¬ Tendsto (fun n ↦ (b n : ℝ) / n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 x)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis of order 2.

Must there exist $B = \{b_1 < b_2 < \dots\} \subseteq A$ which is also a basis such that
$\lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{b_k}{k^2}$ does not exist?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 326 (erdos_326.variants.eq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_326.variants.eq : ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono a) (_ : Set.range a |>.IsAddBasisOfOrder 2) (x : ℝ) (_ : 0 < x), Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a n : ℝ) / n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets (erdos_329)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_329 : sSup {sidonUpperDensity A | (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsSidon A)} = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 329.**
Let `A ⊆ ℕ` be a Sidon set. How large can
`lim sup_{N → ∞} |A ∩ {1,…,N}| / N^{1/2}`
be?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets (erdos_329.variants.converse_implication)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_329.variants.converse_implication : (sSup {sidonUpperDensity A | (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsSidon A)} = 1) → (∀ (A : Finset ℕ), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) → ∃ (D : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n > 0), ↑A ⊆ D ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet D n)
problems.humanStatement:
The converse: if the maximum density is 1, then any finite Sidon set
can be embedded in a perfect difference set modulo $n > 0$.

Since the consequent is false (due to the counterexamples in [Ha47] and [AlMi25]),
this implication is logically equivalent to the statement that the maximum upper
density of Sidon sets is NOT 1.
Because the maximum upper density problem is still open, the truth value of this
implication is also an open research problem.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets (erdos_329.variants.kruckeberg_1961)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_329.variants.kruckeberg_1961 : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsSidon A ∧ sidonUpperDensity A = 1 / Real.sqrt 2
problems.humanStatement:
Krückeberg ([Kr61]) exhibited an infinite Sidon set `A` with
`sidonUpperDensity A = 1 / Real.sqrt 2`, improving Erdős’ earlier
`1 / 2` lower bound.

[Kr61] Krückeberg, Fritz, $B\sb{2}$-Folgen und verwandte Zahlenfolgen. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1961), 53-60.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets (erdos_329.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_329.variants.lower_bound : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsSidon A ∧ sidonUpperDensity A ≥ 1/2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved that upper density `1 / 2` can be attained; in particular,
there exists a Sidon set whose upper density is *at least* `1 / 2`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets (erdos_329.variants.turan_1941)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_329.variants.turan_1941 : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), IsSidon A → sidonUpperDensity A ≤ 1
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Turán [ErTu41] proved the upper bound of 1.

[ErTu41] Erdős, P. and Turán, P., On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on some related problems. J. London Math. Soc. (1941), 212-215.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 33 (erdos_33)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_33 : ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | AdditiveBasisCondition A}, Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N => (A.1 ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (√N : EReal)) = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
for some `a` in `A` and `n ≥ 0`. What is the smallest possible value of
`lim sup n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/2)`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 33 (erdos_33.variants.one_mem_lowerBounds)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_33.variants.one_mem_lowerBounds : ∃ A, AdditiveBasisCondition A ∧ 1 < Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / √N)
problems.humanStatement: Erdos observed that this value is finite and > 1.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 33 (erdos_33.variants.vanDoorn)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_33.variants.vanDoorn : ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | AdditiveBasisCondition A}, Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N => (A.1 ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (√N : EReal)) ≤ ↑(2 * (φ ^ ((5 : ℝ) / 2)))
problems.humanStatement:
The smallest possible value of `lim sup n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/2)`
is at most `2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66`, with `φ` equal to the golden ratio. Proven by
Wouter van Doorn.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 331 (erdos_331.variants.ruzsa)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_331.variants.ruzsa : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A B : Set ℕ, (∃ c_A > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count A n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ c_A * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) → (∃ c_B > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count B n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ c_B * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) → { s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | let ⟨a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂⟩
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa suggests that a non-trivial variant of this problem arises if one imposes the stronger
condition that $|A \cap \{1,\dots,N\}| \sim c_A N^{1/2}$ for some constant $c_A>0$, and similarly
for $B$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 332 (erdos_332)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_332 (A : Set ℕ) : (answer(sorry) : Set ℕ → Prop) A → HasBoundedGaps (D_A A)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and $D(A)$ be the set of those numbers which occur infinitely often as
$a_1 - a_2$ with $a_1, a_2\in A$. What conditions on $A$ are sufficient to ensure $D(A)$ has bounded
gaps?

This is formalised here using the `answer(sorry)` mechanism. In order to solve this problem one
has to provide what the sufficient conditions are, and proof that they imply the desired condition.
If the condition is a solution to the problem is up to human judgement.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 337 (erdos_337.variants.h_fold)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_337.variants.h_fold : ∀ h : ℕ, 2 ≤ h → ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis ∧ (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) ∧ ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((h • A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
This was generalised (to the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$)
by Ruzsa and Turjányi [RT85].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 337 (erdos_337.variants.ruzsa_turjanyi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_337.variants.ruzsa_turjanyi : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis → (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) → Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (2 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty,
$$
and conjecture that the same should be true with $(A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ in the numerator.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 337 (erdos_337.variants.three_fold)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_337.variants.three_fold : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis → (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) → Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (((A + A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (3 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty,
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε > 0) : (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n / n ^ ε) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ ((Set.range greedySidon ∩ Set.Icc 1 n).ncard : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A = \{1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 21, 31, 45, 66, 81, 97, \ldots\}$ be the greedy Sidon sequence:
we begin with $1$ and iteratively include the next smallest integer that preserves the
Sidon property (i.e. there are no non-trivial solutions to $a + b = c + d$). What is the
order of growth of $A$? Is it true that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| \gg N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$ and large $N$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants._22_mem_sub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants._22_mem_sub : 22 ∈ Set.range greedySidon - Set.range greedySidon
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] also asked about the difference set $A - A$ and whether this
contains $22$, which it does.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants._33_mem_sub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants._33_mem_sub : answer(sorry) ↔ 33 ∈ Set.range greedySidon - Set.range greedySidon
problems.humanStatement: The smallest integer which is unknown to be in $A - A$ is $33$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants.co_density_zero_sub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants.co_density_zero_sub : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℕ, S.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ n ∈ Sᶜ, n ∈ Set.range greedySidon - Set.range greedySidon
problems.humanStatement: It may be true that all or almost all integers are in $A - A$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants.cofinite_sub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants.cofinite_sub : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, n ∈ Set.range greedySidon - Set.range greedySidon
problems.humanStatement: It may be true that all or almost all integers are in $A - A$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants.isTheta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants.isTheta (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε > 0) : (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((Set.range greedySidon ∩ Set.Icc 1 n).ncard : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A = \{1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 21, 31, 45, 66, 81, 97, \ldots\}$ be the greedy Sidon sequence:
we begin with $1$ and iteratively include the next smallest integer that preserves the
Sidon property (i.e. there are no non-trivial solutions to $a + b = c + d$). What is the
order of growth of $A$? Is it true that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| \gg N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$ and large $N$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants.sub_hasPosDensity)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants.sub_hasPosDensity : Set.HasPosDensity (Set.range greedySidon - Set.range greedySidon)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] also asked about the difference set $A - A$ and whether this has
positive density.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 340 (erdos_340.variants.third)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_340.variants.third (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε > 0) : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ ((Set.range greedySidon ∩ Set.Icc 1 n).ncard : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: It is trivial that this sequence grows at least like $\gg N^{1/3}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 341 (erdos_341)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_341 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ᶠ n in atTop, IsLeast { x | a n < x ∧ x ∉ { a i + a j | (i ≤ n) (j ≤ n) } } (a (n + 1))) → let d
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots < a_k\}$ be a finite set of integers and extend it to an infinite
sequence $\overline{A}=\{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots \}$ by defining $a_{n+1}$ for $n \geq k$ to be
the least integer exceeding $a_n$ which is not of the form $a_i + a_j$ with $i,j \leq n$.
Is it true that the sequence of differences $a_{m+1}-a_m$ is eventually periodic?

This problem is discussed under Problem 7 on Green's open problems list.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | ∃ m, a m = a n + 2}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → let d (n : ℕ) : ℤ
problems.humanStatement: Does Ulam's sequence eventually have periodic differences? That is, is $a(n+1) - a(n)$ eventually periodic?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → Set.upperDensity (Set.range a) = 0
problems.humanStatement: Part (iii), is the density of the sequence 0?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.test.a0)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.test.a0 : ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → a 0 = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.test.a1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.test.a1 : ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → a 1 = 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.test.a2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.test.a2 : ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → a 2 = 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 342 (erdos_342.test.a3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_342.test.a3 : ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsUlamSequence a → a 3 = 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346 (erdos_346)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_346 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {A : ℕ → ℕ}, IsLacunary A → IsAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq A → (∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ range A → B.Infinite → ¬ IsAddComplete (range A \ B)) → Tendsto (fun n => A (n + 1) / (A n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 ((1 + √5) / 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346 (erdos_346.variants.example)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_346.variants.example : ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, IsAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq A ∧ (∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ range A → B.Infinite → ¬ IsAddComplete (range A \ B)) ∧ liminf (fun n => A (n + 1) / (2 : ℝ)) atTop = 1 ∧ limsup (fun n => A (n + 1) / (A n : ENNReal)) atTop = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346 (erdos_346.variants.f_isAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_346.variants.f_isAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq : IsAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346 (erdos_346.variants.f_isLacunary)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_346.variants.f_isLacunary : IsLacunary f

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_346.variants.f_not_isAddComplete {B : Set ℕ} (h : B ⊆ range f) (hB : B.Infinite) : ¬ IsAddComplete (range f \ B)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 348 (erdos_348)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_348 : { (m, n) | (m) (n) (_ : m < n) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : Monotone a) (_ : ∀ s, s.card = m → IsAddComplete (Set.range (Function.updateFinset a s 0))) (_ : ∀ t, t.card = n → ¬IsAddComplete (Set.range (Function.updateFinset a t 0))) } = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
For what values of $0 \leq m < n$ is there a complete sequence
$A = \{a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots\}$ of integers such that
 1. $A$ remains complete after removing any $m$ elements, but
 2. $A$ is not complete after removing any $n$ elements.

problems.title: erdos_349 (erdos_349)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_349 : {(t, α) | 0 < t ∧ 0 < α ∧ IsGoodPair t α} = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
For what values of $t,\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ is the sequence $\lfloor t\alpha^n\rfloor$ complete
(that is, all sufficiently large integers are the sum of distinct integers of the form $\lfloor t\alpha^n\rfloor$)?

problems.title: erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_even (erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_even)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_even : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | Even ⌊(3/2 : ℝ) ^ n⌋}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that the terms of the sequence $\lfloor (3/2)^n\rfloor$ are even infinitely often?

problems.title: erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_odd (erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_odd)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_349.variants.floor_3_halves_odd : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | Odd ⌊(3/2 : ℝ) ^ n⌋}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that the terms of the sequence $\lfloor (3/2)^n\rfloor$ are odd infinitely
often and even infinitely often?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 350 (erdos_350.variants.strengthening)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_350.variants.strengthening (A : Finset ℕ) (hA : DecidableDistinctSubsetSums A) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) : ∑ n ∈ A, (1 / n : ℝ)^s < 1 / (1 - 2^(-s))
problems.humanStatement:
If `A ⊂ ℕ` is a finite set of integers all of whose subset sums are distinct then `∑ n ∈ A, 1/n^s < 1/(1 - 2^(-s))`, for any `s > 0`.
Proved by Hanson, Steele, and Stenger [HSS77].

We exclude here the case `s = 0`, because in the informal formulation then the right hand side is to be interpreted as `∞`, while the left hand side counts the elements in `A`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 351 (erdos_351.variants.X_sq)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 352 (erdos_352)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_352 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0: ℝ), ∀ A : Set ℝ², MeasurableSet A → ℙ A ≥ c.toEReal → (∃ t : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ², (∀ p : Fin 3, t.points p ∈ A) ∧ EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area (t.points 0) (t.points 1) (t.points 2) = 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some $c > 0$ such that every measurable $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of measure $\geq c$
 contains the vertices of a triangle of area 1?

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.bigTheta_version : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version : (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 357 (erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version_symm)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version_symm : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 357 (erdos_357.variants.hegyvari)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.variants.hegyvari : ∃ (o o' : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ o' =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (g n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc ((1 / 3 + o n) * n) ((2 / 3 + o' n)*n)

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_density (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : StrictMono A) (hA : HasDistinctSums A) : (Set.range A).HasDensity 0

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.variants.monotone.parts.ii.bigO_version : (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ))

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.variants.monotone.parts.ii.littleO_version : (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ))
