problems.title: Erdős Problem 357 (erdos_357.variants.weisenberg)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_357.variants.weisenberg : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (2 + o n) * √n ≤ f n
problems.humanStatement:
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
It is known that $f(n) \geq (2+o(1))\sqrt{n}$.
Source: See comment by Desmond Weisenberg here: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/357.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 358 (erdos_358.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_358.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ ∃ A, StrictMono A ∧ atTop.Tendsto (f A) atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of integers. Let $f(n)$ count the number of
solutions to $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i.$$
Is there such an $A$ for which $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?

Tao [Ta26] constructed such a sequence with $f(n) \gg \log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 358 (erdos_358.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_358.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔ ∃ A, StrictMono A ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 2 ≤ f A n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of integers. Let $f(n)$ count the number of
solutions to $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i.$$
Is there an $A$ such that $f(n)\geq 2$ for all large $n$?

This also follows from Tao's construction with $f(n) \gg \log n$ [Ta26].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 358 (erdos_358.variants.one_le)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_358.variants.one_le : ∃ A, StrictMono A ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ g A n
problems.humanStatement:
It is conjectured that if $A =\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ and $g$ counts the number of representations
$$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i$$ such that the sum has at least two terms, then for all $n$ we have
$1 \leq g(n)$ for sufficiently large $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 358 (erdos_358.variants.prime_set)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_358.variants.prime_set : atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ (f (Nat.nth Nat.Prime) n : ℕ∞)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
When $A =\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ corresponds to the set of primes, it is conjectured that the
$\limsup$ of the number of representations $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i$$ is infinite.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 358 (erdos_358.variants.prime_set_density_representation)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_358.variants.prime_set_density_representation : 0 < {n : ℕ | intervalRepresentations (Nat.nth Nat.Prime) n |>.Nonempty}.upperDensity
problems.humanStatement:
When $A =\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ corresponds to the set of primes, it is conjectured that the set of
numbers $n$ that have representations $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i$$ has positive upper density.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 359 (erdos_359.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_359.parts.i (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) : atTop.Tendsto (fun k ↦ (A k : ℝ) / k) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 359 (erdos_359.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_359.parts.ii (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c): atTop.Tendsto (fun k ↦ A k / (k : ℝ) ^ (1 + c)) (nhds 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 359 (erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_asymptotic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_asymptotic (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) : (fun k ↦ (A k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun k ↦ k * (k : ℝ).log / (k : ℝ).log.log)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 359 (erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) : A '' (Set.Iic 7) = {1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 36 (erdos_36)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_36 : atTop.Tendsto MinOverlapQuotient (𝓝 answer(sorry))
problems.humanStatement: Find the value of the limit of `MinOverlapQuotient`!

problems.title: Erdős Problem 36 (erdos_36.variants.exists)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_36.variants.exists : ∃ c, atTop.Tendsto MinOverlapQuotient (𝓝 c) ∧ c < 0.385694
problems.humanStatement: The limit of `MinOverlapQuotient` exists and it is less than $0.385694$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 36 (erdos_36.variants.lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_36.variants.lower: ∃ (c : ℝ), 0.379005 < c ∧ c ≤ atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient ∧ c = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement: Find a better lower bound!

problems.title: Erdős Problem 36 (erdos_36.variants.upper)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_36.variants.upper : ∃ (c : ℝ), c < 0.380926853433087 ∧ atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ c ∧ c = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement: Find a better upper bound!

problems.title: Erdős Problem 361 (erdos_361)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_361 (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) : subsetSumAvoidanceNumber c = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c > 0$ and $n$ be some large integer. What is the size of the largest set
$A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, \lfloor c n \rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of a subset of $A$?
Does this depend on $n$ in an irregular way?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 361 (erdos_361.asymptotic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_361.asymptotic (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumAvoidanceNumber c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Asymptotic version of Erdős Problem 361: determine the order of growth of the largest cardinality
as $n \to \infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 364 (erdos_364)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_364 : ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ), Powerful n ∧ Powerful (n + 1) ∧ Powerful (n + 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 364 (erdos_364.variants.strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_364.variants.strong : ∃ (c : ℝ) (h : c > 0), ∀ (k : ℕ), Nat.nth Powerful (k + 2) - Nat.nth Powerful k > (Nat.nth Powerful k : ℝ) ^ c
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er76d] conjectured a stronger statement: if $n_k$ is the $k$th powerful number,
then $n_{k+2} - n_k > n_k^c$ for some constant $c > 0$.

[Er76d] Erdős, P., Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 364 (erdos_364.variants.weak)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_364.variants.weak : ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ), Powerful n ∧ Powerful (n + 1) ∧ Powerful (n + 2) ∧ Powerful (n + 3)
problems.humanStatement:
There is no quadruple of powerful numbers, since at least one of the four numbers must be
$2 \pmod{4}$, which cannot be powerful (since $2$ divides it, but $2^2$ does not).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 366 (erdos_366)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_366 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 0, (2).Full n ∧ (3).Full (n + 1)
problems.humanStatement: Are there any $2$-full $n$ such that $n+1$ is $3$-full?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 366 (erdos_366.variants.three_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_366.variants.three_two : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | (3).Full n ∧ (2).Full (n + 1)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Are there infinitely many 3-full $n$ such that $n+1$ is 2-full?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 366 (erdos_366.variants.weaker)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_366.variants.weaker : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 0, (3).Full n ∧ (3).Full (n + 1)
problems.humanStatement: Are there any consecutive pairs of $3$-full integers?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 371 (erdos_371)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_371 : { n | Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 1) > Nat.maxPrimeFac n }.HasDensity (1/2)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. Show that the set of $n$
with $P(n+1) > P(n)$ has density $\frac{1}{2}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 373 (erdos_373)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_373 : S.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Show that the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with `n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, has
only finitely many solutions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 373 (erdos_373.variants.maximal_solution)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_373.variants.maximal_solution : (16, [14, 5, 2]) ∈ S ∧ ∀ s ∈ S, s.fst ≤ 16
problems.humanStatement:
Hickerson conjectured the largest solution the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with
`n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, is `16!=14!5!2!`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 373 (erdos_373.variants.of_limit)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_373.variants.of_limit (H : Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) => (n*(n+1)).maxPrimeFac / (n : ℝ).log) Filter.atTop) : S.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Show that if `P(n(n+1)) / log n → ∞` where `P(m)` denotes the largest prime factor of `m`, then
the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with `n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, has only
finitely many solutions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 373 (erdos_373.variants.of_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_373.variants.of_lower_bound (H : ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 4*(n : ℝ).log < (n*(n-1 : ℕ)).maxPrimeFac) : S.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Show that if `P(n(n−1)) > 4 log n` for large enough `n`, where `P(m)` denotes the
largest prime factor of `m`, then the equation `n!=a_1!a_2!···a_k!`, with
`n−1 > a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ··· ≥ a_k`, has only finitely many solutions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 373 (erdos_373.variants.suranyi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_373.variants.suranyi : {(n, a, b) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | n ! = a ! * b ! ∧ 1 < n ∧ 1 < a ∧ 1 < b ∧ b ≤ a ∧ a + 1 ≠ n} = {(10, 7, 6)}
problems.humanStatement:
Surányi was the first to conjecture that the only non-trivial solution to `a!b!=n!`
is `6!7!=10!`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 (erdos_375)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_375 : answer(sorry) ↔ Erdos375Prop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 (erdos_375.variants.bounded_gap)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_375.variants.bounded_gap : Erdos375Prop → ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (n + 1).nth Nat.Prime - n.nth Nat.Prime < (n.nth Nat.Prime : ℝ) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ) - c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 (erdos_375.variants.le_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_375.variants.le_two : ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ k ≤ 2, (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime) → ∃ p : Fin k → ℕ, p.Injective ∧ ∀ i, (p i).Prime ∧ p i ∣ n + i + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 (erdos_375.variants.legendre)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_375.variants.legendre : Erdos375Prop → (∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ p ∈ Set.Ioo (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2), Nat.Prime p)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 (erdos_375.variants.log)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_375.variants.log : ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, k < c * (Real.log n / (Real.log (Real.log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime) → ∃ p : Fin k → ℕ, p.Injective ∧ ∀ i, (p i).Prime ∧ p i ∣ n + i + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 376 (erdos_376)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_376 : answer(sorry) ↔ { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime 105 }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Are there infinitely many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $105$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 376 (erdos_376.variants.prime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_376.variants.prime {p q : ℕ} (h₁ : p.Prime) (h₂ : Odd p) (h₃ : q.Prime) (h₄ : Odd q) : { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime (p * q) }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75] have shown that, for any two odd primes $p$ and $q$,
there are infinite many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $pq$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 (erdos_377)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_377 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ), sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ≤ C
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some absolute constant $C > 0$ such that
$$
  \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p} \leq C
$$
for all $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 (erdos_377.variants.ae)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_377.variants.ae (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)), ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n = γ₀ + o n
problems.humanStatement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then for almost all integers $f(m) = \gamma_0 + o(1)$.

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 (erdos_377.variants.limit.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_377.variants.limit.i (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) : Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) => (1 : ℝ) / x * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n) atTop (𝓝 γ₀)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then
$$
  \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{n\leq x} f(n) = \gamma_0
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 (erdos_377.variants.limit.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_377.variants.limit.ii (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) : Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) => (1 : ℝ) / x * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 (γ₀ ^ 2))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then
$$
  \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{n\leq x} f(n)^2 = \gamma_0^2
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 (erdos_377.variants.ub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_377.variants.ub : ∃ c < (1 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ≤ c * (n : ℝ).log.log
problems.humanStatement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
then there is some constant $c < 1$ such that for all large $n$
$$
  f(n) \leq c \log\log n.
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 383 (erdos_383)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_383 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Nat.maxPrimeFac (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 0 k, (p ^ 2 + i)) = p}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that for every $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the largest prime
divisor of
$$
  \prod_{i = 0}^k (p ^ 2 + i)
$$
is $p$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 385 (erdos_385.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_385.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n < F n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 385 (erdos_385.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_385.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ F n - n) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 385 (erdos_385.variants.lb)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_385.variants.lb : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (e : ℕ → ℝ) (he : e =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)), ∀ n, n + (1 - e n) * √n ≤ F n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 386 (erdos_386)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_386 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ᶠ n in .atTop, k ≤ n - 2 ∧ ∃ p q : ℕ, n.choose k = ∏ i ∈ .Ico p q, nth Nat.Prime i
problems.humanStatement:
There is a $k$, such that $2 \le k \le n - 2$ and
$\binom{n}{k}$ can be the product of consecutive primes infinitely often?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 386 (erdos_386.variants.forall)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_386.variants.forall : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ᶠ n in .atTop, k ≤ n - 2 ∧ ∃ p q : ℕ, n.choose k = ∏ i ∈ .Ico p q, nth Nat.Prime i
problems.humanStatement:
For all $2 \le k \le n - 2$,
can $\binom{n}{k}$ be the product of consecutive primes infinitely often?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 386 (erdos_386.variants.two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_386.variants.two : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ᶠ n in .atTop, 2 ≤ n - 2 ∧ ∃ p q : ℕ, n.choose 2 = ∏ i ∈ .Ico p q, nth Nat.Prime i
problems.humanStatement: Can $\binom{n}{2}$ be the product of consecutive primes infinitely often?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 387 (erdos_387)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_387 : answer(False) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → k < n → ∃ d : ℕ, (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioc (c * n) n ∧ d ∣ n.choose k
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, for all $1 \leq k < n$, the binomial coefficient
$\binom{n}{k}$ has a divisor in $(cn, n]$?

Bui, Naprienko, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BNPZ26] answered this negatively.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 387 (erdos_387.variants.easy)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_387.variants.easy {n : ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : k ≤ n) : ∃ d : ℕ, (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc (n / k : ℝ) n ∧ d ∣ n.choose k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 387 (erdos_387.variants.guy)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_387.variants.guy : answer(False) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, c < 1 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → k < n → ∃ d : ℕ, (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioc (c * n) n ∧ d ∣ n.choose k
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true for any $c < 1$ and all $n$ sufficiently large, for all $1 \leq k < n$,
$\binom{n}{k}$ has a divisor in $(cn, n]$?

This variant appears in [Gu04]. Bui, Naprienko, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BNPZ26] answered it
negatively.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 387 (erdos_387.variants.schinzel)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_387.variants.schinzel : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ¬ IsPrimePow k → ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ i < k, ¬ n - i ∣ n.choose k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 389 (erdos_389)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_389 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ k ≥ 1, ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + i) ∣ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + k + i)
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that for every $n \geq 1$ there is a $k$ such that
$$
  n(n + 1) \cdots (n + k - 1) \mid (n + k) \cdots (n + 2k - 1)?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 389 (erdos_389.variants.mehta_four)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_389.variants.mehta_four : IsLeast { k | 1 ≤ k ∧ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (4 + i) ∣ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (4 + k + i) } 207
problems.humanStatement:
Bhavik Mehta has computed the minimal such $k$ for $1 \leq n \leq 18$.
For example, the minimal $k$ for $n = 4$ is $207$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 39 (erdos_39)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_39 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), (· ^ (1 / 2 - ε) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] fun N => (((Set.Icc 1 N) ∩ A).ncard : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an infinite Sidon set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2-\epsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 390 (erdos_390)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_390 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, (fun n => f n - 2 * n : ℕ → ℝ) ~[atTop] (fun n => c * n / log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 390 (erdos_390.variants.theta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_390.variants.theta : (fun n => f n - 2 * n : ℕ → ℝ) =Θ[atTop] (fun n => n / log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 392 (erdos_392.variants.implication)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_392.variants.implication (h : type_of% erdos_392) : type_of% erdos_392.variants.lower
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie has observed that a positive answer follows from the result above with $a_t \leq n$, simply
by pairing variables together, e.g. taking $a'_i = a_{2i-1}a_{2i}$ (and the lower bound follows from
Stirling's approximation).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 392 (erdos_392.variants.lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_392.variants.lower (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { t + 1 | (t) (_ : ∃ a : Fin (t + 1) → ℕ, (n)! = ∏ i, a i ∧ Monotone a ∧ a (Fin.last t) ≤ n) } (A n)) : (fun (n : ℕ) => (A n - n + n / Real.log n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n => n / Real.log n
problems.humanStatement:
If we change the condition to $a_t \leq n$ it can be shown that
$$
  A(n) = n - \frac{n}{\log n} + o\left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 394 (erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_10)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_10 : ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → k < 10 → t k (10 !) < t (k - 1) (10 !) - 1
problems.humanStatement: They proved (with Selfridge) that this holds for $n=10$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 394 (erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite { n : ℕ | ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < n → t k (n !) < t (k - 1) (n !) - 1 }
problems.humanStatement:
They ask about the behaviour of $t_{n-3}(n!)$ and also ask whether, for infinitely many $n$,
$t_k(n!)< t_{k-1}(n!)-1$ for all $1\leq k < n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 394 (erdos_394.variants.hall_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_bound : (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 * (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)) / Real.log (Real.log x)))
problems.humanStatement:
In [ErGr80] they mention a conjecture of Erdős that the sum is $o(x^2)$. This was proved by Erdős
and Hall [ErHa78], who proved that in fact
$\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}x^2.$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 394 (erdos_394.variants.hall_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_conjecture : ∀ c < Real.log 2, (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / (Real.log x) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Hall conjecture that the sum is $o(x^2/(\log x)^c)$ for any $c<\log 2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 394 (erdos_394.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_394.variants.lower_bound : (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / Real.log x) ≫ (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: Since $t_2(p)=p-1$ for prime $p$ it is trivial that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\gg \frac{x^2}{\log x}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 396 (erdos_396)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_396 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, descFactorial n (k + 1) ∣ centralBinom n
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that for every $k$ there exists $n$ such that
$$\prod_{0\leq i\leq k}(n-i) \mid \binom{2n}{n}?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 398 (erdos_398)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_398 : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | ∃ m, n ! + 1 = m ^ 2} = {4, 5, 7}
problems.humanStatement:
**Brocard's Problem**
Does $n! + 1 = m^2$ have integer solutions other than $n = 4, 5, 7$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 399 (erdos_399.variants.cambie)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_399.variants.cambie {n x y : ℕ} : x.Coprime y → 1 < x * y → n ! ≠ x ^ 4 + y ^ 4
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie has also observed that considerations modulo $8$ rule out any solutions to $n!=x^4+y^4$ with
$(x,y)=1$ and $xy>1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 399 (erdos_399.variants.erdos_oblath)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_399.variants.erdos_oblath {n x y k : ℕ} : x.Coprime y → 1 < x * y → 2 < k → k ≠ 4 → n ! ≠ x ^ k + y ^ k ∧ n ! + y ^ k ≠ x ^ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 399 (erdos_399.variants.pollack_shapiro)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_399.variants.pollack_shapiro (n x : ℕ) : n ! + 1 ≠ x ^ 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 399 (erdos_399.variants.sum_two_squares)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_399.variants.sum_two_squares : ∀ {n x y : ℕ}, 1 < x * y → n ! = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 → n = 6 ∧ (x = 12 ∧ y = 24 ∨ x = 24 ∧ y = 12)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Obláth observed that the Bertrand-style fact (first proved by Breusch [Br32]) that, if
$q_i$ is the sequence of primes congruent to $3\pmod{4}$ then $q_{i+1}<2q_i$ except for $q_1=3$,
together with Fermat's theorem on the sums of two squares implies that the only solution to
$n!=x^2+y^2$ is $6!=12^2+24^2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 4 (erdos_4)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_4 : answer(True) ↔ (∀ C > 0, Erdos4For C)
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for any $C > 0$, there infinitely many $n$ such that:
$$
  p_{n + 1} - p_n > C \frac{\log\log n\log\log\log\log n}{(\log\log\log n) ^ 2}\log n
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 4 (erdos_4.variants.rankin)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_4.variants.rankin : ∃ C > 0, Erdos4For C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 40 (erdos_40)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_40 : Erdos40ForSet answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
For what functions $g(N) → \infty$ is it true that
$$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \frac{N^{1/2}}{g(N)}$$
implies $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=\infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 40 (erdos_40.variants.implies_erdos_28)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_40.variants.implies_erdos_28 (h_erdos_40 : Erdos40ForSet .univ) : type_of% Erdos28.erdos_28
problems.humanStatement:
If we don't pose additional conditions on the functions, then this is a stronger form of the
Erdős-Turán conjecture, see Erdõs Problem 28,
(since establishing this for any function $g(N) → \infty$ would imply a positive solution to Erdős
Problem 28).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 400 (erdos_400.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_400.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ, (fun x : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 x, (g k n : ℝ))) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ c * x * Real.log x)
problems.humanStatement: Can one show that $\sum_{n\leq x}g_k(n) \sim c_k x\log x$ for some constant $c_k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 400 (erdos_400.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_400.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ε > 0, Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (((Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦ |(g k n : ℝ) - c * Real.log x| ≤ ε * Real.log x)).card : ℝ) / x) atTop (𝓝 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that there is a constant $c_k$ such that for almost all $n < x$ we have
$g_k(n)=c_k\log x+o(\log x)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 400 (erdos_400.variants.g_pos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_400.variants.g_pos (k n : ℕ) (h: k ≥ 2) : 0 < g k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 400 (erdos_400.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_400.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g k n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Graham write that it is easy to show that $g_k(n) \ll_k \log n$ always, but the best
possible constant is unknown.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 402 (erdos_402)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_402 (A : Finset ℕ) (h₁ : 0 ∉ A) (h₂ : A.Nonempty) : ∃ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A), a.gcd b ≤ (a / A.card : ℚ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 402 (erdos_402.variants.equality)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_402.variants.equality (A : Finset ℕ) (h₁ : 0 ∉ A) (h₂ : A.Nonempty) (h₃ : A.gcd id = 1) (h : ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A), (a / A.card : ℚ) ≤ a.gcd b) : A = Finset.Icc 1 A.card ∨ A = (Finset.Icc 1 A.card).image ((Finset.Icc 1 A.card).lcm id / ·) ∨ A = {2, 3, 4, 6}
problems.humanStatement:
has no common divisor) the only cases where equality is achieved are when
$A = \{1, \dots, n\}$ or $A = \{L/1, \dots, L/n\}$ (where $L = \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$) or
$A = \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$.
Note: The source [BaSo96] mentioned on the Erdős page makes it clear what
quantifiers to use for "where equality is achieved". See Theorem 1.1 there.

TODO(firsching): Consider if we should have the other direction here as well or
an iff statement.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 402 (erdos_402.variants.szegedy_zaharescu_weak)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_402.variants.szegedy_zaharescu_weak : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card = n → 0 ∉ A → (n ≤ (A ×ˢ A).sup (fun x => x.1 / x.1.gcd x.2)) ∧ (n = (A ×ˢ A).sup (fun x => x.1 / x.1.gcd x.2) ↔ ∃ k > 0, A = (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (k * ·) ∨ A = (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (k * (Finset.Icc 1 n).lcm id / ·))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 406 (erdos_406)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_406 : answer(sorry) ↔ { n | n.isPowerOfTwo ∧ Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [0, 1] }.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that there are only finitely many powers of $2$ which have only the digits $0$
and $1$ when written in base $3$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 406 (erdos_406.variants.one_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_406.variants.one_two : IsGreatest { n | n.isPowerOfTwo ∧ Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [1, 2] } (2 ^ 15)
problems.humanStatement:
If we only allow the digits $1$ and $2$ then $2^{15}$ seems to be the largest such power
of $2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.i (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } answer(sorry)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.i.isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) : (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = O(g(n))$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.i.isLittleO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isLittleO (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) : (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.i.isTheta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isTheta (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) : (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. What is $\Theta(c(n))$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Can infinitely many $n$ reach the same prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.parts.iii (p : ℕ) (h : p.Prime) (α : ℝ) (hα : { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.HasDensity α) : α = answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement: What is the density of $n$ which reach any fixed prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.variants.sigma)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) : (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.variants.sigma_isTheta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isTheta (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) : (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 409 (erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that iterates of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ always reach a prime?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 41 (erdos_41)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_41 (A : Set ℕ) (h_triple : NtupleCondition A 3) (h_infinite : A.Infinite) : Filter.atTop.liminf (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (N : ℝ)^(1/3 : ℝ)) = 0
problems.humanStatement:
Let `A ⊆ ℕ` be an infinite set such that the triple sums `a + b + c` are all distinct for
`a, b, c` in `A` (aside from the trivial coincidences). Is it true that
`liminf n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/3) = 0`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 41 (erdos_41.variants.pairwise)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_41.variants.pairwise (A : Set ℕ) (hA₂ : NtupleCondition A 2) (hA : A.Infinite) : Filter.atTop.liminf (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (N : ℝ).sqrt) = 0
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved the following pairwise version.
Let `A ⊆ ℕ` be an infinite set such that the pairwise sums `a + b` are all distinct for `a, b`
in `A` (aside from the trivial coincidences).
Is it true that `liminf n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/2) = 0`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 410 (erdos_410)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_410 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ ((sigma 1)^[k] n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (k : ℝ))) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $σ_1(n) = σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.

Is it true that $\lim_{k → ∞} σ_k(n)^{\frac 1 k} = ∞$?

This is problem (iii) from
Erdos, Granville, Pomerance, Spiro
"On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetical functions"
(page 169 of the book "Analytic Number Theory", 1990).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 412 (erdos_412)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_412 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (m ≥ 2) (n ≥ 2), ∃ i j, (σ 1)^[i] m = (σ 1)^[j] n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $σ_1(n)=σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.
Is it true that, for every $m, n ≥ 2$, there exist some $i, j$ such that $σ_i(m) = σ_j(n)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 413 (erdos_413.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_413.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ { n | IsBarrier (fun m => ω m) n }.Infinite

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_413.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ (∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), { n | IsBarrier (fun n => ε * ω n) n }.Infinite)

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_413.variants.bigOmega : answer(sorry) ↔ { n | IsBarrier (fun m => Ω m) n }.Infinite

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_413.variants.bigOmega_largest_barrier_lt_100k : IsGreatest {n : ℕ | n < 10 ^ 5 ∧ IsBarrier (fun m => Ω m) n} 99840

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_413.variants.hasPosDensity_barrier_expProd : { n | IsBarrier (fun m => expProd m) n }.HasPosDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 414 (erdos_414)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_414 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (m > 0) (n > 0), ∃ i j, h^[i] m = h^[j] n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $h_1(n) = h(n)$ and $h_k(n) = h(h_{k-1}(n))$. Is it true, for any $m,n$, there exist
$i$ and $j$ such that $h_i(m) = h_j(n)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.parts.i : Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (V (2 * x) / V (x))) Filter.atTop (𝓝 2)
problems.humanStatement: Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable. Does `V(2x)/V(x)→2` ?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.parts.ii : let f : ℝ → ℝ
problems.humanStatement:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Is there an asymptotic formula for `V(x)`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.variants.Erdos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.variants.Erdos : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, V x = x * x.log ^ (-1 + f x)
problems.humanStatement:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Erdős proved V(x)=x(logx)^(−1+o(1)).
Ref: Erdős, P., _On the normal number of prime factors of $p-1$ and some related problems concerning Euler's $\varphi$-function._

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.variants.Ford)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.variants.Ford : let (C₁, C₂, C₃) : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ
problems.humanStatement:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
`V(x) ≍ x/log x*e^(C_1*(log log log x − log log log log x)^2+C_2 log log log x − C_3 log log log log x)`
Ref: Ford, Kevin, _The distribution of totients_.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance : let C : ℝ
problems.humanStatement:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
`V(x)=x/logx * e^((C+o(1))(log log log x)^2)`, for some explicit constant `C>0`.
Ref:Maier, Helmut and Pomerance, Carl, _On the number of distinct values of Euler's $\phi$-function_.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416 (erdos_416.variants.Pillai)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_416.variants.Pillai : V =o[atTop] id
problems.humanStatement:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Pillai proved `V(x)=o(x)`.
Ref: S. Sivasankaranarayana Pillai, _On some functions connected with $\phi(n)$_

problems.title: Erdős Problem 417 (erdos_417.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_417.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ L : ENNReal, Tendsto (fun x ↦ ({ k | k ∈ range totient ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ x }.ncard : ENNReal) / ((totient '' { m | 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ x }).ncard : ENNReal)) atTop (𝓝 L)
problems.humanStatement:
Let$$V'(x)=\#\{\phi(m) : 1\leq m\leq x\}$$and$$V(x)=\#\{\phi(m) \leq x : 1\leq m\}.$$
Does $\lim V(x)/V'(x)$ exist?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 417 (erdos_417.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_417.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ L > (1 : ENNReal), Tendsto (fun x ↦ ({ k | k ∈ range totient ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ x }.ncard : ENNReal) / ((totient '' { m | 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ x }).ncard : ENNReal)) atTop (𝓝 L)
problems.humanStatement: Is it $>1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 418 (erdos_418.variants.conditional)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_418.variants.conditional (goldbach : ∀ (n : ℕ), 6 < n → Even n → ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n = p + q) (m : ℕ) (h : Odd m) : ∃ n, m + n.totient = n
problems.humanStatement:
It follows from a slight strengthening of the Goldbach conjecture that every odd number can be
written as $n - \phi(n)$.
In particular, we assume that every even number greater than 6 can be written as the sum of two
*distinct* primes, in contrast to the usual Goldbach conjecture that every even number greater than
2 can be written as the sum of two primes.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 418 (erdos_418.variants.density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_418.variants.density : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S.HasPosDensity), S ⊆ { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ
problems.humanStatement: It is open whether the set of non-cototients has positive density.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 418 (erdos_418.variants.sigma)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_418.variants.sigma : ∃ (S : Set ℕ) (hS : S.HasPosDensity), S ⊆ { (σ 1 n - n : ℕ) | n }ᶜ
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er73b] has shown that a positive density set of natural numbers cannot be written as
$\sigma(n)-n$ (numbers not of this form are called nonaliquot, or sometimes untouchable).

The density sits in an existential, so `HasPosDensity` is the *stronger* reading: the witness
`S` is ours to choose, and weakening it to positive lower density would claim less rather than
more. That is the opposite of the usual situation for Erdős' "positive density", where the
density is a hypothesis or a claim about a fixed set. Whether the nonaliquot numbers themselves
have a density is a separate question and is not what this states.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 418 (erdos_418.variants.soln)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_418.variants.soln : { 2 ^ (k + 1) * 509203 | k } ⊆ { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ
problems.humanStatement:
A solution to erdos_418 was shown by Browkin and Schinzel [BrSc95] by showing that any integer of
the form $2^(k + 1)\cdot 509203$ is not of the form $n - \phi(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 421 (erdos_421)

values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.

problems.humanStatement:
**Shiu's theorem**: for any $k \geq 1$ and $(a, q) = 1$ there exist infinitely many $k$-tuples of consecutive primes
$p_m, \dots, p_{m + k - 1}$ all of which are congruent to $a$ modulo $q$.

[Sh00] Shiu, D. K. L., _Strings of congruent primes_. J. London Math. Soc. (2) (2000), 359-373.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 428 (erdos_428)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_428 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, (∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a → a < n → (n - a).Prime) ∧ liminf (fun n ↦ primeDensityRatio A n) atTop > 0
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 43 (erdos_43.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_43.parts.i : answer(False) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ), A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N → B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N → IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) → IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) → (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} → ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) + C
problems.humanStatement:
If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page notes that this follows from the solution to
Erdős Problem 42.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 43 (erdos_43.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_43.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ), A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N → B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N → IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) → IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) → A.card = B.card → (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} → ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 44: Extending Sidon Sets (erdos_44)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_44 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (N ≥ (1 : ℕ)) (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) → ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∃ᵉ (M > N) (B ⊆ Finset.Icc (N + 1) M), IsSidon (A ∪ B : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ (A ∪ B).card
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 44:** Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

This problem asks whether any Sidon set can be extended to achieve a density
arbitrarily close to the optimal density for Sidon sets.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 44: Extending Sidon Sets (erdos_44.variants.empty_start)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_44.variants.empty_start : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∀ᶠ (M : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 M), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ A.card
problems.humanStatement: The case where we start with an empty set (constructing large Sidon sets).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 442 (erdos_442)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_442 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) => 1 / x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop → Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) => 1 / (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2 * ∑ nm ∈ A.bddProdUpper x, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
Is it true that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{Log}_2 x} \sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\to\infty
$$
then
$$
\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2 \sum_{n, m \in A: n < m \leq x}
\frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\to\infty
$$
as $x\to\infty$?

Tao [Ta24b] has shown this is false.

[Ta24b] Tao, T., _Dense sets of natural numbers with unusually large least common multiples_.
arXiv:2407.04226 (2024).

Note: the informal and formal statements follow the solution paper https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226

problems.title: Erdős Problem 442 (erdos_442.variants.tao)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_442.variants.tao : ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (C: ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hf : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ)), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n = Real.exp ((1 / 2 + f x) * √x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne.maxLogOne) ∧ |∑ nm ∈ ((A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊) ×ˢ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊)).toFinset, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2| ≤ C * (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Tao resolved erdos_442 in the negative in Theorem 1 of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226.
The following is a formalisation of that theorem with $C_0 = 1$.

Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
There exists a set $A$ of natural numbers such that
$$
\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n} =
  \exp\left(\left(\left(\frac{1}{2} + o(1)\right)\operatorname{Log}_2^{1/2}x \operatorname{Log}_3x\right)\right)
$$
and
$$
\sum_{n, m\in A: n, m\leq x} \frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\ll\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 445 (erdos_445)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_445 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, c > 1 / 2 → ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ n : ℕ, Erdos445Prop c p n
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for any $c>1/2$, if $p$ is a sufficiently large prime then, for any
$n\geq 0$, there exist $a,b\in(n,n+p^c)$ such that $ab\equiv 1\pmod{p}$?

This is discussed in this MathOverflow question [MathOverflow].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 447 (erdos_447.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_447.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n)
problems.humanStatement:
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Must
$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert =o(2^n)$?

In [Er65b] Erdős reported that the estimate $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=o(2^n)$ was proved in
unpublished work by Sárközy and Szemerédi.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 448 (erdos_448)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_448 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → {n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}.HasDensity 1
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the divisors of $n$ and $\tau^+(n)$ count the number of $k$ such that $n$ has a
divisor in $[2^k, 2^{k+1})$. Is it true that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$ \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n) $$
for almost all $n$?

This is false, and was disproved by Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe81], who showed that in fact the upper
density of the set of such $n$ is $\asymp \epsilon^{1-o(1)}$ (where the $o(1)$ in the exponent
$\to 0$ as $\epsilon \to 0$). A more precise result was proved by Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88]
(see Section 4.6), who showed that the upper density is $\ll \epsilon \log(2/\epsilon)$. Hall and
Tenenbaum further prove that $\tau^+(n)/\tau(n)$ has a distribution function. Erdős and Graham also
asked whether there is a good inequality known for $\sum_{n \leq x} \tau^+(n)$. This was provided by
Ford [Fo08] who proved
$$ \sum_{n \leq x} \tau^+(n) \asymp x\frac{(\log x)^{1-\alpha}}{(\log\log x)^{3/2}} $$
where
$$ \alpha = 1-\frac{1+\log\log 2}{\log 2} = 0.08607\cdots. $$

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_448.variants.erdos_tenenbaum : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Real.log ({n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}.upperDensity) / Real.log ε) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (1 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 450 (erdos_450)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_450 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ Y : ℝ → ℕ → ℕ, IsSufficientScale Y ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (Y ε n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 0)
problems.humanStatement:
How large must $y=y(\epsilon,n)$ be such that the number of integers in
$(x,x+y)$ with a divisor in $(n,2n)$ is at most $\epsilon y$?

A **linear** scale is known to suffice (see `erdos_450.linear_scale_suffices`).
Whether the optimal scale is *sublinear* — a sufficient `Y` with `Y ε n = o(n)` —
is open.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 456 (erdos_456.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_456.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun N ↦ (count { n | m n < p n } N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 456 (erdos_456.parts.ii)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 456 (erdos_456.parts.iii)

problems.humanStatement: Erdős [Er79e] writes it is 'easy to show' that for infinitely many $n$ we have $m_n < p_n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 457 (erdos_457.variants.one_sub)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_457.variants.one_sub : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, q n (Real.log n) < (1 - ε) * Real.log n ^ 2

Taking $n$ to be the product of primes
between $\log n$ and $(2 + o(1)) \log n$ gives an example where
$$
  q(n, \log n) \ge (2 + o(1)) \log n.
$$
Can one prove that $q(n, \log n) < (1 - \epsilon) (\log n)^2$
for all large $n$ and some $\epsilon > 0$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 457 (erdos_457.variants.qnk)

does not divide $\prod_{1 \le i \le k}(n + i)$. This
problem asks whether $q(n, \log n) \ge (2 + \epsilon) \log n$
infinitely often.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 458 (erdos_458)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_458 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, lcm_upto ((k + 1).nth Prime - 1) < k.nth Prime * lcm_upto (k.nth Prime)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$ denote the least common multiple of $\{1, \dots, n\}$.
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime.
Is it true that for all $k \geq 1$, $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_{k+1}-1) < p_k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_k)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 46 (erdos_46.variants.infinitely_many_disjoint)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_46.variants.infinitely_many_disjoint : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite → ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℕ, (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (S i) (S j)) ∧ ∀ i, (∀ n ∈ S i, 2 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S i, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1 ∧ (𝓒 '' (S i : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton
problems.humanStatement: Croot [Cr03] proved more: there are infinitely many disjoint such monochromatic solutions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 46 (erdos_46.variants.positive_rat)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_46.variants.positive_rat : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite → ∀ q : ℚ, 0 < q → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 2 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = q ∧ (𝓒 '' (S : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton
problems.humanStatement: In [ErGr80] they also ask for a monochromatic representation of any $\frac{a}{b}>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 463 (erdos_463)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_463 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : Tendsto f atTop atTop), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ m, m.Composite ∧ n + f n < m ∧ m < n + m.minFac
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a function $f$ with $f(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that,
for all large $n$, there is a composite number $m$ such that
$$
n + f(n) < m < n + p(m)
$$
Here $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$.

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_470.variants.odd_weird_prime_div : ∀ n : ℕ, Odd n → n.Weird → 6 ≤ {m | m ∈ n.divisors ∧ m.Prime}.ncard

that an odd weird number must have at least 6 prime divisors.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 470 (erdos_470.variants.prime_gap_imp_inf_prim_weird)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_470.variants.prime_gap_imp_inf_prim_weird : (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, primeGap n < √ (n.nth Nat.Prime) / 10) → Set.Infinite PrimitiveWeird
problems.humanStatement:
Melfi [Me15](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=3276337) has proved that there
are infinitely many primitive weird numbers, conditional on the fact that
$p_{n+1} - p_n < \frac{1}{10} \sqrt{p_n}$ for all large $n$, which in turn would follow from
well-known conjectures concerning prime gaps.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 470 (erdos_470.variants.smallest_weird_eq_70)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_470.variants.smallest_weird_eq_70 : (∀ n < 70, ¬n.Weird) ∧ (70).Weird
problems.humanStatement: The smallest weird number is 70.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 470 (erdos_470.variants.weird_pos_density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_470.variants.weird_pos_density : {n : ℕ | n.Weird}.HasPosDensity
problems.humanStatement:
Benkoski and Erdős [BeEr74](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=347726) proved
that the set of weird numbers has positive density.

`HasPosDensity` is the right reading here, rather than the positive *lower* density that Erdős'
"positive density" usually abbreviates. Their Theorem 5 is stated as "the density of weird
numbers is positive", and they first establish that the density exists at all: "It is clear that
the weird numbers have a density since both the abundant numbers and the pseudoperfect numbers
have a density. (A weird number is abundant and not pseudoperfect.)" The work in the paper goes
into showing that density is not `0`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 (erdos_477)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_477 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℤ[X], 2 ≤ f.degree ∧ ∃ A : Set ℤ, ∀ z, ∃! ab ∈ A ×ˢ (f.eval '' {n | 0 < n}), z = ab.1 + ab.2
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a polynomial $f:\mathbb{Z}\to \mathbb{Z}$ of degree at least $2$ and a set
$A\subset \mathbb{Z}$ such that for any $z\in \mathbb{Z}$ there is exactly one $a\in A$ and
$b\in \{ f(n) : n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ such that $z=a+b$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 (erdos_477.variants.degree_two_dvd_condition_b_ne_zero)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_477.variants.degree_two_dvd_condition_b_ne_zero {a b c : ℤ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : a ∣ b) : let f
problems.humanStatement:
There is no such $A$ for any polynomial $f(x) = aX^2 + bX + c$, if $a | b$
with $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0.
This was found be AlphaProof for the specific instance $X^2 - X + 1$ and then generalised.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 (erdos_477.variants.monomial)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_477.variants.monomial (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : letI f
problems.humanStatement: Probably there is no such $A$ for the polynomial $X^k$ for any $k \ge 2$. This is asked in [Sek59].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 (erdos_477.variants.S_sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_477.variants.S_sq : letI f
problems.humanStatement:
There is no such $A$ for the polynomial $f(x) = X^2$.

This is shown in [Sek59].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 (erdos_477.variants.X_pow_three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_477.variants.X_pow_three : letI f
problems.humanStatement: Probably there is no such $A$ for the polynomial $X^3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 479 (erdos_479)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_479 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k > 1), { n | 2 ^ n ≡ k [MOD n]}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for all $k\neq 1$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$2^n\equiv k\pmod{n}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 48 (erdos_48)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_48 : answer(True) ↔ {(n, m) : ℕ × ℕ | n.totient = σ 1 m}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Are there infinitely many integers $n, m$ such that $ϕ(n) = σ(m)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 480 (erdos_480)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_480 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (x : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ n, x n ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) → ⨅ (n : ℕ+), atTop.liminf (fun m => (n : ℕ) * |x (m + (n : ℕ)) - x m|) ≤ 1 / √5
problems.humanStatement:
Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots\in [0,1]$ be an infinite sequence.
Is it true that
$$\inf_n \liminf_{m\to \infty} n \lvert x_{m+n}-x_m\rvert\leq 5^{-1/2}\approx 0.447?$$
A conjecture of Newman.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 480 (erdos_480.variants.chung_graham)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_480.variants.chung_graham : let c : ℝ
problems.humanStatement:
This was proved by Chung and Graham \cite{ChGr84}, who in fact prove that
$$\inf_n \liminf_{m\to \infty} n \lvert x_{m+n}-x_m\rvert\leq \frac{1}{c}\approx 0.3944$$
where
$$c=1+\sum_{k\geq 1}\frac{1}{F_{2k}}=2.5353705\cdots$$
and $F_m$ is the $m$th Fibonacci number.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 480 (erdos_480.variants.chung_graham_best_possible)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_480.variants.chung_graham_best_possible : let c : ℝ
problems.humanStatement: They also prove that this constant is best possible.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 481 (erdos_481)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_481 {r : ℕ} (a b : Fin r → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (hab : 1 < ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / a i) : ∃ k, ¬ ((T a b)^[k] [1]).Nodup
problems.humanStatement:
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{i}\frac{1}{a_i}>1$. For any
finite sequence of $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integers $A=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ let $T(A)$ denote
the sequence of length $rn$ given by
$$(a_ix_j+b_i)_{1\leq j\leq n, 1\leq i\leq r}.$$
Prove that, if $A_1=(1)$ and $A_{i+1}=T(A_i)$, then there must be some $A_k$ with repeated
elements.

This is true. This appears to have first been shown by Klarner [Kl82], with a generalisation
given by Kolpakov and Talambutsa [KoTa22]. Essentially the same proof was found independently by
Barreto in the comment section.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 486: Logarithmic density for sets avoiding modular subsets (erdos_486)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_486 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ X : (n : ℕ) → Set (ZMod n), ∃ d, {m : ℕ | ∀ n, (m : ZMod n) ∉ X n}.HasLogDensity d
problems.humanStatement:
For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ choose some $X_n \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$.
Let $B = \{m \in \mathbb{N} : \forall n, m \not\equiv x \pmod{n} \text{ for all } x \in X_n\}$.
Must $B$ have a logarithmic density?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 488 (erdos_488)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_488 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A.Nonempty → -- These are needed for the reasons outlined here: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/256 0 ∉ A → 1 ∉ A → letI B
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A$ be a finite set and
$$B=\{ n \geq 1 : a\mid n\textrm{ for some }a\in A\}.$$
Is it true that, for every $m>n\geq \max(A)$,
$$\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,m]\rvert }{m}< 2\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,n]\rvert}{n}?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 489 (erdos_489.variants.squarefree)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_489.variants.squarefree : ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => GapSumSq {n | ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n = p ^ 2} x / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.card_divisible_by_prime_gt_k)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.card_divisible_by_prime_gt_k : ∀ (k card p : ℕ), p.Prime → k ∈ Set.Ioo 0 p → p ∣ card → Erdos494Unique k card
problems.humanStatement:
Selfridge and Straus [SeSt58] proved that $A$ is determined by $A_k$
if $|A|$ is divisible by a prime greater than $k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.card_eq_2k)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.card_eq_2k : ∀ k > 2, ¬Erdos494Unique k (2 * k)
problems.humanStatement:
Similarly, Tao noted that the conjecture fails when $|A| = 2k$, by taking $A$ to be a set of
the total sum 0 and considering $-A$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.gordon_fraenkel_straus)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.gordon_fraenkel_straus : ∀ k > 2, ∀ᶠ card in atTop, Erdos494Unique k card
problems.humanStatement:
Gordon, Fraenkel, and Straus [GRS62] proved that the claim is true for all $k > 2$ when
$|A|$ is sufficiently large.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.k_eq_2_card_not_pow_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.k_eq_2_card_not_pow_two : ∀ card : ℕ, (∀ l : ℕ, card ≠ 2 ^ l) → Erdos494Unique 2 card
problems.humanStatement:
Selfridge and Straus [SeSt58] showed that the conjecture is true when $k = 2$ and
$|A| \ne 2^l$ for $l \ge 0$.
They also gave counterexamples when $k = 2$ and $|A| = 2^l$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.k_eq_2_card_pow_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.k_eq_2_card_pow_two : ∀ card : ℕ, (∃ l : ℕ, card = 2 ^ l) → ¬Erdos494Unique 2 card
problems.humanStatement:
Selfridge and Straus [SeSt58] gave counterexamples to the conjecture
when $k = 2$ and $|A| = 2^l$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.k_eq_3_card_gt_6)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.k_eq_3_card_gt_6 : ∀ card > 6, Erdos494Unique 3 card
problems.humanStatement:
Selfridge and Straus [SeSt58] also showed that the conjecture is true when
1) $k = 3$ and $|A| > 6$ or
2) $k = 4$ and $|A| > 12$.
More generally, they proved that $A$ is determined by $A_k$ (and $|A|$) if $|A|$ is divisible by
a prime greater than $k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.k_eq_4_card_gt_12)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.k_eq_4_card_gt_12 : ∀ card > 12, Erdos494Unique 4 card
problems.humanStatement:
Selfridge and Straus [SeSt58] showed that the conjecture is true
when $k = 4$ and $|A| > 12$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.k_eq_card)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.k_eq_card : ∀ k > 2, ¬Erdos494Unique k k
problems.humanStatement: Kruyt noted that the conjecture fails when $|A| = k$, by rotating $A$ around an appropriate point.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 494 (erdos_494.variants.product)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_494.variants.product : ∃ (A B : Finset ℂ), A.card = B.card ∧ prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B

problems.title: Erdős Problem 495 (erdos_495)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_495 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ α β : ℝ, liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * distToNearestInt (n * α) * distToNearestInt (n * β)) atTop = 0
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Is it true that$$\liminf_{n\to \infty} n \| n\alpha \|
  \| n\beta\| =0$$? This is also known as the Littlewood conjecture.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 498 (erdos_498)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_498 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : Fin n → ℂ), (∀ i, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) → ∀ c : ℂ, {ε : Fin n → ℤ | (∀ i, ε i = -1 ∨ ε i = 1) ∧ (∑ i, (ε i : ℂ) * z i) ∈ Metric.ball c 1}.ncard ≤ n.choose (n / 2)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathbb{C}$ with $1\leq \lvert z_i\rvert$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. Let $D$ be an
arbitrary disc of radius $1$. Is it true that the number of sums of the shape
$$\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_iz_i \textrm{ for }\epsilon_i\in \{-1,1\}$$
which lie in $D$ is at most $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$?

A strong form of the Littlewood-Offord problem. Erdős [Er45] proved this is true if
$z_i\in\mathbb{R}$, and for general $z_i\in\mathbb{C}$ proved a weaker upper bound of
$$\ll \frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n}}.$$
This was solved in the affirmative by Kleitman [Kl65], who also later generalised this to
arbitrary Hilbert spaces [Kl70].

See also [395].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 499 (erdos_499.variants.one_le)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_499.variants.one_le : answer(True) ↔ ∀ n > 0, ∀ M ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n), ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (∀ i, M i (σ i) ≠ 0) ∧ 1 ≤ ∑ i, M i (σ i)
problems.humanStatement:
A weaker version of Erdős' problem 499, which asks whether for every doubly stochastic matrix, there
exists a permutation $σ \in S_n$ with $M_{i, σ(i)} ≠ 0$ and such that
$$
\sum_{1 \leq i \leq n} M_{i, σ(i)} \geq 1
$$
Proved by Marcus and Ree [MaRe59].

[MaRe59] Marcus, M. and Ree, R., Diagonals of doubly stochastic matrices. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) (1959), 296-302.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C → ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ Tendsto (fun i => normalizedGap (n i)) atTop (𝓝 C)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $C\geq 0$. Is there an infinite sequence of $n_i$ such that
$$\lim_{i\to \infty}\frac{p_{n_i+1}-p_{n_i}}{\log n_i}=C?$$

We formalise "an infinite sequence of $n_i$" as a strictly monotone sequence of indices
`n : ℕ → ℕ`. Note that the numerator is the gap between the two *consecutive* primes
$p_{n_i}$ and $p_{n_i+1}$, which is `primeGap (n i)`, and not the gap between the primes
indexed by two consecutive members of the sequence.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5_iff_limit_point_set)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5_iff_limit_point_set : (∀ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C → C ∈ limitPointSet) ↔ limitPointSet = Ici 0
problems.humanStatement:
The statement of `erdos_5` is equivalent to the description of the set of limit points in
`erdos_5.variants.limit_point_set`; combine with `mem_limitPointSet_iff` to unfold the
membership into the sequence of indices $n_i$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard (β : Fin 9 → ℝ) (hβ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ β i) (hβmono : Monotone β) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ β j - β i ∈ limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement:
Banks, Freiberg, and Maynard [BFM16] showed that at least $12.5\%$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs
to $S$.

This is [BFM16, Theorem 1.1]: for any nine nonnegative reals
$\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\cdots\leq\beta_9$, at least one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$
with $i<j$ belongs to $S$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard_measure)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard_measure : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in atTop, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - ε) * T / 8) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)
problems.humanStatement:
The $12.5\%$ claim itself, as deduced in [BFM16, Corollary 1.2]:
$\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq (1-o(1))T/8$ as $T\to\infty$.

Note that the constant $1/8$ is only attained asymptotically and ineffectively; the bound
[BFM16] obtain for *all* $T>0$ is the weaker $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)>T/22$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.dense)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.dense : answer(sorry) ↔ Ici (0 : ℝ) ⊆ closure limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement:
In [Er65b], [Er85c], and [Er97c] Erdős asks whether $S$ is everywhere dense (but Weisenberg
notes that clearly $S$ is closed so this is equivalent to asking whether $S=[0,\infty]$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.erdos_ricci)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.erdos_ricci : 0 < volume limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement: Erdős [Er55] and Ricci [Ri56] independently showed that $S$ has positive Lebesgue measure.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.goldston_pintz_yildirim)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.goldston_pintz_yildirim : (0 : ℝ) ∈ limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement: $0\in S$ by the work of Goldston, Pintz, and Yildirim [GPY09] on small prime gaps.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier : ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ x ∈ limitPointSet, C < x
problems.humanStatement: Hildebrand and Maier [HiMa88] showed that $S$ contains arbitrarily large (finite) numbers.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier_measure)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier_measure : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in atTop, ENNReal.ofReal (c * T) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)
problems.humanStatement:
[HiMa88] in fact prove the stronger statement that there is a constant $c>0$ with
$\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq cT$ for all sufficiently large $T$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.limit_point_set)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.limit_point_set : answer(sorry) ↔ limitPointSet = Ici 0
problems.humanStatement:
Let $S$ be the set of limit points of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)/\log n$. This problem asks whether
$S=[0,\infty]$.

Since $\infty\in S$ is known (see `erdos_5.variants.westzynthius`), the open content is the
equality of the finite part of $S$ with $[0,\infty)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.merikoski)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski (β : Fin 4 → ℝ) (hβmono : Monotone β) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ β j - β i ∈ limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that at least $1/3$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs to $S$.

This is [Me20, Theorem 1]: for any reals $\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\beta_3\leq\beta_4$, at least
one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$ with $i<j$ belongs to $S$. Note that, in contrast with
`erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard`, the $\beta_i$ are not required to be nonnegative.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.merikoski_bounded_gaps)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_bounded_gaps : ∃ C ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ T ≥ (0 : ℝ), (limitPointSet ∩ Icc T (T + C)).Nonempty
problems.humanStatement:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that $S$ has bounded gaps.

This is [Me20, Corollary 3]: there is a (ineffective) constant $C\geq 0$ such that
$S\cap[T,T+C]\neq\emptyset$ for all $T\geq 0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.merikoski_measure)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_measure : ∀ T > (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal (T / 3) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)
problems.humanStatement:
The $1/3$ claim itself [Me20, Corollary 2]: $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq T/3$ for all $T>0$.

Unlike the $1/8$ of [BFM16], this bound holds uniformly in $T$ with no error term.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.pintz)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.pintz : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Icc 0 c ⊆ limitPointSet
problems.humanStatement: Pintz [Pi16] showed that there exists some small constant $c>0$ such that $[0,c]\subset S$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 (erdos_5.variants.westzynthius)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_5.variants.westzynthius : ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ Tendsto (fun i => normalizedGap (n i)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement: $\infty\in S$ by Westzynthius' result [We31] on large prime gaps.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 50 (erdos_50)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_50 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f), ¬∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Icc 0 1) x
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 50 (erdos_50_schoenberg)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_50_schoenberg : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f
problems.humanStatement:
Schoenberg [Sch38] proved that the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ exists.
That is, for any $c \in [0, 1]$, the proportion of integers $n \le N$ satisfying $\varphi(n)/n < c$
approaches a limit as $N \to \infty$. This limit function is the cumulative distribution function
of the values of $\varphi(n)/n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 50 (erdos_50_singular)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_50_singular (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f) : IsPurelySingular f
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er95] proved that the distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ is purely singular: it is
continuous, but its derivative is zero almost everywhere.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, Bornology.IsBounded (A x)) → (∀ x, volume.toOuterMeasure (A x) < 1) → ∃ X : Set ℝ, X.Infinite ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.tests.empty_family_is_valid)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.tests.empty_family_is_valid : let A : ℝ → Set ℝ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.tests.pair_independent_empty)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.tests.pair_independent_empty : ({0, 1} : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ (fun _ => (∅ : Set ℝ)) y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.tests.singleton_outer_measure_lt_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.tests.singleton_outer_measure_lt_one (x : ℝ) : volume.toOuterMeasure ({x} : Set ℝ) < 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.tests.singleton_zero_independent)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.tests.singleton_zero_independent (A : ℝ → Set ℝ) : ({0} : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.tests.unit_interval_measure)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.tests.unit_interval_measure : volume.toOuterMeasure (Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1) = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.closed_size3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.closed_size3 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, IsClosed (A x)) → (∀ x, volume (A x) < 1) → ∃ X : Set ℝ, 3 ≤ X.ncard ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.erdosHajnal_finite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.erdosHajnal_finite : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, Bornology.IsBounded (A x)) → (∀ x, volume.toOuterMeasure (A x) < 1) → ∃ X : Finset ℝ, n ≤ X.card ∧ (X : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.gladysz_size2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.gladysz_size2 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, IsClosed (A x)) → (∀ x, volume (A x) < 1) → ∃ X : Set ℝ, 2 ≤ X.ncard ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.hechler_CH)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.hechler_CH : answer(True) ↔ (ℵ₁ = 𝔠) → ∃ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, Bornology.IsBounded (A x)) ∧ (∀ x, volume.toOuterMeasure (A x) < 1) ∧ ¬ ∃ X : Set ℝ, X.Infinite ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.newelski_pawlikowski_seredynski)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.newelski_pawlikowski_seredynski : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ), (∀ x, IsClosed (A x)) → (∀ x, volume (A x) < 1) → ∃ X : Set ℝ, X.Infinite ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.pair_independent_iff)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.pair_independent_iff (A : ℝ → Set ℝ) {x y : ℝ} (hxy : x ≠ y) : ({x, y} : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y) ↔ x ∉ A y ∧ y ∉ A x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 (erdos_501.variants.singleton_independent)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_501.variants.singleton_independent (A : ℝ → Set ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ({x} : Set ℝ).Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 (erdos_503)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_503 (n : ℕ) : IsGreatest {(A.ncard) | (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)} answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
What is the size of the largest $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every three points from $A$
determine an isosceles triangle? That is, for any three points $x$, $y$, $z$ from $A$, at least two
of the distances $|x - y|$, $|y - z|$, $|x - z|$ are equal.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 (erdos_503.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_503.variants.lower_bound (n : ℕ) : (n + 1).choose 2 ≤ sSup {(A.ncard) | (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)}
problems.humanStatement:
Alweiss has observed a lower bound of $\binom{n + 1}{2}$ follows from considering the subset of
$\mathbb{R}^{n + 1}$ formed of all vectors $e_i + e_j$ where $e_i$, $e_j$ are distinct coordinate
vectors. This set can be viewed as a subset of some $\mathbb{R}^n$, and is easily checked to have
the required property.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 (erdos_503.variants.R2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_503.variants.R2 : IsGreatest {(A.ncard) | (A : Set ℝ²) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)} 6
problems.humanStatement:
When $n = 2$, the answer is 6 (due to Kelly [ErKe47] - an alternative proof is given by Kovács [Ko24c]).

[ErKe47] Erdős, Paul and Kelly, L. M., Elementary Problems and Solutions: Solutions: E735. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 227-229.
[Ko24c] Z. Kovács, A note on Erdős's mysterious remark. arXiv:2412.05190 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 (erdos_503.variants.R3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_503.variants.R3 : IsGreatest {(A.ncard) | (A : Set ℝ³) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)} 8
problems.humanStatement:
When $n = 3$, the answer is 8 (due to Croft [Cr62]).

[Cr62] Croft, H. T., $9$-point and $7$-point configurations in $3$-space. Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1962), 400-424.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 (erdos_503.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_503.variants.upper_bound (n : ℕ) : ∀ m ∈ {(A.ncard) | (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)}, m ≤ (n + 2).choose 2
problems.humanStatement:
The best upper bound known in general is due to Blokhius [Bl84] who showed that
$$
|A| \leq \binom{n + 2}{2}
$$

[Bl84] Blokhuis, A., Few-distance sets. (1984), iv+70.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 505 (erdos_505.small_dim)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_505.small_dim (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 3) (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (hS : Bornology.IsBounded S) (hd : 0 < diam S) : ∃ (F : Fin (n + 1) → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i ∧ ∀ i, diam (F i) < diam S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 505 (erdos_505.test_dim_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_505.test_dim_one (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (hS : Bornology.IsBounded S) (hd : 0 < diam S) : ∃ (F : Fin 2 → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))), S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i ∧ ∀ i, diam (F i) < diam S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.equivalent)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.equivalent: α ~[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\alpha(n)$ be such that every set of $n$ points in the unit disk contains three points which
determine a triangle of area at most $\alpha(n)$. Estimate $\alpha(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.lower: let ans
problems.humanStatement: Estimate a lower bound for$\alpha(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.upper)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.upper: let ans
problems.humanStatement: Estimate an upper bound for$\alpha(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.variants.lower_erdos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.variants.lower_erdos : α ≫ (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős observed that $\alpha(n) \gg 1/n^2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.variants.lower_kps82)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.variants.lower_kps82 : lowerBest ≪ α
problems.humanStatement: Current best lower bound [KPS82].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.variants.upper_cpz24)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.variants.upper_cpz24 : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ α ≪ (fun n ↦ upperBarrier n * (n : ℝ) ^ o n)
problems.humanStatement: Current best upper bound [CPZ24]: $\alpha(n) \ll n^{-7/6 + o(1)}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 507 (erdos_507.variants.upper_trivial)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_507.variants.upper_trivial : α ≪ (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: It is trivial that $\alpha(n) \ll 1/n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 509 (erdos_509)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_509 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.natDegree ≠ 0 → ∃ (ι : Type), Nonempty (BoundedDiscCover {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} 2 ι)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(z) ∈ ℂ[z]$ be a monic non-constant polynomial. Can the set
$\{z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1\}$
be covered by a set of closed discs the sum of whose radii is $≤ 2$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 509 (erdos_509.variants.Cartan_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_509.variants.Cartan_bound : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.natDegree ≠ 0 → ∃ (ι : Type), Nonempty (BoundedDiscCover {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} (2*rexp 1) ι)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(z) ∈ ℂ[z]$ be a monic non-constant polynomial. Can the set
$\{z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1\}$
be covered by a set of closed discs the sum of whose radii is $≤ 2e$?
Solution: True. This is due to Cartan.
See *Sur les systèmes de fonctions holomorphes à variétés linéaires
lacunaires et leurs applications*, Henri Cartan,
http://www.numdam.org/article/ASENS_1928_3_45__255_0.pdf
