problems.title: Erdős Problem 509 (erdos_509.variants.Pommerenke_connected)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_509.variants.Pommerenke_connected : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.natDegree ≠ 0 → IsConnected {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} → ∃ (ι : Type), Nonempty (BoundedDiscCover {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} 2 ι)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(z) ∈ ℂ[z]$ be a monic non-constant polynomial.
If it is connected, can the set $\{z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1\}$
be covered by a set of circles the sum of whose radii is $≤ 2$?
Solution: True. This is due to Pommerenke.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 51 (erdos_51)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_51 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, ∃ n : A → ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ (∀ a : A, IsLeast (φ ⁻¹' {(a : ℕ)}) (n a)) ∧ Tendsto (fun a : A => (n a : ℝ) / (a : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $a \in A$,
there is an integer n such that $\phi(n)=a$, and
yet if $n_a$ is the smallest such integer, then $\frac{n_a}{a} → \infty$ as $a → ∞$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 510 (erdos_510)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_510 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c), ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), 0 ∉ A → #A = N → ∃ θ, ∑ n ∈ A, cos (n * θ) < -c * sqrt N
problems.humanStatement:
**Chowla's cosine problem**

If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is a finite set of positive integers of size $N > 0$ then is there some
absolute constant $c>0$ and $\theta$ such that
$$\sum_{n\in A}\cos(n\theta) < -cN^{1/2}?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 510 (erdos_510.variants.bedert)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_510.variants.bedert : ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c), ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), 0 ∉ A → #A = N → ∃ θ, ∑ n ∈ A, cos (n * θ) < - c * N ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Bedert [Be25c] proved an upper bound of $-c N^{1/7}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 510 (erdos_510.variants.ruzsa)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_510.variants.ruzsa : ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c), ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), 0 ∉ A → #A = N → ∃ θ, ∑ n ∈ A, cos (n * θ) < - exp (c * sqrt (log N))
problems.humanStatement: Ruzsa [Ru04] proved an upper bound of $-\exp(O(\sqrt{\log N})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 513 (erdos_513)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_513 : answer(sorry) = ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f}, (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 513 (erdos_513.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_513.variants.lower_bound : ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f}, (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) > 1 / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 513 (erdos_513.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_513.variants.upper_bound : ∃ c > 0, ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f}, (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) ≤ 2 / π - c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 516 (erdos_516)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_516 {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : HasFabryGaps n) {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : ∀ n, a n ≠ 0) (hfn : ∀ z, HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)) (hf : OfFiniteOrder f) : limsup (fun r => ratio r f) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 516 (erdos_516.variants.limsup_ratio_eq_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_516.variants.limsup_ratio_eq_one {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ k, n k > k * log k ^ (2 + c)) {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : ∀ n, a n ≠ 0) (hfn : ∀ z, HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)) : limsup (fun r => ratio r f) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 516 (erdos_516.variants.limsup_ratio_eq_one_of_hasFejerGaps)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_516.variants.limsup_ratio_eq_one_of_hasFejerGaps : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : HasFejerGaps n) {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : ∀ n, a n ≠ 0) (hfn : ∀ z, HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)), limsup (fun r => ratio r f) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 517 (erdos_517)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_517 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : HasFabryGaps n) {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : ∀ k, a k ≠ 0) (hf : ∀ z, HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)) (z : ℂ), {x : ℂ | f x = z}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 517 (erdos_517.variants.fejer)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_517.variants.fejer {f : ℂ → ℂ} {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : HasFejerGaps n) {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : ∀ k, a k ≠ 0) (hf : ∀ z, HasSum (fun k => a k * z ^ n k) (f z)) (z : ℂ) : {x : ℂ | f x = z}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 52 (erdos_52)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_52 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : Finset ℤ), (max (A + A).card (A * A).card : ℝ) ≥ C * (A.card : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 520 (erdos_520)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_520 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ (Ω : Type) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), IsRademacherMultiplicative f → ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun N ↦ ∑ m ≤ N, f m ω / sqrt (N * log (log N))) atTop = c
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f$ be a Rademacher multiplicative function.
Does there exist some constant $c > 0$ such that, almost surely,
$$
  \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{m \leq N} f(m)}{\sqrt{N \log \log N}} = c?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 522 (erdos_522)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_522 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] (c : KacCoefficients ({-1, 1} : Set ℂ) Ω), ℙ {ω | atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (2 * c.numRootsInUnitDisk n ω : ℝ) / n) (𝓝 1)} = 1
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(z)=\sum_{0\leq k\leq n} \epsilon_k z^k$ be a random polynomial, where
$\epsilon_k\in \{-1,1\}$ independently uniformly at random for $0\leq k\leq n$.

Is it true that, if $R_n$ is the number of roots of $f(z)$ in
$\{ z\in \mathbb{C} : \lvert z\rvert \leq 1\}$, then
$$
  \frac{R_n}{n/2}\to 1
$$
almost surely?

There is some ambiguity as to whether the intended coefficient set is $\{-1, 1\}$ or $\{0, 1\}$,
see `erdos_522.variants.zero_one` for the alternate version.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 522 (erdos_522.variants.number_real_roots)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_522.variants.number_real_roots : ∃ p o : ℕ → ℝ, atTop.Tendsto o (𝓝 0) ∧ atTop.Tendsto p (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type*) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (f : KacCoefficients ({-1, 1} : Set ℝ) Ω), (ℙ {ω | |(f.roots n ω).card / (n : ℝ).log - 2 / π| ≥ o n}).toReal ≤ p n
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Offord showed that the number of real roots of a random degree `n` polynomial with `±1`
coefficients is `(2/π+o(1))log n`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 522 (erdos_522.variants.yakir_solution)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_522.variants.yakir_solution : ∃ p : ℕ → ℝ, atTop.Tendsto p (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type*) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (f : KacCoefficients ({-1, 1} : Set ℂ) Ω), (ℙ {ω | |(f.roots n ω).countP (· ∈ Metric.closedBall 0 1) - (n / 2 : ℝ)| ≥ n^(9/10 : ℝ) }).toReal ≤ p n
problems.humanStatement: Yakir proved that almost all Kac polynomials have `n/2+O(n^(9/10))` many roots in `{z∈C:|z|≤1}`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 522 (erdos_522.variants.zero_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_522.variants.zero_one : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (f : KacCoefficients ({0, 1} : Set ℂ) Ω), ℙ {ω | atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (2 * f.numRootsInUnitDisk n ω : ℝ) / n) (𝓝 1)} = 1
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(z)=\sum_{0\leq k\leq n} \epsilon_k z^k$ be a random polynomial, where
$\epsilon_k\in \{0,1\}$ independently uniformly at random for $0\leq k\leq n$.

Is it true that, if $R_n$ is the number of roots of $f(z)$ in
$\{ z\in \mathbb{C} : \lvert z\rvert \leq 1\}$, then
$$
  \frac{R_n}{n/2}\to 1
$$
almost surely?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 5 → δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card → ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), c * n ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧ G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\delta > 0$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with no
$K_5$ and at least $\delta n^2$ edges, must $G$ contain a set of $\gg_\delta n$ vertices
spanning no triangle?

Equivalently, writing $\mathrm{RT}_3(n, K_5, m)$ for the maximum number of edges of a
$K_5$-free graph on $n$ vertices in which every triangle-free vertex set has fewer than $m$
vertices (the *triangle Ramsey–Turán number*), is
$$\delta_3(5) = \lim_{\epsilon \to 0} \lim_{n \to \infty}
  \frac{\mathrm{RT}_3(n, K_5, \epsilon n)}{n^2} = 0?$$

This is a problem of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and Szemerédi [EHSSS94], who proved
$\delta_3(5) \leq 1/12$ and the analogous $\delta_3(4) = 0$, and observed $\delta_3(7) \geq 1/4$
via a construction of Erdős and Rogers [ErRo62].

The answer is **no**: Balogh and Lenz [BaLe13] disproved it by showing $\delta_3(5) > 0$, and
the exact value $\delta_3(5) = 1/12$ was determined by the matching lower-bound construction of
Liu, Reiher, Sharifzadeh, and Staden [LRSS21] (see `erdos_533.variants.lrss_lower`).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533.variants.delta_four_eq_zero)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533.variants.delta_four_eq_zero : ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 → δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card → ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), c * n ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧ G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3
problems.humanStatement:
The contrasting positive result $\delta_3(4) = 0$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and
Szemerédi [EHSSS94]: the $K_4$ analogue of `erdos_533` is **true**. For every $\delta > 0$
there is a $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_4$-free graph $G$ on
$n$ vertices with at least $\delta n^2$ edges contains a triangle-free vertex set of size at
least $c n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533.variants.delta_seven_ge_quarter)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533.variants.delta_seven_ge_quarter (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 7 ∧ (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) ∧ (1 / 4 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
problems.humanStatement:
The observation $\delta_3(7) \geq 1/4$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and Szemerédi
[EHSSS94], via a construction of Erdős and Rogers [ErRo62]: for every $\epsilon, \delta > 0$
and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a $K_7$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every
triangle-free vertex set has at most $\delta n$ vertices, yet which has at least
$(1/4 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533.variants.ehsss_upper)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533.variants.ehsss_upper (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 5 → (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) → (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 12 + ε) * n ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
The upper bound $\delta_3(5) \leq 1/12$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and Szemerédi
[EHSSS94]: for every $\epsilon > 0$ there is a $\delta > 0$ such that for all sufficiently
large $n$, every $K_5$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every triangle-free vertex
set has at most $\delta n$ vertices has at most $(1/12 + \epsilon)n^2$ edges.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533.variants.lrss_lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533.variants.lrss_lower (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 5 ∧ (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) ∧ (1 / 12 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
problems.humanStatement:
The matching lower bound $\delta_3(5) \geq 1/12$, from the construction of Liu, Reiher,
Sharifzadeh, and Staden [LRSS21] (improving the earlier $\delta_3(5) > 0$ of Balogh and Lenz
[BaLe13]): for every $\epsilon, \delta > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a
$K_5$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every triangle-free vertex set has at most
$\delta n$ vertices, yet which has at least $(1/12 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges. In particular this
refutes `erdos_533`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 (erdos_533.variants.test_bot)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_533.variants.test_bot (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Sanity check for the triangle-free-set condition: in the empty graph every vertex set spans
no triangle, since the empty graph has no $3$-clique.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535 : ∀ r ≥ 3, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop, (f r N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (c / log (log (N : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $r \geq 3$, and let $f_r(N)$ denote the size of the largest subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$
such that no subset of size $r$ has the same pairwise greatest common divisor between all
elements. Erdős [Er64] proved that $f_3(N) > N^{c/\log\log N}$ for some constant $c > 0$, and
conjectured this should also be an upper bound; here we state the conjectural upper bound
for all $r \geq 3$.

See also [536].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.abbott_hanson)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.abbott_hanson {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop, (f r N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.erdos_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.erdos_upper_bound {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop, (f r N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 4 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.first_open_case)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.first_open_case : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop, (f 3 N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (c / log (log (N : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
The first open case of Erdős Problem 535 is $r = 3$: there should exist $c > 0$ such that
$f_3(N) \leq N^{c/\log\log N}$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.lower_bound : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop, (N : ℝ) ^ (c / log (log (N : ℝ))) ≤ (f 3 N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.sunflower_erdos_rado)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.sunflower_erdos_rado {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : ∃ c_r > (0 : ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, AllBigOmega k A → NoConstantPairwiseGcdCoprimeSubsets r A → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ c_r ^ k * (Nat.factorial k)
problems.humanStatement:
For the stronger $Ω(n)=k$ variant above, the Erdős–Rado method gives the weaker
bound $c_r^k \cdot k!$; see Erdős [Er73].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 (erdos_535.variants.sunflower_strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_535.variants.sunflower_strong {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : ∃ c_r > (0 : ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, AllBigOmega k A → NoConstantPairwiseGcdCoprimeSubsets r A → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ c_r ^ k
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er73] records that Abbott pointed out the ordinary sunflower conjecture
does not seem to suffice here. The stronger auxiliary conjecture uses $Ω(n)=k$,
i.e. prime factors counted with multiplicity; this stronger statement would imply
the conjectured upper bound for $f_r(N)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 536 (erdos_536)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_536 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0: ℝ)), ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A ⊆ Icc 1 N → (ε * (N : ℝ)) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) → ∃ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A), # {a, b, c} = 3 ∧ a.lcm b = b.lcm c ∧ b.lcm c = a.lcm c
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $N$ be sufficiently large. Is it true that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\epsilon N$ then there must be distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that
$$[a, b]=[b, c]=[a, c],$$
where $[\cdot, \cdot]$ denotes the least common multiple?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 538 (erdos_538)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_538 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => maxMass r N * Real.log (Real.log N) / Real.log N) atTop (𝓝 c)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $r\geq 2$ and suppose that $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is such that, for any
$m$, there are at most $r$ solutions to $m=pa$ where $p$ is prime and $a\in A$.
Give the best possible upper bound for $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$.

The order is known — `∑ 1/n = Θ_r(log N / loglog N)` (see `erdos_538.matching_order`) —
but the sharp constant is not. This asks whether `maxMass r N` has a well-defined
leading constant `c_r` in `c_r · log N / loglog N`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539 : (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq : (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq_cube_root)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq_cube_root : (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.limit)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.limit : atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ Real.log (cofactorThreshold n) / Real.log n) answer(sorry)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.sq : (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root : (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root_isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root_isBigO : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 (erdos_539.variants.sq_isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_isBigO : (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 541 (erdos_541.variants.general_moduli)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_541.variants.general_moduli (p : ℕ) (a : Fin p → ZMod p) (ha₀ : ∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) : (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 541 (erdos_541.variants.large_primes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_541.variants.large_primes : ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ a : Fin p → ZMod p, (∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) → (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 562 (erdos_562)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_562 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Prove that, for $r \ge 3$,
$$ \log_{r-1} R_r(n) \asymp_r n, $$
where $\log_{r-1}$ denotes the $(r-1)$-fold iterated logarithm.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 564 (erdos_564)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_564 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (2 : ℝ)^(2 : ℝ)^(c * n) ≤ hypergraphRamsey 3 n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $R_3(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $m$
vertices are $2$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of the complete $3$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Is there some constant $c>0$ such that
$$ R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}? $$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 566 (erdos_566)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_566 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin p)), -- G is sparse: every induced subgraph on k ≥ 2 vertices has ≤ 2k - 3 edges (∀ S : Finset (Fin p), 2 ≤ S.card → (G.induce S).edgeSet.ncard ≤ 2 * S.card - 3) → -- Then G is Ramsey size linear ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel H.Adj], -- H has no isolated vertices (∀ v, 0 < H.degree v) → -- r̂(G,H) ≤ c · m (sizeRamsey G H : ℝ) ≤ c * H.edgeSet.ncard
problems.humanStatement:
Let $G$ be such that any subgraph on $k$ vertices has at most $2k-3$ edges.
Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then $\hat{r}(G,H) \ll m$?

In other words: if $G$ is sparse (every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices has $≤ 2k-3$ edges),
is $G$ Ramsey size linear?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 567 (erdos_567.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_567.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ IsRamseySizeLinear Q3
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 567 (Q3)**

Is $Q_3$ (the 3-dimensional hypercube) Ramsey size linear?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 567 (erdos_567.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_567.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ IsRamseySizeLinear K33
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 567 (K33)**

Is $K_{3,3}$ Ramsey size linear?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 567 (erdos_567.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_567.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ IsRamseySizeLinear H5
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 567 (H5)**

Is $H_5$ ($C_5$ with two vertex-disjoint chords) Ramsey size linear?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 579 (erdos_579)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_579 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), octahedron.Free G → δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card → c * n ≤ (G.indepNum : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\delta > 0$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with no
$K_{2,2,2}$ (the octahedron) and at least $\delta n^2$ edges, must $G$ contain an independent
set of size $\gg_\delta n$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Hajnal, Sós, and Szemerédi [EHSS83]. It is **open**; they proved
the statement for $\delta > 1/8$ (see `erdos_579.variants.ehss_large_delta`), and the
difficulty is to push the edge-density threshold down to an arbitrary $\delta > 0$.

Here $K_{2,2,2}$ is the complete tripartite graph with all parts of size $2$, encoded as
`completeMultipartiteGraph (fun _ : Fin 3 => Fin 2)`; "contains no $K_{2,2,2}$" is expressed
via `SimpleGraph.Free`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 579 (erdos_579.variants.ehss_large_delta)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_579.variants.ehss_large_delta (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 1 / 8 < δ) : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), octahedron.Free G → δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card → c * n ≤ (G.indepNum : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
The partial result of Erdős, Hajnal, Sós, and Szemerédi [EHSS83]: the statement of
`erdos_579` holds whenever the edge-density coefficient exceeds $1/8$. That is, for every
$\delta > 1/8$ there is a $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every
$K_{2,2,2}$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $\delta n^2$ edges has an independent
set of size at least $c n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 579 (erdos_579.variants.octahedron_not_free)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_579.variants.octahedron_not_free : ¬ octahedron.Free octahedron
problems.humanStatement:
Sanity check that the forbidden structure is non-trivial: the octahedron is of course not
octahedron-free, since it contains a copy of itself.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 587 (erdos_587.variants.nguyen_vu)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_587.variants.nguyen_vu : ∃ᵉ (O > 0) (O' > 0), ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, (MaxNotSqSum N : ℝ) ≤ O' * Real.nthRoot 3 N * (N : ℝ).log^O
problems.humanStatement: Nguyen and Vu proved that $|A| \ll N^{1/3} (\log N)^{O(1)}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 590 (erdos_590)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_590 : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$. It was proved by Chang [Ch72] that any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 590 (erdos_590.variants.finite_cardinal)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_590.variants.finite_cardinal (m : ℕ) : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) m
problems.humanStatement:
Let m be a finite cardinal $< \omega$. Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$.
It was proved by Milnor that any red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a
red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$. A shorter proof was found by Larson [La73]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 590 (erdos_590.variants.ge_three_false)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_590.variants.ge_three_false {n : ℕ} (h : 3 ≤ n) : ¬ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ n) (ω ^ n) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^n$ for $3≤ n < \omega$ then it is not the case that any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 590 (erdos_590.variants.two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_590.variants.two : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ 2) (ω ^ 2) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^2$ any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 591 (erdos_591)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_591 : answer(True) ↔ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω ^ 2) (ω ^ ω ^ 2) 3
problems.humanStatement:
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega^2}$. Is it true that any red/blue colouring of the
edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$?

This is true and was proved independently by Schipperus [Sc10] and Darby.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 592 (erdos_592)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_592 (β : Ordinal.{u}) : β.card ≤ ℵ₀ → OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ β) (ω ^ β) 3 ↔ (answer(sorry) : Ordinal.{u} → Prop) β
problems.humanStatement:
Determine which countable ordinals $β$ have the property that, if $α = \omega^β$, then in any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), IsObligatory F ↔ F.IsTwoColorable
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 593 ($500)**: Characterize those finite 3-uniform hypergraphs which appear
in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number $> \aleph_0$.

A natural conjectural characterization, recorded here, is that the obligatory finite 3-uniform
hypergraphs are exactly the 2-colorable ones (Property B). The forward direction
(`IsObligatory → IsTwoColorable`) and converse (`IsTwoColorable → IsObligatory`) are stated as
separate variants below; in the graph case ($r = 2$), Erdős–Galvin–Hajnal [EGH75] proved the
analogous result (obligatory ⇔ bipartite).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.empty_hypergraph_obligatory)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.empty_hypergraph_obligatory : IsObligatory (W
problems.humanStatement:
**The empty hypergraph is trivially obligatory**: The 3-uniform hypergraph on `PEmpty` (no
vertices, no edges) appears in every hypergraph via the empty injection.

This degenerate case confirms the definition is well-formed.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.graph_case_bipartite_obligatory)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.graph_case_bipartite_obligatory : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), ℵ₀ < G.chromaticCardinal → ∀ (W : Type*) [Fintype W] (F : SimpleGraph W), F.IsBipartite → Nonempty (F ↪g G)
problems.humanStatement:
**Graph analogue — bipartite graphs are obligatory (Erdős–Galvin–Hajnal [EGH75])**:
For the 2-uniform (graph) case, a graph of chromatic cardinal $> \aleph_0$ must contain all
finite bipartite graphs. Specifically, for every finite bipartite graph `F` and every graph
`G` with chromatic cardinal $> \aleph_0$, there is a graph embedding from `F` into `G`.

This uses `Nonempty (F ↪g G)` (graph embedding), aligned with the injective vertex map
used in the hypergraph `Appears` definition.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.graph_case_no_odd_cycle)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.graph_case_no_odd_cycle : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, Odd k → 3 ≤ k → ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ IsEmpty (cycleGraph k →g G)
problems.humanStatement:
**Graph analogue — no odd cycle is obligatory (Erdős–Galvin–Hajnal [EGH75])**:
For every odd $k \geq 3$, there exists a graph with chromatic cardinal $\aleph_1$ that
contains no cycle of length $k$. This shows the class of obligatory graphs is strictly
smaller than all finite graphs.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.implications_combine)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.implications_combine (h₁ : ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), IsObligatory F → F.IsTwoColorable) (h₂ : ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), F.IsTwoColorable → IsObligatory F) : ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), IsObligatory F ↔ F.IsTwoColorable
problems.humanStatement:
**Conjunction of the two open implications gives the conjectured characterization**: if both
`obligatory_implies_two_colorable` and `two_colorable_implies_obligatory` hold, then the
characterization conjectured in `erdos_593` (`IsObligatory F ↔ F.IsTwoColorable`) follows by
elementary `Iff` manipulation.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.nonempty_edges_if_large_chromatic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.nonempty_edges_if_large_chromatic {V : Type} (H : ThreeUniformHypergraph V) (hχ : ℵ₀ < H.chromaticCardinal) : H.edges.Nonempty
problems.humanStatement:
**No hyperedges implies chromatic cardinal ≤ 1**: A 3-uniform hypergraph with no edges can
be properly colored with a single color, so its chromatic cardinal is at most 1. In
particular, $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$ implies `H` has at least one hyperedge.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.obligatory_implies_two_colorable)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.obligatory_implies_two_colorable : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), IsObligatory F → F.IsTwoColorable
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 593 — Necessary direction**: Every obligatory finite 3-uniform
hypergraph is 2-colorable.

This is the natural necessary condition for the conjectural characterization in `erdos_593`:
if a finite 3-uniform hypergraph `F` is not 2-colorable, one expects to construct a
hypergraph with large chromatic number that contains no copy of `F`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.obligatory_monotone)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.obligatory_monotone {W₁ W₂ : Type} [Fintype W₁] [Fintype W₂] [DecidableEq W₂] {F₁ : ThreeUniformHypergraph W₁} {F₂ : ThreeUniformHypergraph W₂} (h12 : F₁.Appears F₂) (hObl : IsObligatory F₂) : IsObligatory F₁
problems.humanStatement:
**Monotonicity of the obligatory property**: If `F₁` appears in `F₂` and `F₂` is obligatory,
then `F₁` is also obligatory.

**Proof:** For any `H` with $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$, since `F₂` is obligatory, `F₂` appears
in `H` via some injection `φ₂`. Since `F₁` appears in `F₂` via `φ₁`, the composition
`φ₂ ∘ φ₁` witnesses that `F₁` appears in `H`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.two_colorable_implies_obligatory)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.two_colorable_implies_obligatory : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (F : ThreeUniformHypergraph W), F.IsTwoColorable → IsObligatory F
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 593 — Sufficient direction**: Every finite 2-colorable 3-uniform
hypergraph is obligatory.

This is the converse direction of the `erdos_593` characterization: if 2-colorability
matches the graph-case characterization (bipartite ⇔ obligatory), then every 2-colorable
finite 3-uniform hypergraph must appear in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number
$> \aleph_0$.

Together with `erdos_593.variants.obligatory_implies_two_colorable`, this implies `erdos_593`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (erdos_593.variants.uncountable_vertices_if_large_chromatic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_593.variants.uncountable_vertices_if_large_chromatic {V : Type} (H : ThreeUniformHypergraph V) (hχ : ℵ₀ < H.chromaticCardinal) : ¬ Countable V
problems.humanStatement:
**Vertices must be uncountable**: Every 3-uniform hypergraph with chromatic cardinal
$> \aleph_0$ must have an uncountable vertex set.

**Proof:** If `V` is countable, there exists an injection `φ : V → ℕ`. Using distinct natural
numbers as colors gives a proper coloring, so $\chi(H) \leq \#\mathbb{N} = \aleph_0$,
contradicting $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 594 (erdos_594)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_594 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ) → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k → ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 594** (Erdős–Hajnal [ErHa66], [Er69b]):

Does every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ contain all sufficiently
large odd cycles?

The answer is **Yes**, proved by Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah [EHS74].

A graph has chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ (i.e. uncountable chromatic number)
if and only if it admits no proper colouring with countably many colours; this is
encoded as `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`. The conclusion states that there is some
$N$ such that for every $k \geq N$ the graph contains a cycle of odd length $2k + 1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 594 (erdos_594.variants.bot_countably_colorable)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_594.variants.bot_countably_colorable : ¬ IsEmpty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph ℕ).Coloring ℕ)
problems.humanStatement:
Sanity check for the encoding of "chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$": a countably
colourable graph, such as the empty graph on $\mathbb{N}$, does not satisfy the
hypothesis `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 594 (erdos_594.variants.erdos_hajnal)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_594.variants.erdos_hajnal (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : ∀ (α : Type), #α ≤ ℵ_ 1 → IsEmpty (G.Coloring α)) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k → ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1
problems.humanStatement:
The earlier result of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66]: every graph with chromatic number
$\geq \aleph_2$ contains all sufficiently large odd cycles.

Chromatic number $\geq \aleph_2$ is encoded as the nonexistence of a proper colouring
with any set of at most $\aleph_1$ colours.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type*) (_ : Infinite V) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ ¬IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 595 ($250)**: Is there an infinite graph $G$ which contains no $K_4$ and is
not the union of countably many triangle-free graphs?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er87].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.complete_nat_is_union)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.complete_nat_is_union : IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree (⊤ : SimpleGraph ℕ)
problems.humanStatement:
**The complete graph `⊤` on `ℕ` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs**: we decompose
it into the family of star graphs `{H_m}_{m : ℕ}`, where `H_m` is the graph with edges `{m, n}`
for all `n ≠ m`. Each star is triangle-free (any two non-center vertices share no edge within
the star), and their union covers all edges of `⊤`.

**Proof sketch (star triangle-free):** If `{a, b, c}` were a triangle in `H_m`, then each of
the three edges `{a, b}`, `{a, c}`, `{b, c}` would pass through `m`. In particular, from
`{a, b}` we get `a = m` or `b = m`; from `{b, c}` we get `b = m` or `c = m`. Case analysis
shows that two vertices must equal `m`, contradicting the triangle having three distinct vertices.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.folkman_finite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.folkman_finite : answer(True) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ (V : Type*) (_ : Fintype V) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ ∀ (H : Fin n → SimpleGraph V), (∀ i, (H i).CliqueFree 3) → G ≠ ⨆ i, H i
problems.humanStatement:
**Folkman–Nešetřil–Rödl (finite version) [Fo70, NeRo75]**: For every `n ≥ 1`, there exists a
graph `G` (on a finite vertex set) that contains no $K_4$ and whose edges cannot be covered by
`n` triangle-free graphs.

More precisely: for every `n : ℕ` with `1 ≤ n`, there exist a finite type `V` and a graph
`G : SimpleGraph V` with:
1. `G.CliqueFree 4` (no $K_4$), and
2. For every family `H : Fin n → SimpleGraph V` of triangle-free graphs, `G ≠ ⨆ i, H i`.

This is the finite analogue of Problem 595. The proofs of Folkman [Fo70] and Nešetřil–Rödl
[NeRo75] give different explicit constructions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.K4_not_cliqueFree)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.K4_not_cliqueFree : ¬ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).CliqueFree 4
problems.humanStatement:
**The complete graph `⊤` on `Fin 4` is not $K_4$-free**: `⊤` on `Fin 4` equals the complete
graph $K_4$, so it contains $K_4$ as a subgraph and is not $K_4$-free.

This sanity check confirms the $K_4$-free hypothesis of Problem 595 is non-trivial.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.reformulation_edge_colouring)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.reformulation_edge_colouring {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G ↔ ∃ c : G.edgeSet → ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {e | ∃ h : e ∈ G.edgeSet, c ⟨e, h⟩ = n}).CliqueFree 3
problems.humanStatement:
**Reformulation via edge colourings**: A graph `G` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs
if and only if there is a colouring of the edges of `G` by `ℕ` such that no monochromatic
triangle exists.

More precisely: `IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G` is equivalent to the existence of a map
`c : G.edgeSet → ℕ` such that for each `n : ℕ`, the subgraph of edges coloured `n` is triangle-free.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.subgraph_of_countable_union)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.subgraph_of_countable_union {V : Type*} {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hH : H ≤ G) (hG : IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G) : IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree H
problems.humanStatement:
**Monotonicity**: If `G` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs and `H ≤ G` (i.e., `H` is
a subgraph of `G`), then `H` is also a countable union of triangle-free graphs.

**Proof**: If `G = ⨆ i, G_i` with each `G_i` triangle-free, then `H = ⨆ i, H ⊓ G_i`.
Each `H ⊓ G_i` is triangle-free because it is a subgraph of `G_i`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 595 (erdos_595.variants.triangle_free_is_union)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_595.variants.triangle_free_is_union {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) : IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G
problems.humanStatement:
**Triangle-free graphs are trivially countable unions of triangle-free graphs**: if `G` is
already triangle-free, then `G = ⨆ i : ℕ, G_i` where `G_0 = G` and `G_i = ⊥` for `i ≥ 1`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596 : ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂), IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂ ↔ (answer(sorry) : ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type}, SimpleGraph U₁ → SimpleGraph U₂ → Prop) G₁ G₂
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 596** (Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

  (1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured that no such pair exists; but $(C_4, C_6)$
witnesses it (Nešetřil–Rödl + Erdős–Hajnal). The full question is to characterise the
class of all such pairs, recorded here as `answer(sorry)`.

See Problem 595 for the specific case $(G_1, G_2) = (K_4, K_3)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.test.empty_is_free)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.test.empty_is_free : (cycleGraph 4).Free (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 0))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_finite_ramsey)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_finite_ramsey : HasFiniteRamseyProperty (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_is_exceptional)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_is_exceptional : IsErdosHajnalExceptional (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.C4_free_countable_escape)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_free_countable_escape : HasCountableRamseyEscape (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.exists_exceptional)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.exists_exceptional : ∃ (U₁ U₂ : Type) (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂), IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_exceptional_iff)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_exceptional_iff : answer(sorry) ↔ IsErdosHajnalExceptional (completeGraph (Fin 4)) (completeGraph (Fin 3))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_finite_ramsey)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_finite_ramsey : HasFiniteRamseyProperty (completeGraph (Fin 4)) (completeGraph (Fin 3))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596 (erdos_596.variants.original_conjecture_is_false)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_596.variants.original_conjecture_is_false : answer(False) ↔ ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂), ¬IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂

problems.title: Erdős Problem 598 (erdos_598)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_598 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : { s : Set m // s.Countable } → κ.out, ∀ X : Set m, #X = κ → c '' { s : { sub : Set m // sub.Countable } | s.1 ⊆ X } = Set.univ
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 598:**
Let $m$ be an infinite cardinal and $\kappa$ be the successor cardinal of $2^{\aleph_0}$.
Can one colour the countable subsets of $m$ using $\kappa$ many colours so that every
$X \subseteq m$ with $|X| = \kappa$ contains subsets of all possible colours?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 599 (erdos_599)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_599 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V), Disjoint A B → G.IsIndepSet A → G.IsIndepSet B → ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V), (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧ (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧ S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧ (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧ (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S)
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 599** (the Erdős–Menger conjecture).

Let $G$ be a (possibly infinite) graph and let $A, B$ be disjoint independent sets of
vertices. Must there exist a family $P$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from $A$ to $B$,
and a set $S$ of vertices containing exactly one vertex from each path in $P$, such that
every path from $A$ to $B$ contains at least one vertex of $S$?

For finite $G$ this is equivalent to Menger's theorem. The answer is **yes**, proved by
Aharoni and Berger [AhBe09].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 599 (erdos_599.test.empty_A)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_599.test.empty_A (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (B : Set V) : ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V), (∀ i, a i ∈ (∅ : Set V)) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧ (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧ S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧ (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧ (∀ a' ∈ (∅ : Set V), ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S)
problems.humanStatement:
Sanity check: when $A = \varnothing$ the conclusion of `erdos_599` holds trivially, with
the empty family of paths and $S = \varnothing$ (the covering condition is vacuous since
there is no path starting in $\varnothing$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 599 (erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger : ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V), ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V), (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧ (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧ S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧ (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧ (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S)
problems.humanStatement:
**Menger's theorem for infinite graphs** (Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09]).

The theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger holds for arbitrary vertex sets $A$
and $B$: in any (possibly infinite) graph $G$ there is a family $P$ of pairwise
vertex-disjoint $A$--$B$ paths together with an $A$--$B$ separator $S$ consisting of the
choice of exactly one vertex from each path in $P$. The disjointness and independence
hypotheses of `erdos_599` are not needed.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6 (erdos_6)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_6 : {n | primeGap n < primeGap (n + 1) ∧ primeGap (n + 1) < primeGap (n + 2)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6 (erdos_6.variants.decreasing)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) : {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6 (erdos_6.variants.increasing)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) : {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 60 (erdos_60)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_60 : ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj], (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) → (c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $>\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$ edges contain $\gg n^{1/2}$ many
copies of $C_4$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 60 (erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang : ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) (_hq : Even q), ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q^2 + q + 1))) [DecidableRel G.Adj], (extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) → (c * Real.sqrt ((q^2 + q + 1) : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some even integer $q$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 60 (erdos_60.variants.two_copies)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_60.variants.two_copies : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj], (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) → (2 ≤ { H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Simonovits conjectured that at least 2 copies of $C_4$ are guaranteed.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 600 (erdos_600.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_600.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (eFunction n (r + 1) : ℝ) - (eFunction n r : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement: Let $r \geq 2$. Is it true that $e(n,r+1) - e(n,r) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 600 (erdos_600.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_600.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (eFunction n (r + 1) : ℝ) / (eFunction n r : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)
problems.humanStatement: Let $r \geq 2$. Is it true that $\frac{e(n,r+1)}{e(n,r)} \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 600 (erdos_600.variants.ruzsa_szemeredi_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_600.variants.ruzsa_szemeredi_upper_bound : ∀ r : ℕ, (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (eFunction n r : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ)^2)
problems.humanStatement: Ruzsa and Szemerédi [RuSz78] proved that $e(n,r)=o(n^2)$ for any fixed $r$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {α : Type*} {I : Type*} (A : I → Set α), (∀ i, (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Set.ncard (A i ∩ A j) ≠ 1) → HasPropertyB I A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.countable_index)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602.variants.countable_index : answer(True) ↔ ∀ {α : Type*} (A : ℕ → Set α), (∀ i, (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Set.ncard (A i ∩ A j) ≠ 1) → HasPropertyB ℕ A
problems.humanStatement:
**Countable index set case.**

If the index set is countable, the answer is yes, and the intersection
condition is unnecessary. This is Bernstein's Lemma:
every countable system of infinite sets has Property B.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.disjoint)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602.variants.disjoint : answer(True) ↔ ∀ {α : Type*} {I : Type*} (A : I → Set α), (∀ i, (A i).Infinite) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (A i) (A j)) → HasPropertyB I A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.empty_index)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602.variants.empty_index {α : Type*} : ∀ (A : PEmpty → Set α), (∀ i, (A i).Infinite) → HasPropertyB PEmpty A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.single_set)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602.variants.single_set {α : Type*} (A : Set α) (hA : A.Infinite) : ∃ f : α → Fin 2, ¬IsMonochromatic f A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.two_sets)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602 (erdos_602.variants.unique_index)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_602.variants.unique_index {α : Type*} (I : Type*) [Unique I] (A : I → Set α) (hInfinite : ∀ i, (A i).Infinite) : HasPropertyB I A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture (erdos_61)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_61 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α), ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement:
The Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture states that there is a constant $c(H) > 0$ for each
$H$ such that we can take $f(n) = n^{c(H)}$ in the above formulation.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture (erdos_61.variants.bnss23)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_61.variants.bnss23 : ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α), ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n * log (log n))))
problems.humanStatement:
Bucić, Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [BNSS23] improved this to
$f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n \log \log n})$ for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[BNSS23] Bucić, M. and Nguyen, T. and Scott, A. and Seymour, P., A loglog step towards Erdos-Hajnal

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture (erdos_61.variants.c5)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_61.variants.c5 : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (cycleGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement:
Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [CSSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = C_5$, the
cycle on five vertices: every graph with no induced five-cycle has a clique or independent
set of polynomial size.

[CSSS23] Chudnovsky, M., Scott, A., Seymour, P. and Spirkl, S., Erdős–Hajnal for graphs with
no 5-hole. Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) 126 (2023), 997–1014.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture (erdos_61.variants.erha89)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_61.variants.erha89 : ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α), ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n)))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89] proved that we can take $f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n})$
for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[ErHa89] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., Ramsey-type theorems. Discrete Appl. Math. (1989), 37-52.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture (erdos_61.variants.p5)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_61.variants.p5 : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (pathGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = P_5$, the path on five
vertices: every $P_5$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a clique or independent set of
polynomial size.

[NSS23] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., Induced subgraph density. VII. The
five-vertex path. [arXiv:2312.15333](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15333)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 613 (erdos_613)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_613 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 3, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), [DecidableRel G.Adj] → G.edgeFinset.card = Nat.choose (2 * n + 1) 2 - Nat.choose n 2 - 1 → ∃ (B D : SimpleGraph V), [DecidableRel B.Adj] → [DecidableRel D.Adj] → G = B ⊔ D ∧ B.IsBipartite ∧ ∀ v, D.degree v < n
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 613:**
Let $n \geq 3$ and $G$ be a graph with $\binom{2n+1}{2} - \binom{n}{2} - 1$ edges.
Must $G$ be the union of a bipartite graph and a graph with maximum degree less than $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 (erdos_615)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_615 : answer(False) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), (1 / 8 - c) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card → ¬ G.CliqueFree 4 ∨ (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ≤ G.indepNum
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist some constant $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, if $G$ is a
graph with $n$ vertices and at least $(1/8 - c)n^2$ edges then $G$ must contain either a $K_4$
or an independent set on at least $n/\log n$ vertices?

The answer is no, as shown by Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 (erdos_615.variants.fox_loh_zhao)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_615.variants.fox_loh_zhao (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ n, 0 ≤ f n) (hfo : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f n / Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n))) atTop (nhds 0)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ n * Real.exp (-f n) ∧ (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card
problems.humanStatement:
The result of Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15] disproving the problem: if $f(n) \geq 0$ satisfies
$f(n) = o(\sqrt{\log n/\log\log n})$, then for every $\epsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently
large $n$ there is a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at most
$ne^{-f(n)}$ and at least $(1/8 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges; that is,
$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, ne^{-f(n)}) \geq (1/8 - o(1))n^2$. Applied with
$f(n) = \log\log n$, this disproves the headline problem, since
$ne^{-f(n)} = n/\log n = o(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 (erdos_615.variants.sudakov)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_615.variants.sudakov (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f n / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)) atTop atTop) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ n * Real.exp (-f n) → (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ ε * n ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
The complementary result of Sudakov [Su03]: if $f(n)/\sqrt{\log n} \to \infty$ then
$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, ne^{-f(n)}) = o(n^2)$; that is, for every $\epsilon > 0$ and all
sufficiently large $n$, every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at
most $ne^{-f(n)}$ has at most $\epsilon n^2$ edges.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 (erdos_615.variants.test_bot)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_615.variants.test_bot (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ≤ (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).indepNum
problems.humanStatement:
A sanity check for `erdos_615`: the empty graph on $n \geq 3$ vertices contains an independent
set on at least $n/\log n$ vertices (namely the whole vertex set), so it satisfies the
conclusion of the implication in the problem statement.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 (erdos_617)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_617 (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 3) {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (hV : Fintype.card V = r^2 + 1) (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin r) : ∃ (S : Finset V) (k : Fin r), S.card = r + 1 ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k
problems.humanStatement:
Let $r\geq 3$. If the edges of $K_{r^2+1}$ are $r$-coloured then there exist $r+1$ vertices with at
least one colour missing on the edges of the induced $K_{r+1}$.

In other words, there is no balanced colouring.

A conjecture of Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 (erdos_617.variants.r_eq_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_617.variants.r_eq_3 (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 3) {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (hV : Fintype.card V = 3^2 + 1) (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin 3) : ∃ (S : Finset V) (k : Fin 3), S.card = 3 + 1 ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] proved the conjecture for $r=3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 (erdos_617.variants.r_eq_4)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_617.variants.r_eq_4 (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 3) {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (hV : Fintype.card V = 4^2 + 1) (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin 4) : ∃ (S : Finset V) (k : Fin 4), S.card = 4 + 1 ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] proved the conjecture for $r=4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 (erdos_617.variants.r2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_617.variants.r2 : {r : ℕ | ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V), Fintype.card V = r^2 ∧ ∃ (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin r), ∀ (S : Finset V), S.card = r + 1 → ∀ (k : Fin r), ∃ u ∈ S, ∃ v ∈ S, u ≠ v ∧ coloring s(u, v) = k}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] showed this property fails for infinitely many $r$ if we replace $r^2+1$
by $r^2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.test.minNewEdges_eq_zero)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.test.minNewEdges_eq_zero {V : Type*} {r : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) (hdiam : G.ediam ≤ r) : minNewEdges r G = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.test.minNewEdges_singleton)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.test.minNewEdges_singleton : minNewEdges 4 (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 1)) = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.variants.add_edges_diam_three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.variants.add_edges_diam_three {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) : ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, G ≤ H ∧ H.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.ediam ≤ 3
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: every connected triangle-free graph on a finite
vertex set can be extended, by adding edges, to a triangle-free graph of diameter at
most $3$. This shows that the infimum defining `minNewEdges r G` ranges over a nonempty
set for every `3 ≤ r`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.variants.h_five_le)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.variants.h_five_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) : (minNewEdges 5 G : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V - 1) / 2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: $h_5(G) \leq \frac{n-1}{2}$ for every connected
triangle-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.variants.h_three_le)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.variants.h_three_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) : minNewEdges 3 G ≤ Fintype.card V
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: $h_3(G) \leq n$ for every connected triangle-free
graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 (erdos_619.variants.h_three_lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_619.variants.h_three_lower : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (G : SimpleGraph V), Fintype.card V = n ∧ G.Connected ∧ G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ (n : ℝ) - c ≤ minNewEdges 3 G
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that for every
$n$ there exist connected triangle-free graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with
$h_3(G) \geq n - c$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 623 (erdos_623)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_623 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type u) (hX : #X = ℵ_ ω) (f : Finset X → X), (∀ A : Finset X, f A ∉ A) → (∃ Y : Set X, Set.Infinite Y ∧ (∀ (B : Finset X), ↑B ⊆ Y → f B ∉ Y))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $X$ be a set of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$ and $f$ be a function from the finite subsets of
$X$ to $X$ such that $f(A)\not\in A$ for all $A$. Must there exist an infinite $Y\subseteq X$
that is independent - that is, for all finite $B\subset Y$ we have $f(B)\not\in Y$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 624 (erdos_624)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_624 : atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => H n - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ)) atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $X$ be a finite set of size $n$ and $H(n)$ be such that there is a function
$f:\{A : A\subseteq X\}\to X$ so that for every $Y\subseteq X$ with $\lvert Y\rvert \geq H(n)$
we have $\left\{ f(A) : A\subseteq Y\right\}=X$.
Prove that $H(n)-\log_2 n \to \infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 628 (erdos_628)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_628 (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) (hG_chrom : G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞)) (hG_clique : G.CliqueFree k) (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≥ 2) (hb : b ≥ 2) (hab : a + b = k + 1) : ∃ (s : Set V), (G.induce s).chromaticNumber ≥ (a : ℕ∞) ∧ (G.induce sᶜ).chromaticNumber ≥ (b : ℕ∞)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $k$ containing no $K_k$. If $a,b\geq 2$ and $a+b=k+1$
then must there exist two disjoint subgraphs of $G$ with chromatic numbers $\geq a$ and $\geq b$
respectively?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 628 (erdos_628.variants.independence_number_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_628.variants.independence_number_2 (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG_indep : G.indepNum = 2) (k : ℕ) (hG_chrom : G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞)) (hG_clique : G.CliqueFree k) (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≥ 2) (hb : b ≥ 2) (hab : a + b = k + 1) : ∃ (s : Set V), (G.induce s).chromaticNumber ≥ (a : ℕ∞) ∧ (G.induce sᶜ).chromaticNumber ≥ (b : ℕ∞)
problems.humanStatement: Balogh, Kostochka, Prince, and Stiebitz [BKPS09] proved the conjecture for graphs with independence number 2.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 628 (erdos_628.variants.k_5_a_3_b_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_628.variants.k_5_a_3_b_3 (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG_chrom : G.chromaticNumber = (5 : ℕ∞)) (hG_clique : G.CliqueFree 5) : ∃ (s : Set V), (G.induce s).chromaticNumber ≥ (3 : ℕ∞) ∧ (G.induce sᶜ).chromaticNumber ≥ (3 : ℕ∞)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős [Er68b] originally asked about $a=b=3$ which was proved by Brown and Jung [BrJu69] (who in fact prove that $G$ must contain two vertex disjoint odd cycles)..

problems.title: Erdős Problem 628 (erdos_628.variants.quasi_line)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_628.variants.quasi_line (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG_quasi : IsQuasiLineGraph G) (k : ℕ) (hG_chrom : G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞)) (hG_clique : G.CliqueFree k) (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≥ 2) (hb : b ≥ 2) (hab : a + b = k + 1) : ∃ (s : Set V), (G.induce s).chromaticNumber ≥ (a : ℕ∞) ∧ (G.induce sᶜ).chromaticNumber ≥ (b : ℕ∞)
problems.humanStatement: Balogh, Kostochka, Prince, and Stiebitz [BKPS09] proved the conjecture for quasi-line graphs.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 633 (erdos_633)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_633 : T ∈ (answer(sorry) : Set <| Triangle ℝ ℝ²) ↔ ∀ n, IsCuttable n T → IsSquare n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 64 (erdos_64)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_64 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj], G.minDegree ≥ 3 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (v : V) (c : G.Walk v v), k ≥ 2 ∧ c.IsCycle ∧ c.length = 2^k
problems.humanStatement:
Does every finite graph with minimum degree at least $3$
contain a cycle of length $2^k$ for some $k \geq 2$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 647 (erdos_647)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_647 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 24, ⨆ m : Fin n, m + σ 0 m ≤ n + 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 647 (erdos_647.variants.infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_647.variants.infinite : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, { n | ⨆ m : Set.Ioo (n - k) n, ↑m + σ 0 m ≤ n + 2 }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 647 (erdos_647.variants.lim)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_647.variants.lim : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ ⨆ m : Fin n, σ 0 m + m - n) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 647 (erdos_647.variants.twenty_four)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_647.variants.twenty_four : ⨆ m : Fin 24, (m : ℕ) + σ 0 m ≤ 26

problems.title: Erdős Problem 649 (erdos_649.variants.no_solution_two_seven)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_649.variants.no_solution_two_seven : ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, n.maxPrimeFac = 2 ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = 7
problems.humanStatement:
In fact, the answer to this question as written is easily seen to be no, since there are no
solutions to $2^k\equiv -1\pmod{7}$, and hence this fails with $p=2$ and $q=7$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 649 (erdos_649.variants.rmm_2020)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_649.variants.rmm_2020 : {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n.maxPrimeFac * (n + 1).maxPrimeFac ≠ 2 * p}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Problem 6 in the 12th Romanian Master of Mathematics Competitions in 2020 was to prove that there
exist infinitely many odd primes $p$ such that, for every $n$, $P(n)P(n+1)\neq 2p$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 649 (erdos_649.variants.sampaio)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_649.variants.sampaio : ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, n.maxPrimeFac = 19 ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = 2
problems.humanStatement:
Sampaio independently observed that the answer to Erdős' original problem is no if one of the
primes can be $2$ - for example this is false with $p=19$ and $q=2$, since if $n+1=2^k$ and
$19\mid n$ then (since $2$ is a primitive root modulo $19$) we must have $18\mid k$, and hence
$73\mid 2^{18}-1\mid n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 649 (erdos_649.variants.tong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_649.variants.tong (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : {q : ℕ | q.Prime ∧ ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Even with such amendments, this problem is false in a strong sense: Alan Tong has provided the
following elegant elementary proof that, for any given prime $p$, there are infinitely many
primes $q$ such that this statement is false: let $m$ be the product of all primes $\leq p$, and
choose a prime $q$ congruent to $-1$ modulo $4m$. If $p$ is the greatest prime divisor of $n$
then, using quadratic reciprocity, every prime divisor of $n$ is a quadratic residue modulo $q$,
and hence $n$ is a quadratic residue modulo $q$. On the other hand, since $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ we
know that $-1$ is not a quadratic residue modulo $q$, and hence $n\not\equiv -1\pmod{q}$, so it
is impossible for $q\mid n+1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 649 (erdos_649.variants.tong_question)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_649.variants.tong_question : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → Odd q → {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Tong asks whether, for any given odd prime $q$, there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that
there is no integer $n$ with $P(n)=p$ and $P(n+1)=q$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 650 (erdos_650.variants.erdos_selfridge)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_650.variants.erdos_selfridge (m : ℕ) : f (m ^ 2) ≤ 2 * m
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Selfridge proved (see [Er78] and [Er86c]) that $f(m^2)\leq 2m$, which implies
$f(m)\leq 2\lceil \sqrt{m}\rceil$ for all $m$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 650 (erdos_650.variants.erdos_suranyi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_650.variants.erdos_suranyi (m : ℕ) : Real.sqrt m ≤ (f m : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Surányi [ErSu59] proved that $f(m)\geq\sqrt{m}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 653 (erdos_653)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_653 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (1 - o n) * n ≤ maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 655 (erdos_655.variants.general_position)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_655.variants.general_position : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (X : Finset ℝ²), #X = n → IsValid X → InGeneralPosition X → (1 + c) * n / 2 ≤ distinctDistances X

problems.title: Erdős Problem 659 (erdos_659)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_659 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ A : ℕ → Finset ℝ², (∀ n, #(A n) = n ∧ ∀ S ⊆ A n, #S = 4 → 3 ≤ distinctDistances S) ∧ (fun n ↦ distinctDistances (A n)) ≪ fun n ↦ n / sqrt (log n)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every subset of $4$ points determines at
least $3$ distances, yet the total number of distinct distances is $\ll \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$?

There does exist such a set: a suitable truncation of the lattice
$\{(a,b\sqrt{2}): a,b\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ suffices. This construction appears to have been first
considered by Moree and Osburn \cite{MoOs06}, who proved that it has
 $\ll \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances. This construction was independently found by
 [Lund and Sheffer](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/2014/07/16/point-sets-with-few-distinct-distances/),
 who further noted that this configuration contains no squares or equilateral triangles.

There are only six possible configurations of $4$ points which determine only $2$ distances
(first noted by Erdős and Fishburn [ErFi96]), and five of them contain either a square or an
equilateral triangle. The remaining configuration contains four points from a regular pentagon,
and Grayzel [Gr26] (using Gemini) has noted in the comments that this configuration can also be
ruled out, thus giving a complete solution to this problem.

Boris Alexeev provides a formalisation of the reduction, which is conditional on Bernays' theorem
(assumed as an axiom in the proof to obtain the $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ bound).
See the [formal proof](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/226d5fad7143dcebea2bbb5ec87f18a3a1dcea69/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos659.lean).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 66 (erdos_66)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_66 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), c ≠ 0 ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ (sumRep A n : ℝ) / Real.log n) atTop (𝓝 c)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there and $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1_A\ast 1_A(n)}{\log n}$$
exists and is $\ne 0$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 660 (erdos_660)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_660 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ³, P.card = n → IsPolyhedronVertices P → (1 - ε) * ((n : ℝ) / 2) ≤ (distinctDistances P : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in \mathbb{R}^3$ be the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Are there at least
$$(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$$
many distinct distances between the $x_i$?

The $(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$ lower bound is formalised as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, every set
of $n$ vertices of a convex polyhedron with $n$ sufficiently large determines at least
$(1 - \varepsilon) \frac{n}{2}$ distinct distances.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 660 (erdos_660.variants.altman_planar)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_660.variants.altman_planar (n : ℕ) (P : Finset ℝ²) (hcard : P.card = n) (hconv : ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : ↥(P : Set ℝ²) → ℝ²)) (haff : affineSpan ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) = ⊤) : n / 2 ≤ distinctDistances P
problems.humanStatement:
For the similar problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there are always at least $n/2$ distances, as proved by
Altman [Al63].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 660 (erdos_660.variants.Er75f)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_660.variants.Er75f : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ³, P.card = n → IsPolyhedronVertices P → c * n ≤ (distinctDistances P : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
In [Er75f] Erdős claims that Altman proved that the vertices determine $\gg n$ many distinct
distances, but gives no reference.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 67 (erdos_67)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_67 (f : ℕ → ({-1, 1} : Finset ℝ)) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) : ∃ᵉ (d ≥ 1) (m ≥ 1), C < |∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, (f (k * d)).1|
problems.humanStatement:
**The Erdős discrepancy problem**

If $f\colon \mathbb N \rightarrow \{-1, +1\}$ then is it true that for every $C>0$ there
exist $d, m \ge 1$ such that $$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq m}f(kd)\right\rvert > C?$$
This is true, and was proved by Tao [Ta16]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 67 (erdos_67.variants.complex)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_67.variants.complex (f : ℕ → Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) : ∃ᵉ (d ≥ 1) (m ≥ 1), C < ‖∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, (f (k * d)).1‖
problems.humanStatement:
**The Erdős discrepancy problem (complex variant)**

If $f\colon \mathbb N \rightarrow S^1 ⊆ ℂ$ then is it true that for every $C>0$ there
exist $d, m \ge 1$ such that $$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq m}f(kd)\right\rvert > C?$$
This is true, and was proved by Tao [Ta16]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 672 (erdos_672)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_672 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k) (l > 1), k ≥ 4 → Erdos672With k l
problems.humanStatement:
Can the product of an arithmetic progression of positive integers $n, n + d, ..., n + (k - 1)d$
of length ≥ 4, with $(n, d) = 1$, be a perfect power?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 672 (erdos_672.variants.euler)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_672.variants.euler : Erdos672With 4 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 672 (erdos_672.variants.oblath)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_672.variants.oblath : Erdos672With 5 2 ∧ Erdos672With 3 3 ∧ Erdos672With 3 4 ∧ Erdos672With 3 5

problems.title: Erdős Problem 677 (erdos_677)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_677 : ∀ (m n k : ℕ), k > 0 → m ≥ n + k → lcmInterval m k ≠ lcmInterval n k
problems.humanStatement:
Denote by $M(n, k)$ the least common multiple of the finite set $\{n+1, \dotsc, n+k\}$.
Is it true that for all $m \geq n + k$, we get $M(m, k) \neq M(n, k)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 68 (erdos_68)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_68 : answer(sorry) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, 1 / ((n + 2).factorial - 1 : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Is
$$\sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{n!-1}$$
irrational?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 680 (erdos_680.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_680.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in .atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0, (n + k).minFac > k^2 + 1
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that
$$
p(n+k)>k^2+1,
$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 680 (erdos_680.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_680.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ C > 0, ¬ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0, Nat.minFac (n + k) > exp ((1 + ε) * √k) + C
problems.humanStatement:
Can one prove this is false if we replace $k^2+1$ by $e^{(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{k}}+C_\epsilon$, for all
$\epsilon>0$, where $C_\epsilon>0$ is some constant?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 681 (erdos_681)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_681 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ k > 0, (n + k).Composite ∧ ∀ p, IsLPF p (n + k) → p > k ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős problem 681.**
Is it true that for all large $n$ there exists $k$
such that $n + k$ is composite and $p(n+k) > k^2$,
where $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$ ?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683 (erdos_683)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_683 : answer(sorry) ↔ (∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k < n → P n k > min (n - k + 1 : ℝ) (k ^ (1 + c)))
problems.humanStatement: There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) > \min\{n-k+1, k^{1 + c}\}$ for all $0 < k < n$.}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683 (erdos_683.variant.erdos_log)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_683.variant.erdos_log : ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > c * k * Real.log k
problems.humanStatement: Erdos [Er55d] improved this to $P(n, k) \gg k \log k $ for $k \le n/2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683 (erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt : ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt k)
problems.humanStatement: Standard heuristics suggest that $P(n, k) > e^{c\sqrt{k}}$ for some constant $c > 0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683 (erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur : ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > k
problems.humanStatement: Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that $P(n, k) > k$ for $k \le n/2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can every integer $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.four)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.four : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can $4$ be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.four_three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.four_three : ¬ ∃ᵉ (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + 3), (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 3, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 3, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
The number $4$ cannot be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 3}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 3}(n+i)}$$
for $m≥n+3$!

See [comment section on erdosproblems.com](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/686#post-4599)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.four_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.four_two : ¬ ∃ᵉ (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + 2), (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2, (n + i))
