problems.humanStatement:
The number $4$ cannot be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 2}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 2}(n+i)}$$
for $m≥n+2$!

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.nine)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.nine : answer(True) ↔ ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (9 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can $9$ be written as
$$9=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.non_square)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.non_square : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), (¬ IsSquare N) → ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can every non-square $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.square)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.square : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), (IsSquare N) → ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can every square $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686 (erdos_686.variants.twenty_five)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_686.variants.twenty_five : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k), (25 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))
problems.humanStatement:
Can $25$ be written as
$$25=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 688 (erdos_688.parts.i.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_688.parts.i.lower_bound : (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] epsilonFunction
problems.humanStatement: Estimate $\epsilon_n$ - lower bound.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 688 (erdos_688.parts.i.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_688.parts.i.upper_bound : epsilonFunction =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Estimate $\epsilon_n$ - upper bound.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 688 (erdos_688.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_688.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ epsilonFunction =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (1 : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: In particular, is it true that $\epsilon_n = o(1)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 688 (erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o : (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (log (log (log (n : ℝ)))) / (log (log (n : ℝ)))) =O[atTop] epsilonFunction
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős claims in [Er80] (p. 106) that it is not difficult to prove
$\epsilon_n \gg \frac{\log\log\log n}{\log\log n}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 689 (erdos_689)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_689 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 2 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 n |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card
problems.humanStatement:
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 69 (erdos_69)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_69 : Irrational <| ∑' n, ω (n + 2) / 2 ^ (n + 2)
problems.humanStatement:
Is
$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? (Here $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 69 (erdos_69.variants.specialisation_of_erdos_257)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_69.variants.specialisation_of_erdos_257 : let A
problems.humanStatement:
Tao observed that `erdos_69` is a special case of `erdos_257`, since
$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n} = \sum_p \frac{1}{2^p - 1}.
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692 (erdos_692.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_692.parts.ii (n : ℕ) : ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) → IsGreatest (δ n '' Set.Ioi (n + 1)) (δ n answer(sorry))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\delta_1(n,m)$ be the density of the set of integers with exactly one divisor in $(n,m)$.
For fixed $n$, where does $\delta_1(n,m)$ achieve its maximum?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692 (erdos_692.variants.cambie_local_maxima)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_692.variants.cambie_local_maxima (k : ℕ) : ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ({m : ℕ | n + 1 < m ∧ δ n (m - 1) ≤ δ n m ∧ δ n (m + 1) ≤ δ n m}.ncard : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie [Ca25] has shown that, for fixed $n$, the sequence $\delta_1(n,m)$ has superpolynomially
many local maxima $m$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692 (erdos_692.variants.cambie_three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_692.variants.cambie_three : ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) → δ 3 7 < δ 3 6 ∧ δ 3 7 < δ 3 8
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie has calculated that unimodularity fails even for $n=2$ and $n=3$. For example,
$$\delta_1(3,6)= 0.35\quad \delta_1(3,7)\approx 0.33\quad \delta_1(3,8)\approx 0.3619.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692 (erdos_692.variants.erdos_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_692.variants.erdos_upper_bound : ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m, δ n m ≤ C / Real.log n ^ c
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved that
$$\delta_1(n,m) \ll \frac{1}{(\log n)^c}$$
for all $m$, for some constant $c>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 694 (erdos_694)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_694 : ∀ᵉ (fmax : ℕ → ℕ) (fmin : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, IsGreatest (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmax n)) → (∀ n, IsLeast (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmin n)) → ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ x : ℕ, sSup { (fmax n : ℝ) / fmin n | (n : ℕ) (_ : n ≤ x) (_ : ∃ m, Nat.totient m = n) } = (exp eulerMascheroniConstant + o x) * log (log (x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f_\max(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that $\phi(m) = n$, and
$f_\min(n)$ be the smallest such $m$, where $\phi$ is Euler's
totient function. Investigate
$$
  \max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)}.
$$

GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has proved (see also the comments for a summary) that
$$
\max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_{\max}(n)}{f_{\min}(n)}=(e^\gamma+o(1))\log\log x.
$$

A Lean formalisation of the reduction exists, conditional on Mertens' product theorem and
Linnik's theorem; see the
[formal proof](https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P694/Proof.lean).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 694 (erdos_694.variants.carmichael)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_694.variants.carmichael : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 0, ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n
problems.humanStatement:
Carmichael has asked whether there is an integer $n$ for which $\phi(m) = n$ has
exactly one solution, that is $\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)} = 1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 694 (erdos_694.variants.inf_unique)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_694.variants.inf_unique (h : ∃ n > 0, ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n) : { n | ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős has proved that if there exists an integer $n$ for which $\phi(m) = n$ has
exactly one solution, then there must be infinitely many such $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 695 (erdos_695)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_695 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {q : ℕ → ℕ}, StrictMono q → (∀ i, (q i).Prime) → (∀ i, q (i + 1) % q i = 1) → Tendsto (fun k => (q k : ℝ) ^ (1 / k : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of primes such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$. Is it
true that
$$
\lim_{k \to \infty} q_k^{1/k} = \infty?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 695 (erdos_695.variants.upperBound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_695.variants.upperBound : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono q ∧ (∀ i, (q i).Prime) ∧ (∀ i, q (i + 1) % q i = 1) ∧ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, (o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ -- We use `(k + 1)` here as the informal statement is 1-indexed. ∀ k, q k ≤ exp ((k + 1) * log (k + 1) ^ (1 + o k))
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a sequence of primes $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$ and
$$
q(k) \leq \exp(k (\log k)^{1 + o(1)})?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697 (erdos_697.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_697.parts.i {α : ℝ} (hα : 1 / log (2 : ℝ) < α) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697 (erdos_697.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_697.parts.ii {α : ℝ} (hα : α < 1 / log (2 : ℝ)) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697 (erdos_697.variants.delta_lt)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_697.variants.delta_lt (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : δ m α < (m ^ α + 1) / m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 698 (erdos_698)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_698 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ h : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto h atTop atTop ∧ ∀ n i j : ℕ, 2 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → h n ≤ Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some $h(n)\to \infty$ such that for all $2\leq i<j\leq n/2$
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \geq h(n)?$$

This was resolved by Bergman [Be11], who proved that for any $2\leq i<j\leq n/2$
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \gg n^{1/2}\frac{2^i}{i^{3/2}},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 698 (erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres (n i j : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i < j) (hj : j ≤ n / 2) : (n.choose i : ℝ) / (j.choose i : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j) : ℝ) ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ i ≤ (n.choose i : ℝ) / (j.choose i : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
A problem of Erdős and Szekeres, who observed that
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \geq \frac{\binom{n}{i}}{\binom{j}{i}}
\geq 2^i$$
(in particular the greatest common divisor is always $>1$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 698 (erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres_sharp)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres_sharp (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : 2 < p) : (Nat.gcd ((2 * p).choose 1) ((2 * p).choose p) : ℝ) = ((2 * p).choose 1 : ℝ) / (p.choose 1 : ℝ) ∧ ((2 * p).choose 1 : ℝ) / (p.choose 1 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ 1
problems.humanStatement: This inequality is sharp for $i=1$, $j=p$, and $n=2p$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 699 (erdos_699)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_699 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j)
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 699.** Is it true that for every $1 \le i < j \le n / 2$ there exists a prime
$p \ge i$ with $p \mid \gcd\big(\binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j}\big)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 7 (erdos_7)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_7 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i, ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤
problems.humanStatement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 70 (erdos_70)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_70 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (β : Ordinal.{0}) (n : ℕ) (_ : β.card ≤ ℵ₀) (_ : 2 ≤ n), OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 (𝔠).ord β n
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 70**: Let $\mathfrak{c}$ be the cardinality of the continuum,
let $\beta$ be a countable ordinal, and let $2 \le n < \omega$.
Is it true that $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$?

Note: The cases $n \le 3$ are trivially true (see `omega_three`), so the
genuine content of the conjecture begins at $n = 4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 (erdos_700.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_700.parts.i (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ n.Prime) (hn1 : 1 < n) : f n = n / P n ↔ answer(sorry)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 (erdos_700.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_700.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ (f n) ^ 2 > n}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 (erdos_700.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_700.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ (∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ n.Prime → 1 < n → (f n : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) / (Real.log n) ^ A)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 (erdos_700.variants.prime_mul)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_700.variants.prime_mul (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) : f (p * q) = p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 (erdos_700.variants.prime_pow)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_700.variants.prime_pow (p a : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (ha : 2 ≤ a) : f (p ^ a) = p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 701 (erdos_701)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_701 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {X : Type} [Nonempty X] [Fintype X], ∀ (F : Set (Set X)), IsLowerSet F → ∃ x : X, ∀ᵉ (F' ⊆ F), F'.Intersecting → (#F' ≤ #{ A : Set X | A ∈ F ∧ x ∈ A })
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of sets closed under taking subsets (i.e. if
$B\subseteq A\in\mathcal{F}$ then $B\in \mathcal{F}$). There exists some element $x$ such that
whenever $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an intersecting subfamily we have
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}'\rvert \leq \lvert \{ A\in \mathcal{F} : x\in A\}\rvert.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 705 (erdos_705)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_705: answer(False) ↔ ∃ k, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite → (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).girth ≥ k → (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).chromaticNumber ≤ 3
problems.humanStatement:
Let $G$ be a finite unit distance graph in $\mamthbb{R}^2$.
Is there some $k$ such that if $G$ has girth $≥ k$, then $\chi(G) ≤ 3$?

The general case was solved by O'Donnell [OD99], who constructed finite unit distance graphs with
chromatic number $4$ and arbitrarily large girth.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.counterexample_hall)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_hall (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 3, 9, 10, 13}) : Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧ ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n
problems.humanStatement:
This conjecture was actually first disproved by Hall in 1947 [Ha47], long before Erdős asked
this question.
A counterexample for any modulus from from [Ha47] in the paragraph following Theorem 4.3, where it
was given as $\{-8, -6, 0, 1, 4\}$, but this can be shifted to natural numbers
as pointed out in [arxiv/2510.19804].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.counterexample_mian_chowla)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_mian_chowla (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 2, 4, 8, 13}) : Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧ ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n
problems.humanStatement:
Alexeev and Mixon [arxiv/2510.19804] have disproved this conjecture,
showing that $\{1, 2, 4, 8, 13\}$ cannot be extended to any perfect difference set.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.counterexample_prime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_prime (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 2, 4, 8}) : Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧ ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), Prime p → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p ^ 2 + p + 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Alexeev and Mixon [arxiv/2510.19804] have disproved this conjecture, proving that $\{1,2,4,8\}$
cannot be extended to a perfect difference set modulo $p^2+p+1$
for any prime $p$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.example_embedding)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.example_embedding : ∃ (B : Set ℕ), {1, 2, 4} ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B 7
problems.humanStatement: The set `{1, 2, 4}` can be embedded in a perfect difference set modulo 7.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.example_sidon_set)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.example_sidon_set : IsSidon ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ)
problems.humanStatement: The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a Sidon set.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.perfect_difference_set_size_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.perfect_difference_set_size_bound (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hB : IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n) : B.ncard ≤ n.sqrt + 1
problems.humanStatement: A perfect difference set modulo `n` must have size `≤ √n + 1`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.prime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.prime : (∀ (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.Finite), IsSidon A → ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ A ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)) ↔ False
problems.humanStatement:
It is false that any finite Sidon set can be embedded in a perfect
difference set modulo `p^2 + p + 1` for some prime `p`.

As described in [arxiv/2510.19804], a counterexample is provided in [Ha47], see below.
The proof of this has been formalized.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.prime_power)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.prime_power : (∀ (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.Finite), IsSidon A → ∃ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), IsPrimePow p ∧ A ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)) ↔ False

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.singer_construction)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.singer_construction (p : ℕ) (hp : IsPrimePow p) : ∃ (B : Set ℕ), IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1) ∧ B.ncard = p + 1
problems.humanStatement:
The Singer construction gives perfect difference sets for `n = p^2 + p + 1` where `p` is a
prime power.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets (erdos_707.variants.small_sidon_sets)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_707.variants.small_sidon_sets (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Finite) (h : A.ncard ≤ 3) (hSidon : IsSidon A) : ∃ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), IsPrimePow p ∧ A ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)
problems.humanStatement: For small Sidon sets, we can check the conjecture directly.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture. (erdos_723)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_723 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {P L : Type} (_: Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L), ∀ pp : ProjectivePlane P L, IsPrimePow pp.order
problems.humanStatement: If there is a finite projective plane of order $n$ then must $n$ be a prime power?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture. (erdos_723.variants.bruck_ryser)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_723.variants.bruck_ryser {P L : Type} [Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L] (n : ℕ) (pp : ProjectivePlane P L) (hpp : pp.order = n) : (n ≡ 1 [MOD 4] ∨ n ≡ 2 [MOD 4]) → ∃ a b, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Bruck and Ryser have proved that if $n \equiv 1 (\mod 4)$ or $n \equiv 2 (\mod 4)$ then $n$ must be
the sum of two squares.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture. (erdos_723.variants.eq_12)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_723.variants.eq_12 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L) (pp : ProjectivePlane P L), pp.order = 12
problems.humanStatement: It is open whether there exists a projective plane of order 12.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture. (erdos_723.variants.leq_11)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_723.variants.leq_11 {P L : Type} [Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L] : ∀ pp : ProjectivePlane P L, pp.order ≤ 11 → IsPrimePow pp.order
problems.humanStatement: This conjecture has been proved for $n \leq 11$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture. (erdos_723.variants.prime_power_is_projplane_order)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_723.variants.prime_power_is_projplane_order : ∀ n, IsPrimePow n → ∃ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L) (pp : ProjectivePlane P L), pp.order = n
problems.humanStatement: These always exist if $n$ is a prime power.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 726 (erdos_726)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_726 : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < (n % p : ℝ)), (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2)
problems.humanStatement:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 726 (erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate : (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter (fun p ↦ p.Prime), (1 : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement: The classical estimate of Mertens states that $\sum_{p\leq n}\frac{1}{p}\sim \log\log n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 (erdos_727)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_727 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (Nat.factorial (n + k)) ^ 2 ∣ Nat.factorial (2 * n)}
problems.humanStatement: Let $k ≥ 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 (erdos_727.variants.k_1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_727.variants.k_1 : letI k
problems.humanStatement:
Balakran proved this holds for $k = 1$.

Let $k = 1$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ for infinitely many $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 (erdos_727.variants.k_1_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_727.variants.k_1_2 (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (Nat.factorial (n + k)) * (Nat.factorial (n + 1)) ∣ Nat.factorial (2 * n)}
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus observe that the method of Balakran can be further used to prove
that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $(n+k)!(n+1)!∣(2n)!$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 (erdos_727.variants.k_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_727.variants.k_2 : letI k
problems.humanStatement:
It is open even for $k = 2$.
Let $k = 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many n?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 730 (erdos_730)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_730 : answer(sorry) ↔ S.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n < m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$
and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 730 (erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one : ∃ (n m : ℕ), (n, m) ∈ S ∧ m ≠ n + 1
problems.humanStatement:
There are examples where $(n, m) ∈ S$ with $m ≠ n + 1$.

(Found by AlphaProof, although it was implicit already in [A129515])

problems.title: Erdős Problem 730 (erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs : {(87, 88), (607, 608)} ⊆ S
problems.humanStatement: For example, $(87,88)$ and $(607,608)$ are such pairs.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 74 (erdos_74)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_74 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop → (∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ f n)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ possibly very slowly.
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $f(n)$ edges?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 74 (erdos_74.variants.sqrt)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_74.variants.sqrt : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ (n : ℝ).sqrt
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $\sqrt{n}$ edges?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 740: Infinitary version of chromatic number and odd cycles (erdos_740)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_740 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), ℵ₀ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal → ∀ (r : ℕ), ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = G.chromaticCardinal ∧ NoShortOddCycle H.coe r
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal and $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$.
Let $r\geq 1$. Must $G$ contain a subgraph of chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$ which does not contain
any odd cycle of length $\leq r$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 741 (erdos_741.variants.lower)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_741.variants.lower : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < lowerDensity (A + A) → ∃ A₁ A₂, A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ 0 < lowerDensity (A₁ + A₁) ∧ 0 < lowerDensity (A₂ + A₂)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive lower density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive lower density?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 742 (erdos_742)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_742 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], IsDiameter2Critical G → G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Fintype.card V) ^ 2 / 4
problems.humanStatement:
**Murty-Simon Conjecture**

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with diameter $2$ such that deleting any edge increases the
diameter. Is it true that $G$ has at most $\lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor$ edges? Equality is conjectured
to hold for the complete balanced bipartite graph $K_{\lceil n/2 \rceil, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

The conjecture is resolved up to a finite check: Fan [Fa87] verified it for $n \leq 24$ and
$n = 26$, and Füredi [Fü92] proved it for all sufficiently large $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 749 (erdos_749)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_749 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ A : Set ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ lowerDensity (A + A) ∧ ((Nat.cast (R
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 75 (erdos_75)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_75 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ #V = ℵ_ 1 ∧ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (H : G.Subgraph), H.verts.ncard = n → ∃ (I : Finset V), (I : Set V) ⊆ H.verts ∧ G.IsIndepSet (I : Set V) ∧ (I.card : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a graph of chromatic number `ℵ_ 1` with `ℵ_ 1` vertices such that for all
`ε > 0`, if `n` is sufficiently large and `H` is a subgraph on `n` vertices,
then `H` contains an independent set of size `> n ^ (1 - ε)`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 750 (erdos_750.variants.c_gt_quarter)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_750.variants.c_gt_quarter : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (c : ℝ≥0), c > 1 / 4 → ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set V), 0 < m → S.ncard = m → ∃ I ⊆ S, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ m / 2 - c * m ≤ I.ncard
problems.humanStatement: In [ErHa67b] Erdős and Hajnal prove this for $f(m)\geq cm$ for all $c>1/4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 750 (erdos_750.variants.epsilon)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_750.variants.epsilon : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ≥0), ε > 0 → ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set V), 0 < m → S.ncard = m → ∃ I ⊆ S, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ m / 2 - ε * m ≤ I.ncard
problems.humanStatement:
In [Er69b] Erdős conjectures this for $f(m)=\epsilon m$ for any fixed $\epsilon>0$. This follows
from a result of Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi [EHS82], as described by Sellke in the comments.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 750 (erdos_750.variants.stiebitz)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_750.variants.stiebitz {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) (h : IsRecursivelyBuiltMr r G) : (r : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber
problems.humanStatement:
**Stiebitz's theorem** [St85]: every graph in $M_r$ has chromatic number at least $r$. The
matching upper bound follows from the construction, so the chromatic number is exactly $r$.

This is stated ahead of `erdos_750` because the formal proof linked there assumes it, and the
`assuming` clause must name a declaration that already exists. See also [SaSt89] and [MuSt19].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751 (erdos_751.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_751.parts.i : answer(False) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 4 ∧ ∀ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∀ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' → m + k ≤ m'
problems.humanStatement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=4$. If $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ are the lengths of the
cycles in $G$ then can $\min(m_{i+1}-m_i)$ be arbitrarily large?

The answer is no: Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$
has two cycles whose lengths differ by at most $2$, and hence the same is true for every graph with
chromatic number $4$.

`erdos_751.variants.finite` below carries the Lean proof. It assumes a finite vertex type,
where this quantifies over any `V : Type`, and the two are joined by de Bruijn-Erdős: a graph
that is not $3$-colourable has a finite subgraph that is not $3$-colourable, and cycles of that
subgraph are cycles of the whole. Mathlib does not have de Bruijn-Erdős, so that step is not
formalised here.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751 (erdos_751.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_751.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ k g : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 4 ∧ g ≤ G.girth ∧ ∀ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∀ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' → m + k ≤ m'
problems.humanStatement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=4$. If $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ are the lengths of the
cycles in $G$ then can $\min(m_{i+1}-m_i)$ be arbitrarily large? Can this happen if the girth of
$G$ is large?

The answer is no: Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$
has two cycles whose lengths differ by at most $2$, and hence the same is true for every graph with
chromatic number $4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751 (erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : 3 ≤ G.minDegree) : ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∃ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' ∧ m' ≤ m + 2
problems.humanStatement:
Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$ has two cycles
whose lengths differ by at most $2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 753 (erdos_753.variants.alon)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_753.variants.alon : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), (listChromaticNumber G : ℝ) + (listChromaticNumber Gᶜ : ℝ) ≤ C * ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)
problems.humanStatement:
Alon [Al92] proved that, for every $n$, there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that
$$\chi_L(G)+\chi_L(G^c)\ll (n\log n)^{1/2},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 755 (erdos_755)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_755 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ => (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (TUnit 6 n : ℝ) ≤ ((1 / 27 : ℝ) + o n) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős asked whether every $n$-point set in
$\mathbb{R}^6$ spans at most $(1/27 + o(1)) n^3$ unit equilateral triangles.

Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger any-size statement
$T_6(n) = (1/27 + o(1)) n^3$. The unit-triangle upper bound follows as a
corollary, since unit equilateral triangles are a subset of equilateral
triangles of any positive side length: $T_\mathrm{unit} \leq T_\mathrm{anysize}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 755 (erdos_755.test_dim_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_755.test_dim_one : unitEquilateralTriangleCount 1 (∅ : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 755 (erdos_755.variants.any_size_cdl)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_755.variants.any_size_cdl : (fun n : ℕ => (TAnySize 6 n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (1 / 27 : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3)
problems.humanStatement:
Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger version where
equilateral triangles of all positive side lengths are counted.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 756 (erdos_756)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_756 : answer(True) ↔ (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (maxRichDistances n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Can there be $\gg n$ many distinct distances
each of which occurs for more than $n$ many pairs from $A$?

The answer is yes: Bhowmick [Bh24] constructs a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+1$ times.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 756 (erdos_756.variants.bhowmick_general)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_756.variants.bhowmick_general (m : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = n ∧ n / (2 * (m + 1)) ≤ (richDistances A (n + m)).card
problems.humanStatement:
More generally, they construct, for any $m$ and large $n$, a set of $n$ points such that
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2(m+1)}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+m$ times.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757 (erdos_757)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_757 {A : Set ℝ} : answer(sorry) = sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757 (erdos_757.variants.lowerBound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_757.variants.lowerBound {A : Set ℝ} : 1 / (2 : ℝ) < sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757 (erdos_757.variants.upperBound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound {A : Set ℝ} : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 760 (erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ), G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) → ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧ (c * Real.sqrt ((m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ)) ≤ (k : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 762 (erdos_762.variants.bounded_clique_number)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_762.variants.bounded_clique_number (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) : ∃ f : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree n → G.chromaticNumber ≤ G.cochromaticNumber + f
problems.humanStatement:
A conjecture of Erdős, Gimbel, and Straight [EGS90], who proved that for every $n>2$ there exists
some $f(n)$ such that if $G$ contains no clique on $n$ vertices then $\chi(G)\leq \zeta(G)+f(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 762 (erdos_762.variants.steiner)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_762.variants.steiner : ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.cliqueNum = 4 ∧ G.cochromaticNumber = 4 ∧ G.chromaticNumber = 7
problems.humanStatement:
This has been disproved by Steiner [St24b], who constructed a graph $G$ with $\omega(G)=4$,
$\zeta(G)=4$, and $\chi(G)=7$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 769 (erdos_769.variants.growth_rate)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_769.variants.growth_rate : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧ ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ)
problems.humanStatement:
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 (erdos_770.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_770.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a, HasDensity {n | h n = p} a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 (erdos_770.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_770.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ liminf h atTop = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 (erdos_770.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_770.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, let p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 (erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded : Unbounded (· ≤ ·) (ENat.toNat '' (h '' Odd))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 (erdos_770.variants.three)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_770.variants.three : {n | h n = 3}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 774 (erdos_774)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_774 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → A.IsProportionatelyDissociated → ∃ (T : Set (Set ℕ)), (∀ S ∈ T, S.IsDissociated) ∧ T.Finite ∧ A = ⋃₀ T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 775 (erdos_775.variants.gao)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_775.variants.gao : ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : ThreeUniformHypergraph (Fin n), (ThreeUniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard + f n ≤ n
problems.humanStatement:
The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 775 (erdos_775.variants.moon_moser)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_775.variants.moon_moser : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) + C
problems.humanStatement:
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes, which Moon and Moser [MoMo65] showed to be best possible.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 775 (erdos_775.variants.spencer)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_775.variants.spencer : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) - C ≤ ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 779 (erdos_779)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_779 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 1): let P

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsAdditiveComplement A B → limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) → Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement: Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.chen_fang)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) : ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement: Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold for any constant $c>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B) (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) : Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp : ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧ limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧ ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1
problems.humanStatement:
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.danzer)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer : ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B
problems.humanStatement:
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) : (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧ Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨ (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧ Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2))
problems.humanStatement:
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) : (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ) < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨ (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ) < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) : ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧ ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x
problems.humanStatement:
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 (erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) : ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786 (erdos_786.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_786.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ε ≤ 1 → ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ A.IsMulCardSet
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of density $> 1 - \epsilon$
such that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786 (erdos_786.parts.i.example)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_786.parts.i.example (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = { n | n % 4 = 2 }) : A.HasDensity (1 / 4) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet
problems.humanStatement: An example of such a set with density $\frac 1 4$ is given by the integers $\equiv 2\pmod{4}$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786 (erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / rexp 1) : ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in atTop, p.Prime → ∃ k, ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (1 : ℝ) / q < 1 ∧ 1 < ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p (k + 1), (1 : ℝ) / q ∧ letI A
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then, for a sufficiently large prime `p`, take the sequence of
consecutive primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_k$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{p_i} < 1 < \sum_{i=1}^{k + 1} \frac{1}{p_i},
$$
and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $\frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786 (erdos_786.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_786.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : ℕ → Set ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)), ∀ N, A N ⊆ Set.Icc 1 (N + 1) ∧ (1 - f N) * N ≤ (A N).ncard ∧ (A N).IsMulCardSet
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some set $A\subset\{1, ..., N\}$ of size $\geq (1 - o(1))N$ such that
$a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789 : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Estimate $h(n)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Is $h(n) = \Theta((n\log(n)))^{1/3})$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic_isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic_isBigO : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.isBigO_cube_root_linearithmic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.isBigO_cube_root_linearithmic : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.isBigO_sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.isBigO_sq : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.sq : (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ √n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Is $h(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789 (erdos_789.variants.sq_isBigO)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_789.variants.sq_isBigO : (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 794 (erdos_794.variants.balogh)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_794.variants.balogh {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (H : Finset (Finset V)) (hH : H.IsThreeUniform) (h : H.ContainsSubgraph 5 7) : H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3
problems.humanStatement:
Balogh has observed that this problem is probably misstated by Erdős - indeed, every graph with
$5$ vertices spanning $7$ edges contains a graph on $4$ vertices spanning $3$ edges, so the
second condition can be dropped.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 794 (erdos_794.variants.frankl_furedi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_794.variants.frankl_furedi (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsThreeUniform ∧ ¬ H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∧ (2 / 7 - ε) * (n.choose 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.card : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
This problem is then now asking how many edges a $3$-uniform hypergraph can have before it
contains $K_4$ minus an edge, and whether the critical edge density is $2/9$. In fact there is a
construction of Frankl and Füredi [FrFu84] showing it must be at least $2/7$, which is the
conjectured truth (although Turán conjectured before [Er69] that the edge density was $1/4$, and
so likely there is simply a typo in this problem's statement).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 794 (erdos_794.variants.harris)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_794.variants.harris : harrisHypergraph.IsThreeUniform ∧ harrisHypergraph.card = 28 ∧ ¬ harrisHypergraph.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∧ ¬ harrisHypergraph.ContainsSubgraph 5 7
problems.humanStatement:
Harris has provided the following simple counterexample to the problem as stated: the
$3$-uniform graph on $\{1,\ldots,9\}$ with $28$ edges, formed by taking $27$ edges by choosing
one element each from $\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\{7,8,9\}$, and then adding the edge $\{1,2,3\}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 798 (erdos_798.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_798.variants.lower_bound : (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 798 (erdos_798.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_798.variants.upper_bound : (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log n)
problems.humanStatement: Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 80 (erdos_80)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_80 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 → ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ ε < f c n
problems.humanStatement:
Let $c>0$ and let $f_c(n)$ be the maximal $m$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and
at least $cn^2$ edges, where each edge is contained in at least one triangle, must contain a
book of size $m$, that is, an edge shared by at least $m$ different triangles. Estimate
$f_c(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f_c(n)>n^\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$?

The bound $c < 1/2$ is what makes the hypothesis satisfiable: a simple graph on $n$ vertices
has at most $n(n-1)/2$ edges, so no graph has $cn^2$ of them once $c \geq 1/2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 80 (erdos_80.variants.log)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_80.variants.log : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 → (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f c n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log n)
problems.humanStatement:
The weaker question from the same problem: is $f_c(n) \gg \log n$?

Same feasibility bound on `c` as above.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 812 (erdos_812.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_812.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (R (n + 1) : ℝ) / (R n : ℝ) ≥ 1 + c
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $\frac{R(n+1)}{R(n)}\geq 1+c$ for some constant $c>0$, for all large $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 812 (erdos_812.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_812.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (R (n + 1) : ℝ) - (R n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $R(n+1)-R(n) \gg n^2$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 812 (erdos_812.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_812.variants.lower_bound : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → (R (n + 1) : ℤ) - (R n : ℤ) ≥ 4 * (n : ℤ) - 8
problems.humanStatement: Burr, Erdős, Faudree, and Schelp [BEFS89] proved that $R(n+1)-R(n) \geq 4n-8$ for all $n\geq 2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 817 (erdos_817)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_817 : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n => (3 ^ n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 817 (erdos_817.variants.bdd_power)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_817.variants.bdd_power : ∃ O > (0 : ℝ), (fun (n : ℕ) => (3 ^ n : ℝ) / n ^ O) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 818 (erdos_818.variants.solymosi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_818.variants.solymosi : ∀ K : ℝ, 0 < K → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ A : Finset ℤ, 2 ≤ A.card → ((A + A).card : ℝ) ≤ K * (A.card : ℝ) → c * (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 / Real.log (A.card : ℝ) ≤ ((A * A).card : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
This was proved by Solymosi [So09d], in the strong form
$$\lvert AA\rvert \gg \frac{\lvert A\rvert^2}{\log \lvert A\rvert}.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 82 (erdos_82)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_82 : Tendsto (fun n => F n / Real.log n) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement: $F(n) / \log n \to \infty as n \to \infty$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 82 (erdos_82.variants.F_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_82.variants.F_upper_bound : (fun n => (F n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => Real.sqrt n * (Real.log n) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
$F(n) \le O(n^{1/2} \ln ^ {3/4} n)$

Theorem 1.4 from [AKS07]

[AKS07] Alon, N. and Krivelevich, M. and Sudakov, B., Large nearly regular induced subgraphs. arXiv:0710.2106 (2007).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 821 (erdos_821)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_821 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (g n : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ such that
$g(n) > n^{1-\epsilon}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 821 (erdos_821.variants.erdos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_821.variants.erdos : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ c < (g n : ℝ) }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er35b] proved that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that $g(n) > n^c$ for infinitely
many $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 821 (erdos_821.variants.lichtman)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_821.variants.lichtman : ∃ c > (0.71568 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ c < (g n : ℝ) }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
The best known bound is that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $g(n) > n^{0.71568\cdots}$,
obtained by Lichtman [Li22] as a consequence of proving that there are
$\geq \frac{x}{(\log x)^{O(1)}}$ many primes $p\leq x$ such that all prime factors of $p-1$ are
$\leq x^{0.2843\cdots}$ (which improves a number of previous exponents, most recently Baker and
Harman [BaHa98]).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 821 (erdos_821.variants.pillai)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_821.variants.pillai : atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : EReal)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement: Pillai proved that $\limsup g(n)=\infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 822 (erdos_822)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_822 : answer(True) ↔ (Set.range fun n => n + Nat.totient n).HasPosDensity
problems.humanStatement:
Does the set of integers of the form $n + \varphi(n)$ have positive (lower) density?

[GIL24] proved this was true.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 825 (erdos_825)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_825 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ (C : ℝ) (_ : C > 0), ∀ (n) (_ : σ 1 n > C * n), ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by Larsen - in fact, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $L$
such that if $n$ has only prime divisors $>L$ and $\sigma(n)>(2+\epsilon)n$ then $n$ is the distinct
sum of proper divisors of $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 825 (erdos_825.variants.necessary_cond)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_825.variants.necessary_cond (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : σ 1 n > C * n), ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id) : 2 < C
problems.humanStatement:
Show that if the constant $C > 0$ is such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$, then we
must have $C > 2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 826 (erdos_826)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_826 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), { n | ∀ k ≥ 1, σ 0 (n + k) ≤ C * k }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 828 (erdos_828)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_828 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℤ, Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | ↑(φ n) ∣ n + a}
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 828 (erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, φ n ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n
problems.humanStatement: When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 829 (erdos_829)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_829 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, (fun n : ℕ => (sumRep cubes n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (Real.log n) ^ C)
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős Problem 829 (open).**  Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the set of perfect cubes.  Is
it true that $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \ll (\log n)^{O(1)}$?  That is, does there exist a natural
number $C$ such that the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
$O((\log n)^C)$ as $n \to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 (erdos_830.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_830.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ {(a, b) | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 (erdos_830.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_830.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in atTop, x ^ (1 - o x) < A x
problems.humanStatement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 (erdos_830.variants.erdos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_830.variants.erdos : A =o[atTop] id
problems.humanStatement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that $A(x) = o(x)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 (erdos_830.variants.pomerance)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- Real.nthRoot 3 x.log)
problems.humanStatement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 (erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger : ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- (1/ 2 + o x) * √(x.log * x.log.log))
problems.humanStatement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 835 (erdos_835)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_835 : (∃ k > 2, Property k) ↔ answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 835 (erdos_835.variants.johnson)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_835.variants.johnson : (∃ l, -- making sure k > 2 letI k
problems.humanStatement:
Alternative statement of Erdős Problem 835 using the chromatic number of the Johnson graph.
This is equivalent to asking whether there exists $k > 2$ such that the chromatic number of the
Johnson graph $J(2k, k)$ is $k+1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 847 (erdos_847)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_847 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Infinite A → HasFew3APs A → ∃ n, ∃ (S : Fin n → Set ℕ), (∀ i, ThreeAPFree (S i)) ∧ A = ⋃ i : Fin n, S i
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon > 0$ such that
in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no
three-term arithmetic progression.

Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic
progression?

A negative answer was given by Reiher, Rödl, and Sales [RRS24], who proved that, for any
$0<\mu<1/2$, there exists $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every finite colouring of $A$ contains
a three-term arithmetic progression, and yet every subset of $A$ of size $n$ contains a subset of
size $\geq \mu n$ without a three-term arithmetic progression.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 848 (erdos_848)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_848 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N, Erdos848For N
problems.humanStatement:
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 849 (erdos_849)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_849 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ t ≥ 1, ∃ a : ℕ, {n : ℕ | ∃ k ≥ 1, 2 * k ≤ n ∧ choose n k = a}.ncard = t
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$
with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 85 (erdos_85)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_85 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, f n ≤ f (n + 1)
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that, for all large $n$, $f(n + 1) \ge f(n)$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 850 (erdos_850)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_850 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ x y : ℕ, x ≠ y ∧ x.primeFactors = y.primeFactors ∧ (x + 1).primeFactors = (y + 1).primeFactors ∧ (x + 2).primeFactors = (y + 2).primeFactors
problems.humanStatement:
Can there exist two distinct integers $x$ and $y$ such that $x,y$ have the same prime factors,
$x+1,y+1$ have the same prime factors, and $x+2,y+2$ also have the same prime factors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 851 (erdos_851)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r d, (TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 851 (erdos_851.variants.romanoff)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet
problems.humanStatement: The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 853 (erdos_853.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_853.parts.i : atTop.Tendsto r atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) \to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 853 (erdos_853.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_853.parts.ii : atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ r n / Real.log n) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 855 (erdos_855)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_855 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∀ᶠ y in atTop, π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for sufficiently large $x, y$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 857 (erdos_857)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_857 : let f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
problems.humanStatement: Estimate `m(n,k)`, or better give an asymptotic formula.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 859 (erdos_859)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_859 : ∃ c₁ > 0, ∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), ∃ d : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ t > 0, (DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity (d t)) ∧ (fun (t : ℕ) ↦ d t) ~[atTop] (fun t ↦ c₁ / Real.log t ^ c₂)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 859 (erdos_859.variants.erdos_upper_lower_bounds)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_859.variants.erdos_upper_lower_bounds : ∃ᵉ (c₃ > (0 : ℝ)) (c₄ > (0 : ℝ)) (t₀ : ℕ), ∀ᶠ t in atTop, ∃ dₜ : ℝ, (DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity dₜ ∧ 1 / Real.log t ^ c₃ < dₜ ∧ dₜ < 1 / Real.log t ^ c₄
problems.humanStatement:
The density `dₜ` of `DivisorSumSet (t : ℕ)` is bounded from below by `1 / log (t) ^ c₃` and
from above by `1 / log (t) ^ c₄` for some positive constants `c₃` and `c₄`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 859 (erdos_859.variants.positive_density)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_859.variants.positive_density (t : ℕ) : (DivisorSumSet t).HasPosDensity
problems.humanStatement:
An easy sanity check is to prove that for every natural number `t` the density `dₜ` is
a positive number.
Hint: investigate some multiplicative structure of `DivisorSumSet t`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 859 (erdos_859.variants.trivial_case)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos_859.variants.trivial_case : DivisorSumSet 0 = Set.univ
problems.humanStatement: A case where we can easily calculate the density of `DivisorSumSet t` is that of `t=0`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 862 (erdos_862.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 865 (erdos_865.variants.k2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_865.variants.k2 (N : ℕ) : ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 (2 * N), A.card ≥ N + 2 → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a + b ∈ A
problems.humanStatement:
It is a classical folklore fact that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ has size $\geq N+2$ then
there are distinct $a,b\in A$ such that $a+b\in A$, which establishes the $k=2$ case.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 865 (erdos_865.variants.sos)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_865.variants.sos : ∀ᵉ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k), (fun N ↦ (f N k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun N ↦ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (1 + ∑ r ∈ Icc 1 (k - 2), (1 / 4 : ℝ) ^ r) * N)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Sós conjectured that
$f_k(N)\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\sum_{1\leq r\leq k-2}\frac{1}{4^r}\right) N$,
where $f_k(N)$ is the minimal size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ guaranteeing $k$ elements
have all pairwise sums in the set.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 865 (erdos_865.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_865.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (f N k : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - ε) * N
problems.humanStatement:
Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75] have proved that, for all $k\geq 3$, there exists $\epsilon_k>0$
such that (for large enough $N$) $f_k(N)\leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\epsilon_k\right)N$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 (erdos_867.variants.adenwalla)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_867.variants.adenwalla (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 + ε) * (N : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Adenwalla has observed that
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq (\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1))N.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 (erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧ ((13 / 24 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 (erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - 1 / 512) * (N : ℝ) + Real.log (N : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 (erdos_867.variants.freud)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_867.variants.freud : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧ (((19 / 36 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 (erdos_867.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_867.variants.lower_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧ ((N : ℝ) / 2 - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: Taking $A=(N/2,N]\cap \mathbb{N}$ shows $\lvert A\rvert \geq N/2-O(1)$ is possible.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 (erdos_868.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_868.parts.i : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 → atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ncard_add_repr A 2 n) atTop → ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2
problems.humanStatement:
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 (erdos_868.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_868.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (ε > 0), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 → (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ε * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2
problems.humanStatement:
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 (erdos_868.variants.fixed_)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 → (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹ * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 (erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson (o : ℕ) (ho : 1 < o) : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o ∧ ∀ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o → ∃ b ∈ B, (B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o

problems.title: Erdős Problem 872 (erdos_872.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_872.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (L n : ℝ) ≥ ε * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 872 (erdos_872.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_872.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (L n : ℝ) ≥ (1 - ε) * n / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 872 (erdos_872.trivial_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_872.trivial_upper_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : L n ≤ n - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 872 (erdos_872.variants.prime_question)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_872.variants.prime_question : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, Maximal (IsPrimitive n) A → ((Finset.Icc 2 n).filter Nat.Prime).card ≤ A.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 873 (erdos_873)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_873 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ε > (0 : ℝ)), 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a → ∃ k, ∀ X > 0, F a X k < (X^ε).toEReal

problems.title: Erdős Problem 881 (erdos_881)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_881 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ), IsMinimalAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder k A → ∃ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ A ∧ B.Infinite ∧ (A \ B).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (k + 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Let `A ⊂ ℕ` be an additive basis of order `k` which is minimal in the sense that
if `B ⊂ A` is any infinite set, then `A \ B` is not a basis of order `k`.

Must there exist an infinite `B ⊂ A` such that `A \ B`
is an additive basis of order `k + 1`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 884 (erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood : ∀ (k : ℕ) (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m → ¬Erdos884Prop
problems.humanStatement:
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdos conjecture 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *Qualitative Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture*.
See [here](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).
The *qualitative* version of the conjecture only states that there are infinitely many tuples
of primes and does not require any asymptotical bounds and as such is a corollary of the general
form of the Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture.
We state the 'weaker' implication using general Hardy-Littlewood here, since this conjecture is
already formalized.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 885 (erdos_885)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_885 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = k ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 885 (erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2 : ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 2 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 2
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved this is true for $k=2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 885 (erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3 : ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 3 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 3
problems.humanStatement: Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 885 (erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4 : ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 4 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 4
problems.humanStatement: Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 886 (erdos_886)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_886 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (Erdos886Divisors n ε 1).card ≤ K
problems.humanStatement:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Is it true that, for all large $n$, the number of divisors of $n$ in
$(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ is $O_\epsilon(1)$?

Erdős attributes this conjecture to Ruzsa.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 886 (erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_bound : ∀ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ((divisors n).filter (fun (d : ℕ) => (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) ∧ (d : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) + C * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ))).card ≤ 1 + C ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that, for any constant $C>0$, all large $n$ have at most
$1+C^2$ many divisors in $[n^{1/2}, n^{1/2}+Cn^{1/4}]$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 886 (erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_infinite : Set.Infinite {n | 4 ≤ (Erdos886Divisors n (1/4) 16).card}
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that there are infinitely many $n$ such that there are
four divisors of $n$ in $(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+16n^{1/4})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 887 (erdos_887.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_887.parts.i : ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n } ≤ answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 887 (erdos_887.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_887.parts.ii : ∃ K, ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n } ≤ K
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 887 (erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_4)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_4 : IsGreatest {K | ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), Infinite {n : ℕ | K ≤ #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n }}} 4
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Rosenfeld, ask whether $4$ is the best possible $K$ for the infinitude of $n$
with (at least) $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 887 (erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_infinite : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), Infinite {n : ℕ | 4 ≤ #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n }}
problems.humanStatement:
A question of Erdős and Rosenfeld, who proved that there are infinitely many $n$ with (at least)
$4$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + cn^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 888 (erdos_888)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_888 : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n)
problems.humanStatement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that if
$a\leq b\leq c\leq d\in A$ are such that $abcd$ is a square then $ad=bc$?

This was proved by GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Chojecki).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 888 (erdos_888.variants.primes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_888.variants.primes : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) / Real.log n)
problems.humanStatement: The primes show that $\lvert A\rvert \gg n/\log n$ is possible.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 888 (erdos_888.variants.sarkozy)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_888.variants.sarkozy : (fun n ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős claims that Sárközy proved that $\lvert A\rvert =o(n)$ (a proof of this
bound is provided by Tao in the comments).
