problems.title: Erdős Problem 888 (erdos_888.variants.semiprimes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_888.variants.semiprimes : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n)
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie and Weisenberg have noted in the comments that the set of semiprimes
also works, showing $(1+o(1))\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n \leq \lvert A\rvert$ is achievable.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889 (erdos_889)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_889 : Tendsto v₀ atTop (𝓝 ⊤)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $v(n,k)$ count the prime factors of $n+k$ which
do not divide $n+i$ for $0\leq i < k$. Is it true that
$v_0(n)=\max_{k\geq 0}v(n,k)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889 (erdos_889.variants.general)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_889.variants.general : ∀ l, Tendsto (v_l l) atTop (𝓝 ⊤)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $v_l(n) = \max_{k\geq l} v(n,k)$. For every fixed $l$,
$v_l(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889 (erdos_889.variants.v0_gt_1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_889.variants.v0_gt_1 : ∀ n : ℕ, n ∉ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16} : Finset ℕ) → 1 < v₀ n
problems.humanStatement:
$v_0(n) > 1$ for all $n$ except $n$ = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889 (erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | v_l 1 n = 1}.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Does $v_1(n) = 1$ have finite solutions?

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889 (erdos_889.variants.V1_eq_1_finite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_889.variants.V1_eq_1_finite : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | V_l 1 n = 1}.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Does $V_1(n) = 1$ have finite solutions?

This is a modification of `erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite`,
which might make it more amenable to attack according to [ErSe67].

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 89 (erdos_89)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_89 : (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log.sqrt) =O[atTop] (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er46] asked whether every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$
determines $\gg \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 89 (erdos_89.variants.grid_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_89.variants.grid_upper_bound : (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log.sqrt)
problems.humanStatement:
The square grid construction, going back to Erdős and Moser, shows that
$\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ is the correct order if the conjecture is true:
there are configurations whose number of distinct distances is
$O(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 89 (erdos_89.variants.implies_n_dvd_log_n)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_89.variants.implies_n_dvd_log_n (h : type_of% erdos_89) : type_of% erdos_89.variants.n_dvd_log_n
problems.humanStatement:
This theorem provides a sanity check, showing that the main conjecture (`erdos_89`) is strictly
stronger than the solved Guth and Katz result. It proves that, trivially, if the lower bound
$\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ holds, then the weaker lower bound $\frac{n}{\log n}$ must also hold.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 89 (erdos_89.variants.n_dvd_log_n)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_89.variants.n_dvd_log_n : (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log) =O[atTop] (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Guth and Katz [GuKa15] proved that there are always $\gg \frac{n}{\log n}$
many distinct distances.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 (erdos_890.parts.a)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_890.parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω_gt k (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≤ k
problems.humanStatement:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 (erdos_890.parts.b)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_890.parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, limsup (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal)) * (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 (erdos_890.variants.liminf_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_890.variants.liminf_lower_bound (k : ℕ) : liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≥ k + π k - 1
problems.humanStatement:
A question of Erdős and Selfridge [ErSe67], who observe that
$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\geq k+\pi(k)-1$ for every $k$. This follows from
Pólya's theorem that the set of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded gaps - indeed,
$n(n+1)\cdots (n+k-1)$ is divisible by all primes $\leq k$ and, provided $n$ is large, all but at
most one of $n,n+1,\ldots,n+k-1$ has a prime factor $>k$ by Pólya's theorem.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 (erdos_890.variants.omega_limsup)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_890.variants.omega_limsup : limsup (fun n ↦ (ω n : EReal) * (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1
problems.humanStatement: It is a classical fact that $\limsup_{n\to \infty}\omega(n)\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1.$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891 (erdos_891)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_891 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime), k < ω m
problems.humanStatement:
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891 (erdos_891.variants.case_k_2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_891.variants.case_k_2 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + 6), 3 ≤ ω m
problems.humanStatement:
This is unknown even for $k=2$ - that is, is it true that in every interval of $6$
(sufficiently large) consecutive integers there must exist one with at least $3$ prime factors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891 (erdos_891.variants.schinzel)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_891.variants.schinzel : ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range (k - 1), i.nth Nat.Prime) * k.nth Nat.Prime), k < ω m
problems.humanStatement:
Schinzel deduced from Pólya's theorem [Po18] (that the sequence of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded
gaps) that this is true with $p_1\cdots p_k$ replaced by $p_1\cdots p_{k-1}p_{k+1}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891 (erdos_891.variants.weisenberg)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_891.variants.weisenberg (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) : ∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1), ω m ≤ k
problems.humanStatement:
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 893 (erdos_893)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_893 : answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) : ℝ) / (f n : ℝ)) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Does the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)}$ tend to infinity?

(Other finite limits have been ruled out by [KoLu25], see below)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 893 (erdos_893.variants.unbounded)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_893.variants.unbounded : ¬ BddAbove (Set.range fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) : ℝ) / f n)
problems.humanStatement:
Kovač and Luca [KoLu25] (building on a heuristic independently found by
Cambie (personal communication)) have shown that there is no finite limit, in that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)}$ is unbounded.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 897 (erdos_897.variants.log_growth)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_897.variants.log_growth (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) (C : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ n, |f (n+1) - f n| ≤ C) : ∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ n, f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n
problems.humanStatement:
Wirsing [Wi70] proved that if $|f(n+1)−f(n)| ≤ C$ then $f(n) = c \log n + O(1)$ for some constant
$c$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 897 (erdos_897.variants.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) → ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) → (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) → Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 897 (erdos_897.variants.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) → ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) → (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) → Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/f(n) = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 899 (erdos_899)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_899 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → Tendsto (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 0) → atTop.limsup (fun N => ((A - A : Set ℕ) ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : EReal) / (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru78].

[Ru78] Ruzsa, I. Z., _On the cardinality of {$A+A$}\ and {$A-A$}_. (1978), 933--938.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 9 (erdos_9)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_9 : answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < Erdos9A.upperDensity
problems.humanStatement:
Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus
two powers of 2 positive?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 9 (erdos_9.variants.infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_9.variants.infinite : Erdos9A.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
The set is known to be infinite. In [Er77c] Erdős credits Schinzel with proving that there are
infinitely many odd integers not of this form, but gives no reference.

[Er77c] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III._.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem (erdos_90)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_90 : answer(False) ↔ ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ) (hO : O =O[atTop] (fun n => 1 / (n : ℝ).log.log)), (fun n => (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)) =ᶠ[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + O n)
problems.humanStatement:
Does every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contain at most
$n^{1+O(\frac{1}{\log\log n})}$ many pairs which are distance $1$ apart?

This was
[disproved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/74c24085-19b0-4534-9c90-465b8e29ad73/unit-distance-proof.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI, which constructed (for infinitely many $n$) a set $P$ of $n$ points
in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the number of unit distance pairs in $P$ is at least $n^{1+c}$, where
$c > 0$ is an absolute constant.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem (erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), {n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c) ≤ (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
**Constructive form of the disproof.** There is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that
infinitely many $n$ admit a configuration realising at least $n^{1+c}$ unit distances.

This is the qualitative content of Theorem 1.1 of Alon–Bloom–Gowers–Litt–Sawin–Shankar–
Tsimerman–Wang–Matchett Wood, [*Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695)
(2026). An explicit bound $c \ge 0.014114$ is given by Sawin, [*An explicit lower bound for the
unit distance problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579) (2026); see
`erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit` below.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem (erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound_implies_erdos_90)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound_implies_erdos_90 : type_of% erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound → type_of% erdos_90

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem (erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit : {n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ (1.014114 : ℝ) ≤ (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
**Sawin's explicit exponent.** The constructive disproof can be realised with $c \ge 0.014114$
(absorbing the implicit constant $C$ of Sawin's Theorem 1 into a slightly smaller exponent for
all large enough $n$). Reference: Theorem 1 of Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579)
(2026).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem (erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit_implies_polynomial_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit_implies_polynomial_lower_bound : type_of% erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit → type_of% erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound

problems.title: Erdős Problem 91 (erdos_91)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_91 : (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ UniqueMinimizer n) ↔ answer(sorry)
problems.humanStatement:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 91 (erdos_91.variants.five)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_91.variants.five : UniqueMinimizer 5

For $n = 5$ the regular pentagon is the unique such set (which has two distinct distances).
Erdős mysteriously remarks in [Er90] this was proved by 'a colleague'. (In [Er87b] this is
described as 'a colleague from Zagreb (unfortunately I do not have his letter)'.)
A published proof of this fact is provided by Kovács [Ko24c].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 912 (erdos_912)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_912 : ∃ c > 0, (fun n => (h n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n => c * (n / Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 913 (erdos_913)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_913 : answer(sorry) ↔ { n | Set.InjOn (n * (n + 1)).factorization (n * (n + 1)).primeFactors }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that if
$$
  n(n + 1) = \prod_i p_i^{k_i}
$$
is the factorisation into distinct primes then all exponents $k_i$ are distinct?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 913 (erdos_913.variants.conditional)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_913.variants.conditional (h : { p | p.Prime ∧ (8 * p ^ 2 - 1).Prime }.Infinite) : { n | Set.InjOn (n * (n + 1)).factorization (n * (n + 1)).primeFactors }.Infinite

problems.statementText: theorem erdos_913.variants.infinite_many_8p_sq_add_one_primes : { p | p.Prime ∧ (8 * p ^ 2 - 1).Prime }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: It is likely that there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $8p^2 - 1$ is also prime.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 914 (erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m) (hdeg : G.maxDegree ≤ m - 1) : ∃ C : G.Coloring (Fin m), ∀ i, (C.colorClass i).ncard = r
problems.humanStatement:
Equivalently, every graph with $rm$ vertices and maximum degree at most $m-1$ has a proper vertex
colouring with $m$ colours in which every colour class has exactly $r$ vertices (an equitable
colouring).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 918 (erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.i)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 92 (erdos_92.variants.strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_92.variants.strong : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ n^(c / (n : ℝ).log.log)
problems.humanStatement: Or even $f(n) < n^{c/\log\log n}$ for some constant $c > 0$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 92 (erdos_92.variants.weak)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_92.variants.weak : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ n, (f n : ℝ) ≤ n^(o n)
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{o(1)}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 (erdos_920)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_920 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, k ≥ 4 → ∃ c > 0, (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)) / (log n) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for $k\geq 4$, $f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}$ for some
constant $c_k>0$?

This problem follows immediately from Mattheus and Verstraete's lower bound [MaVe23] for k = 4 and
Bradač's lower bound [Br26] for k ≥ 5.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 (erdos_920.variants.k_eq_3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_920.variants.k_eq_3 : (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) / log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement: It is known that $f_3(n)\asymp (n/\log n)^{1/2}$ (see [erdosproblems.com/1104]).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 (erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_eq_4)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_eq_4 : (fun n ↦ f 4 n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) / (log n) ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
The lower bound $R(4,m) \gg m^3/(\log m)^4$ of Mattheus and Verstraete [MaVe23]
(see [erdosproblems.com/166]) implies $f_4(n) \gg \frac{n^{2/3}}{(\log n)^{4/3}}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 (erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5 (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 3) : ∃ c > 0, (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 2 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) / (log n) ^ c)
problems.humanStatement:
A positive answer to this question for all $k\geq 5$ follows from the lower bound in
[erdosproblems.com/986] given by Bradač [Br26].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 (erdos_920.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_920.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 3) : (fun n ↦ f k n) ≪ (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) * log (log n) / log n) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)))
problems.humanStatement:
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved that
$f_k(n) \ll \left(n\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}.$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930 (erdos_930)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_930 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r > 0, ∃ k, ∀ I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ, (∀ i : Fin r, 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) → (∀ i j : Fin r, i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) → ¬ IsPower (∏ i : Fin r, ∏ m ∈ Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930 (erdos_930.variants.consecutive_integers)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_integers : ∀ n k, 0 ≤ n → 2 ≤ k → ¬ IsPower (∏ m ∈ Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdos and Selfridge [ErSe75] proved that the product of
consecutive integers is never a power (establishing the case $r=1$).

Theorem 1 from [ErSe75].

It is implied from `erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong`.

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930 (erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong : ∀ k l n, 3 ≤ k → 2 ≤ l → nextPrime k ≤ n + k → ∃ p, k ≤ p ∧ p.Prime ∧ ¬ (l ∣ Nat.factorization (∏ m ∈ Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m) p)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k$, $l$, $n$ be integers such that $k \ge 3$, $l \ge 2$ and $n + k \ge p^{(k)}$,
where $p^{(k)}$ is the least prime satisfying $p^{(k)} \ge k$.
Then there is a prime $p \ge k$ for which $l$ does not divide
the multiplicity of the prime factor $p$ in $(n + 1) \ldots (n + k)$.

Theorem 2 from [ErSe75].

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 931 (erdos_931)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_931 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ → { (n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors }.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 931 (erdos_931.variants.additional_condition)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ → {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧ (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős thought perhaps if the two products have the same factors then
$n_2 > 2(n_1 + k_1)$.
It is an open question whether this is true when allowing a finite number of counterexamples.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 931 (erdos_931.variants.additional_condition_nonempty)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition_nonempty : ∃ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ), ∃ (_h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁), ∃ (_h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂), {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧ (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Nonempty
problems.humanStatement: In fact there exist counterexamples, like this one found by AlphaProof.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 931 (erdos_931.variants.exists_prime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_931.variants.exists_prime (k₁ k₂ n₁ n₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁) (h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂) (h₃ : n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂) (h₄ : (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors) : ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ n₁ ≤ p ∧ p ≤ n₂
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős was unable to prove that if the two products have the same factors
then there must exist a prime between $n_1$ and $n_2$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 932 (erdos_932)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_932 : { r : ℕ | 2 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two
integers $p_r < n < p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $< p_{r + 1} - p_r$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 932 (erdos_932.variants.one_le)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_932.variants.one_le : { r : ℕ | 1 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement: Erdős could show that the density of $r$ such that at least one such $n$ exists is $0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 933 (erdos_933)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_933 : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ))) : EReal)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 933 (erdos_933.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_933.variants.lower_bound : Set.Infinite { n : ℕ | ((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) }
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er76d] wrote 'it is easy to see' that for infinitely many $n$, $2^k 3^l > n\log n$.

Steinerberger has noted a simple proof of this fact follows from taking $n=2^{3^r}$ for any
integer $r\geq 1$, when $k=3^r$ and $l=r+1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 933 (erdos_933.variants.mahler)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_933.variants.mahler : ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c n)
problems.humanStatement: Mahler proved (a more general result that implies in particular) that $2^k3^l<n^{1+o(1)}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 936 (erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one : answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (·! + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 936 (erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one : answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (·! - 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 936 (erdos_936.variants.two_pow_add_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_add_one : answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 936 (erdos_936.variants.two_pow_sub_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_sub_one : answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · - 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 937 (erdos_937)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_937 : answer(True) ↔ {p : ℕ × ℕ | IsCoprimePowerfulAP4 p.1 p.2}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Are there infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of coprime powerful numbers?
(A number $n$ is *powerful* if $p \mid n \to p^2 \mid n$; `Nat.Powerful`.)

Erdős [Er76d] asked this; the answer is **yes**: Bajpai, Bennett and Chan [BBC24] proved that
there are infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of pairwise coprime powerful numbers.
(Without coprimality this is easy, and by a theorem of Fermat there are no four *squares* in
arithmetic progression.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 938 (erdos_938)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_938 : answer(sorry) ↔ {P : Finset ℕ | (P : Set ℕ).IsAPOfLength 3 ∧ ∃ k, P = {nth Powerful k, nth Powerful (k + 1), nth Powerful (k + 2)}}.Finite
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A=\{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots\}$ be the sequence of powerful numbers (if $p\mid n$ then $p^2\mid n$).
Are there only finitely many three-term progressions of consecutive terms $n_k,n_{k+1},n_{k+2}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty
problems.humanStatement: If $r≥4$ then can the sum of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers ever be itself $r$-powerful?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.eight)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.eight : (Erdos939Sums 8).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.euler)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.euler : ¬ (∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.card = k - 1 → ¬ (∃ q, ∑ s ∈ S, s ^ k = q ^k))
problems.humanStatement:
Euler had conjectured that the sum of $k - 1$ many $k$-th powers is never a
$k$-th power, but this is false for $k=5$, as Lander and Parkin [LaPa67] found
$$27^5+84^5+110^5+133^5=144^5$$.

[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., "A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture."
  Math. Comp. (1967), 101--103.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.examples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.examples : (∃ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty)
problems.humanStatement:
Cambie has found several examples of the sum of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers being itself
$r$-powerful. For example when $r=5$ we have
$$3761^5=2^8\cdot3^{10}\cdot 5^7 + 2^{12}\cdot 23^6 + 11^5\cdot 13^5$$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.infinite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.infinite : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
If $r≥4$ are there infinitely many sums of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers
that are themselves $r$-powerful?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.seven)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.seven : (Erdos939Sums 7).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 (erdos_939.variants.triples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_939.variants.triples : answer(sorry) ↔ {(a,b,c) | ({a, b, c} : Finset ℕ).Coprime ∧ (3).Full a ∧ (3).Full b ∧ (3).Full c ∧ a + b = c}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Are there infinitely many triples of coprime $3$-powerful numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a + b = c$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 94 (erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ², NonTrilinear (P : Set ℝ²) → ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3
problems.humanStatement:
Lefmann and Theile [LeTh95] prove a stronger version of this question, that
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3$$
under the weaker assumption that no three points are on a line.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 94 (erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ², P.card = n → ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) → ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ ∑ u ∈ distanceSet (regularNGon n), (distanceMultiplicity (regularNGon n) u : ℝ) ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Fishburn also make the stronger conjecture that $\sum f(u_i)^2$ is maximal for the
regular $n$-gon (for large enough $n$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 94 (erdos_94.variants.sum_multiplicity)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_94.variants.sum_multiplicity (P : Finset ℝ²) : ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, distanceMultiplicity P u = P.card.choose 2
problems.humanStatement: Note it is trivial that $\sum f(u_i)=\binom{n}{2}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 (erdos_940)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_940 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3, {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
Let $r \ge 3$. Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most $r$ $r$-powerful numbers
has density $0$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 (erdos_940.variants.large_integers)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_940.variants.large_integers : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3, (∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ x = S.sum)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $r \ge 3$. It is not known if all large integers are the sum of at most $r$-many
$r$-powerful numbers.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 (erdos_940.variants.three_cubes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_940.variants.three_cubes : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ n = (Multiset.map (· ^ 3) S).sum}.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most three cubes has density $0$?

The cubes are those of non-negative integers, which is what `Multiset ℕ` gives. This choice
decides the question: over `ℤ` a sum of three cubes is conjectured to represent every integer
that is not $\pm 4 \bmod 9$, which is density $7/9$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 (erdos_940.variants.three_powerful)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_940.variants.three_powerful : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ x = S.sum
problems.humanStatement:
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

This is the case $r = 2$ of `Erdos1107.erdos_1107`, which asks the same question with $r + 1$
summands, and it is stated there as `Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 (erdos_940.variants.two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_940.variants.two : {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 2 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.

Erdős called this 'easy'. Baker and Brüdern [BaBr94] gave the first proof in the literature.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 942 (erdos_942)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_942 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ (∀ᶠ n in atTop, erdos_942.h n < (Real.log n) ^ (c + o n)) ∧ {n | erdos_942.h n > (Real.log n) ^ (c - o n)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 942 (erdos_942.variants.density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_942.variants.density : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ l, {n | erdos_942.h n = l}.HasDensity (δ l) ∧ ∑' l, δ l = 1
problems.humanStatement:
It is not hard to prove that the density $\delta_l$ of integers for which $h(n) = l$ exists
and satisfies $$\sum_l \delta_l = 1$$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 942 (erdos_942.variants.limsup)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_942.variants.limsup : atTop.limsup (((fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℕ∞)) ∘ erdos_942.h)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement: It is not hard to prove that $\limsup h(n) = \infty$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 943 (erdos_943)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_943 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (sumRep Powerful n) ≤ (n : ℝ)^(o n)
problems.humanStatement: Let $A$ be the set of powerful numbers. Is is true that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n^{o(1)}$ for every $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
 such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k \ge 4$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$?

This was conjectured by Dirac in 1970.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_5)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_5 : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 5 1
problems.humanStatement:
Dirac's conjecture was proved, for $k=5$: There exists a graph $G$ with chromatic number $5$, such
that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$, or in other words:
has no critical edge.

[Br92] Brown, Jason I., A vertex critical graph without critical edges. Discrete Math. (1992), 99--101

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_four)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_four : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 4 1
problems.humanStatement: The case $k=4$ and $r=1$ remains open: Are there $4$-critical graphs without any critical edges?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_ge_five)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_ge_five (k : ℕ) (hk : 5 ≤ k) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1
problems.humanStatement:
Jensen [Je02] gave an construction for $k$-critical graphs without any critical edges for all $k ≥ 5$.

[Je02] Jensen, Tommy R., Dense critical and vertex-critical graphs. Discrete Math. (2002), 63--84.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (h : ¬ (k - 1).Prime) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1
problems.humanStatement:
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 (erdos_944.variants.large_k_for_any_r)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_944.variants.large_k_for_any_r (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r
problems.humanStatement:
Martinsson and Steiner [MaSt25] proved for every $r \ge 1$ if $k$ is sufficiently large, depending
on $r$, there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ such that every vertex is critical,
yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$.

[MaSt25] Martinsson, Anders and Steiner, Raphael, Vertex-critical graphs far from edge-criticality. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2025), 151--157

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945 (erdos_945)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_945 : answer(sorry) ↔ Erdos945Prop
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $F(x) \leq (\log x)^{O(1)}$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945 (erdos_945.variants.constant)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_945.variants.constant : answer(sorry) ↔ Erdos945Constant
problems.humanStatement:
Is there a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all large $x$, every interval $[x, x+(\log x)C]$
contains two integers with the same number of divisors?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945 (erdos_945.variants.equivalence)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_945.variants.equivalence : Erdos945Prop ↔ Erdos945Constant
problems.humanStatement: The two ways of phrasing the conjecture are equivalent.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945 (erdos_945.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_945.variants.lower_bound : (fun (x : ℕ) => (log x).sqrt /(log x).log) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (F n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Mirsky [ErMi52] proved that $\frac{(\log x)^{1/2}}{\log\log x}\ll F(x)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945 (erdos_945.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_945.variants.upper_bound : (fun (n : ℕ) => (F n : ℝ).log) =O[atTop] fun (x : ℕ) => (log x).sqrt /(log x).log
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Mirsky [ErMi52] proved that $\log F(x) \ll \frac{(\log x)^{1/2}}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946 (erdos_946)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946 (erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound : (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count
problems.humanStatement:
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946 (erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound : (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count
problems.humanStatement: Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946 (erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946 (erdos_946.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log )
problems.humanStatement: Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 949 (erdos_949)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_949 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Set ℝ, (∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∉ S) → ∃ A ⊆ Sᶜ, #A = 𝔠 ∧ A + A ⊆ Sᶜ
problems.humanStatement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a + b = c$.
Must there be a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R} \setminus S$ of cardinality continuum such that
$A + A \subseteq \mathbb{R}\setminus S$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : EReal)) = 1
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $\liminf f(n)=1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : EReal)) = ⊤
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ f =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log n))
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that $f(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for all $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.variants.debruijn_erdos_turan)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.variants.debruijn_erdos_turan : (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, f n) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ)) ∧ (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, (f n) ^ 2) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that
$\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x$. They gave no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second
claim is given by Gorodetsky here [mathoverflow/508491].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.variants.sum_primes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.variants.sum_primes : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (Finset.range x).filter Prime, (f p) ^ 2) ~[atTop] fun x ↦ (π x : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
The study of $f(p)$ is even harder, and Erdős could not prove that
$\sum_{p<x}f(p)^2\sim \pi(x)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ y < x, (π x : ℝ) < (π y : ℝ) + ε * (π (x - y) : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős writes that a 'weaker conjecture which is perhaps not quite inaccessible' is that,
for every $\epsilon>0$, if $x$ is sufficiently large there exists $y<x$ such that
$\pi(x)< \pi(y)+\epsilon \pi(x-y)$. Compare this to [855].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 (erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi_implies_f)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi_implies_f (h : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ K > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, ∀ y : ℕ, (y : ℝ) < x - (Real.log x) ^ C → (π x : ℝ) < (π y : ℝ) + K * ((x - y : ℝ) / Real.log x)) : f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n))
problems.humanStatement:
He notes that if $\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)$ for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for
some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 951 (erdos_951)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_951 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 951 (erdos_951.variants.beurling)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling : ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a → ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) → a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 951 (erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : 1 < a 0) (hm : StrictMono a) (he : Erdos951Prop a) : IsBeurlingPrimes a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 952 (erdos_952)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_952 : ∃ (x : ℕ → GaussianInt) (C : ℤ), Function.Injective x ∧ ∀ n, Prime (x n) ∧ (x (n + 1) - x n).norm < C
problems.humanStatement:
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$
such that $\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 0 → { x | s x ∈ A }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has density $0$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ must also have density $0$.

A conjecture of Erdős, Granville, Pomerance, and Spiro [EGPS90].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.empty_preimage)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.empty_preimage : ∃ A : Set ℕ, (∃ d > 0, A.HasDensity d) ∧ { x | s x ∈ A } = ∅
problems.humanStatement: Erdős [Er73b] proved that there are sets $A$ of positive density such that $s^{-1}(A)$ is empty.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.pollack_pomerance_thompson_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.pollack_pomerance_thompson_bound : ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (count A n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) + ε n)) → { x | s x ∈ A }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
Pollack, Pomerance, and Thompson [PPT18] prove that if $\epsilon(x)=o(1)$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$
has size at most $x^{1/2+\epsilon(x)}$ then $\#\{ n\leq x: s(n)\in A\} =o(x)$ as $x\to \infty$. It
follows that (using $s(n)\ll n\log\log n$) if $A$ grows like
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\leq x^{1/2+o(1)}$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ has density $0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.pollack_primes)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.pollack_primes : { x | Nat.Prime (s x) }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement: Pollack [Po14b] has shown that this is true if $A$ is the set of primes.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.positive_density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.positive_density : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 0 ∧ (∃ d > 0, (s '' A).HasDensity d)
problems.humanStatement:
It is possible for $s(A)$ to have positive density even if $A$ has zero density (for example
taking $A$ to be the product of two distinct primes).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.troupe_sum_of_two_squares)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.troupe_sum_of_two_squares : { x | ∃ a b : ℕ, s x = a^2 + b^2 }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
Troupe [Tr20] has also shown this is true if $A$ is the set of integers which are the sum of two
squares.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 (erdos_955.variants.troupe_unusually_many_prime_factors)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_955.variants.troupe_unusually_many_prime_factors : ∀ ε > 0, { x | (1 + ε) * Real.log (Real.log (s x)) < (ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (s x) : ℝ) }.HasDensity 0
problems.humanStatement:
Troupe [Tr15] has shown that this is true if $A$ is the set of integers with unusually many prime
factors.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 959 (erdos_959)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_959 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (extremalGap n) / Real.log n) atTop (𝓝 γ)
problems.humanStatement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of size $n$ and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be
the set of distinct distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the number of times
the distance $d$ is determined, ordered so that
$f(d_1)\geq f(d_2)\geq \cdots \geq f(d_k)$. Estimate
$$\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2)),$$
where the maximum is taken over all $A$ of size $n$ (this is `extremalGap n`).

The asymptotic order of `extremalGap` is not known; a natural formalization of
"estimate" asks whether it has a well-defined polynomial growth exponent.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 96 (erdos_96)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_96 : answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n => (maxConvexUnitDistances n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
If $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then there are $O(n)$ many pairs which are
distance $1$ apart.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, f k < log k ^ C
problems.humanStatement: It is conjectured that $f(k) \ll (\log k)^O(1)$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961.sylvester_schur)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961.sylvester_schur (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : Erdos961Prop k k
problems.humanStatement:
Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that every set of $k$ consecutive integers greater than $k$
contains an integer divisible by a prime greater than $k$, i.e. not $(k+1)$-smooth.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961.variants.erdos_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961.variants.erdos_upper_bound : ∀ᶠ k in atTop, f k < 3 * k / log k
problems.humanStatement: Erdos [Er55d] proved $f(k) < 3 \frac{k}{\log k}$ for sufficiently large $k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961.variants.jutila_ramachandra_shorey_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961.variants.jutila_ramachandra_shorey_upper_bound : (fun k => (f k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun k => log (log (log k)) / log (log k) * (k / log k)
problems.humanStatement:
Jutila [Ju74], and Ramachandra--Shorey [RaSh73] proved a stronger upper bound
$f(k) \ll \frac{\log \log \log k}{\log \log k} \frac{k}{\log k}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961.variants.sylvester_schur_1_1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961.variants.sylvester_schur_1_1 : Erdos961Prop 1 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 (erdos_961.variants.well_defined)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_961.variants.well_defined (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k): ∃ n, Erdos961Prop k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962 (erdos_962)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_962 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, log (k n : ℝ) ≤ rpow (log n) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε n)
problems.humanStatement:
Main conjecture:

$\log k(n) \le (\log n)^{(1/2 + o(1))}$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962 (erdos_962.variants.tang_lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_962.variants.tang_lower_bound : ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 / sqrt 2 - ε n) * sqrt (log n * log (log n)) ≤ log (k n : ℝ)
problems.humanStatement:
Tang's lower bound [Tang]:

$\log k(n) \ge (1/\sqrt{2} - o(1)) * \sqrt{\log n * \log \log n}$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962 (erdos_962.variants.tao_upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_962.variants.tao_upper_bound : ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (k n : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε n) * sqrt n
problems.humanStatement:
Tao's upper bound [Tao]:

$k(n) \le (1 + o(1)) * n^{1/2}$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 965 (erdos_965)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_965 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧ ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A) (d ∈ A), a ≠ b → c ≠ d → f (a + b) = f (c + d)
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

In [Ko16] Péter Komjáth constructed a counterexample.
The same result was proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 965 (erdos_965.variants.generalization)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_965.variants.generalization : answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧ ∀ s t : Finset ℝ, ↑s ⊆ A → ↑t ⊆ A → s.card = k → t.card = k → f (s.sum id) = f (t.sum id)
problems.humanStatement: In fact, in both [Ko16] and [SWCol] a generalized example for $k$-sums is constructed.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 967 (erdos_967.variants.finite)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_967.variants.finite : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ A, 1 < n) → ∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑ n ∈ A, summand t n) ≠ 0
problems.humanStatement: It remains open whether this is true for every finite sequence of integers.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 967 (erdos_967.variants.tauberian)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_967.variants.tauberian (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha₀ : 1 < a 0) (hsum : Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / (a k : ℝ))) : (∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑' k, summand t (a k)) ≠ 0) ↔ ∀ f : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone f → (∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ f x) → (∀ x < 1, f x = 0) → (∀ x y : ℝ, BddAbove (f '' Set.Icc x y)) → Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (f x + ∑' k, f (x / (a k : ℝ))) / x) atTop (𝓝 (1 + ∑' k, 1 / (a k : ℝ))) → Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => f x / x) atTop (𝓝 1)
problems.humanStatement:
Their interest in this problem arose from their proof that the statement that there are no such
zeros is equivalent to the fact that, for any non-decreasing $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$
which is bounded on every bounded interval and is $=0$ for $x<1$, the relationship
$$f(x)+\sum_k f(x/a_k)=\left(1+\sum_k \frac{1}{a_k}+o(1)\right)x$$
implies $f(x)=(1+o(1))x$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 967 (erdos_967.variants.two_three_five)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_967.variants.two_three_five : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑ n ∈ ({2, 3, 5} : Finset ℕ), summand t n) ≠ 0
problems.humanStatement:
A question of Erdős and Ingham [ErIn64]. The simplest case they could not decide this question
for was the finite sequence $\{2,3,5\}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 967 (erdos_967.variants.yip)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_967.variants.yip (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) : ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ 1 < a 0 ∧ Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / (a k : ℝ)) ∧ (1 + (∑' k, summand t (a k)) = 0)
problems.humanStatement:
Yip [Yi25] has proved that this is not always true - in fact, for any real $t\neq 0$, there
exists a sequence of integers $1<a_1<\cdots$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$ and
$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}=0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 (erdos_968)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_968 : answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < {n : ℕ | u n < u (n + 1)}.lowerDensity
problems.humanStatement: Does the set `{n | u n < u (n+1)}` have positive lower density?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 (erdos_968.variants.decreasing_steps_pos_lower_density)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_968.variants.decreasing_steps_pos_lower_density : 0 < {n : ℕ | u n > u (n + 1)}.lowerDensity
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Prachar proved that the set `{n | u n > u (n+1)}` has positive lower density
(see [ErPr61]).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 (erdos_968.variants.infinite_decreasingTriples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_decreasingTriples : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | u n > u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) > u (n + 2)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ > uₙ₊₁ > uₙ₊₂`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 (erdos_968.variants.infinite_increasingTriples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_increasingTriples : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | u n < u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) < u (n + 2)}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement: Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ < uₙ₊₁ < uₙ₊₂`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 (erdos_968.variants.sum_abs_diff_isTheta_log_sq)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_968.variants.sum_abs_diff_isTheta_log_sq : (fun x : ℕ => ∑ n < Nat.primeCounting' x, |u (n + 1) - u n|) =Θ[atTop] fun x : ℕ => log x ^ 2
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős and Prachar proved `∑_{pₙ < x} |u (n+1) - u n| ≍ (log x)^2` (see [ErPr61]).

We encode `∑_{pₙ < x}` as a sum over `n < Nat.primeCounting' x` (the number of primes `< x`).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 (erdos_97)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_97 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty → ConvexIndep A → ¬HasNEquidistantProperty 4 A
problems.humanStatement: Does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 (erdos_97.variants.k_equidistant)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_97.variants.k_equidistant : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty → ConvexIndep A → ¬HasNEquidistantProperty k A
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős also conjectured that there is a $k$ for which every convex polygon has a vertex
with no other $k$ vertices equidistant from it.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 (erdos_97.variants.three_equidistant)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_97.variants.three_equidistant : ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty ∧ ConvexIndep A ∧ HasNEquidistantProperty 3 A
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős originally conjectured this (in [Er46b]) with no 3 vertices equidistant,
but Danzer found a convex polygon on 9 points such that every vertex has three
vertices equidistant from it (but this distance depends on the vertex).
Danzer's construction is explained in [Er87b].

[Er46b] Erdős, P., _On sets of distances of $n$ points_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248-250.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 (erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance : ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty ∧ ConvexIndep A ∧ HasNUnitDistanceProperty 3 A
problems.humanStatement:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] have found a convex polygon on 20 points such that
every vertex has three vertices equidistant from it (and this distance is the same for all vertices).

[FiRe92] Fishburn, P. C. and Reeds, J. A., _Unit distances between vertices of a convex polygon_. Comput. Geom. (1992), 81-91.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 (erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance_cut_min)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance_cut_min : sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (V : Finset ℝ²) (A B : Finset ℝ²), n = V.card ∧ ConvexIndep V ∧ A.Nonempty ∧ B.Nonempty ∧ IsCut V A B ∧ HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 B A ∧ HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 A B} = 20
problems.humanStatement:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] also proved that the smallest $n$ for which there exists
a convex $n$-gon and a cut $\{A, B\}$ of its vertices such that $|\{b \in B : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$
for all $a \in A$, and $|\{a \in A : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$ for all $b \in B$, is $n = 20$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971 (erdos_971)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_971 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d in atTop, C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤ #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) > (1 + c) * d.totient * log d}
problems.humanStatement:
Let `p(a, d)` be the least prime congruent to `a (mod d)`.
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that for all large `d`,
`p(a, d) > (1 + c) * φ(d) * log d` for `≫ φ(d)` many values of `a`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971 (erdos_971.variants.infinite_sequence)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_971.variants.infinite_sequence : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), {d : ℕ | C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤ #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) > (1 + c) * d.totient * log d}}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that the statement in `erdos_971` holds for infinitely many values of `d`.

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971 (erdos_971.variants.many_small)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_971.variants.many_small : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d in atTop, C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤ #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) < ε * d.totient * log d}
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that for any `ε > 0` we have `p(a, d) < ε * φ(d) * log d` for `≫_ε φ(d)` many
values of `a` (for all large `d`).

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 972 (erdos_972)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_972 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (primeSet α).Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 (erdos_973)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_973 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ, z 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧ (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 (erdos_973.variants.le_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_973.variants.le_one : ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ, z 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 (erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∀ M_2 : ℝ, IsGLB { M | ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ, (∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∃ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧ (∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), M = ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧ ∀ m ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M) } M_2 → (1.746 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < (1.745 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 (erdos_973.variants.tang)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_973.variants.tang : ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ, (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) → ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥ (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ))
problems.humanStatement:
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 974 (erdos_974.variants.two_tuples)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_974.variants.two_tuples {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (z : Fin n → ℂ) (hz : z 0 = 1) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≠ b) (ha : ∀ j < n - 1, ∑ i, z i ^ (a + j) = 0) (hb : ∀ j < n - 1, ∑ i, z i ^ (b + j) = 0) : IsTuranConfiguration z
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős speculates that this may be true if there are two distinct $(n-1)$-tuples of consecutive
values of $s_k$ which are $0$. He does not elaborate on what the 'essentially' may mean precisely.

This is true (in the stronger form with only two such tuples) - in fact if $n$ is odd then the
$z_i$ must be exactly the $n$th roots of unity, and if $n$ is even they must be the vertices of
two regular $(n/2)$-gons with the same circumscribed circle centred at the origin. This was first
proved by Tijdeman [Ti66]. An independent proof of this was given in the comments section by Hu,
Tang, and Zhang.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ f : ℤ[X], f.natDegree ≠ 0 → Irreducible f → (∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum f x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975.variants.lower_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975.variants.lower_bound (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hfdeg : f.natDegree ≠ 0) (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) : (fun x ↦ x * log x) =O[atTop] Erdos975Sum f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1 : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum (X ^ 2 + 1) x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1_strong)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1_strong : (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum (X ^ 2 + 1) x - (3 / π) * x * log x) =O[atTop] id
problems.humanStatement:
More concrete example for $f(n) = n^2 + 1$, where the asymptote is
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(n^2 + 1) \sim \frac{3}{\pi} x \log x + O(x)$. See Tao's blog [T].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975.variants.quadratic)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975.variants.quadratic (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval ↑n) (hf_degree : f.degree = 2) (c : ℝ) : c = answer(sorry) → 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum f x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)
problems.humanStatement:
When $f$ is an irreducible quadratic polynomial, the question is answered first by Hooley [Ho63].
More compact expression of the constant in terms of Hurwitz class numbers (when $a = 1$)
is given by McKey in [Mc95], [Mc97], [Mc99].

TODO: formalize Hurwitz class numbers and the expression of the constant in terms of them.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975 (erdos_975.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_975.variants.upper_bound (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) : Erdos975Sum f =O[atTop] (fun x ↦ x * log x)
problems.humanStatement: The correctness of the growth rate is shown in [Va39] (lower bound) and [Er52b] (upper bound).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978 (erdos_978.parts.i)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_978.parts.i {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree) (hp2 : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff) (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) : HasPosDensity {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978 (erdos_978.parts.ii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_978.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 → (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff → (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) → {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite
problems.humanStatement:
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978 (erdos_978.parts.iii)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_978.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978 (erdos_978.variants.sub_one)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_one {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree) (hp : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff) : {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978 (erdos_978.variants.sub_two)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_two {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 9 ≤ f.natDegree) (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) : {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 979 (erdos_979)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_979 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n k).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k ≥ 2$, and let $f_k(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n = p_1^k + \dots + p_k^k$,
where the $p_i$ are prime numbers. Is it true that $\limsup f_k(n) = \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 979 (erdos_979.variants.k2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_979.variants.k2 : Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n 2).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős [Er37b] proved that if $f_2(n)$ counts the number of solutions to $n = p_1^2 + p_2^2$, where $p_1$ and $p_2$ are prime numbers, then $\limsup f_2(n) = \infty$.

[Er37b] Erdős, Paul, On the Sum and Difference of Squares of Primes. J. London Math. Soc. (1937), 133--136.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 979 (erdos_979.variants.k3)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_979.variants.k3 : Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n 3).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤
problems.humanStatement: Erdős (unpublished)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 98 (erdos_98)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_98 : answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((h n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))) atTop atTop
problems.humanStatement:
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 98 (erdos_98.variants.upper_bound)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_98.variants.upper_bound : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (h n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős could not even prove $h(n)\geq n$. Pach has shown $h(n) < n^{\log_2 3}$.
Erdős, Füredi, and Pach [EFPR93] have improved this to
$h(n) < n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$ for some constant $c>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 982 (erdos_982)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_982 (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p) (hp' : EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p) : ∃ (i : Fin n), { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2
problems.humanStatement:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 985 (erdos_985)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_985 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp_prime : p.Prime) (hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2), ∃ q, q.Prime ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1
problems.humanStatement: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 985 (erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root : Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨ orderOf (3 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨ orderOf (5 : ZMod p) = p - 1)}
problems.humanStatement: Heath-Brown proved that at least one of 2, 3, or 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 99 (erdos_99)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_99 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = n → HasMinDist1 A → (IsMinOn (fun B: Finset ℝ² => diam (B : Set ℝ²)) {B : Finset ℝ² | B.card = n ∧ HasMinDist1 B} A) → ∃ᵉ (p ∈ A) (q ∈ A) (r ∈ A), FormsEquilateralTriangle p q r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 990 (erdos_990.variants.counterexample)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_990.variants.counterexample : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ f.support.card = n ∧ M f < 3 ∧ ∃ x : ℝ, 0 < x ∧ f.rootMultiplicity (x : ℂ) = n - 1
problems.humanStatement:
An internal OpenAI model (see [APSSV26b]) has disproved the conjecture, constructing, for every
$n\geq 1$, a polynomial $f$ with $n$ non-zero coefficients such that $M<3$ and with a positive real
zero of multiplicity $n-1$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 990 (erdos_990.variants.erdos_turan)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_990.variants.erdos_turan : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 → ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ β → β ≤ 2 * π → |(rootArgCount f (Set.Icc α β) : ℝ) - (β - α) / (2 * π) * (f.natDegree : ℝ)| ≤ C * Real.sqrt ((f.natDegree : ℝ) * Real.log (M f))
problems.humanStatement: Erdős and Turán [ErTu50] proved such an upper bound with $n$ replaced by $d$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 990 (erdos_990.variants.hayman)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_990.variants.hayman : ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 → ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ β → β ≤ 2 * π → |(rootArgCount f (Set.Icc α β) : ℝ) - (β - α) / (2 * π) * (f.natDegree : ℝ)| ≤ (f.support.card : ℝ) - 1
problems.humanStatement:
Hayman [Ha72b] proved
$$
\left\lvert (\# \theta_i \in I) - \frac{\lvert I\rvert}{2\pi}d\right\rvert \leq n-1,
$$
and noted this is essentially sharp since $f(x)=(x^{p}-1)^{n-1}$ has $n$ non-zero coefficients and
has $1$ as a positive real zero of multiplicity $n-1$ (although for this $f$ the parameter $M$
becomes very large).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 996 (erdos_996)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_996 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 996 (erdos_996.variants.log2)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_996.variants.log2 : ∀ (C : ℝ), 0.5 < C → ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 997 (erdos_997.variants.irrational)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_997.variants.irrational : ∃ α : ℝ, Irrational α ∧ ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun n ↦ Int.fract (α * (n.nth Nat.Prime)))
problems.humanStatement:
He also claimed in [Er64b] to have proved that there exists an irrational $\alpha$ for which
$\{\alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed. He later retracted this claim in [Er85e], saying "The
theorem is no doubt correct and perhaps will not be difficult to prove but I never was able to
reconstruct my 'proof' which perhaps never existed."

The existence of such an $\alpha$ was established by Champagne, Le, Liu, and Wooley [CLLW24].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 997 (erdos_997.variants.lacunary)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_997.variants.lacunary (n : ℕ → ℕ) (h : IsLacunary n) : ∀ᵐ α, ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun k ↦ Int.fract (α * (n k : ℝ)))
problems.humanStatement:
Erdős proved that, if $n_k$ is a lacunary sequence, then the sequence $\{ \alpha n_k\}$ is not
well-distributed for almost all $\alpha$.

problems.title: The Erdős–Moser equation (erdos_moser_conjecture)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_moser_conjecture : ∀ k m : ℕ, 0 < k → 0 < m → powerSum k m = m ^ k → k = 1 ∧ m = 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 70 (erdos_rado)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_rado (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 (𝔠).ord (ω + n) 4
problems.humanStatement:
**Erdős–Rado partial result**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for any
$2 \le n < \omega$. Positive partial answer to Problem 70 with $\beta = \omega + n$
and the blue side fixed at $4$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 699 (erdos_szekeres_strengthening)
problems.statementText: theorem erdos_szekeres_strengthening : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ E : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ), ∀ n i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → (n, i, j) ∉ E → ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 124 (erdos124.melfi_construction)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos124.melfi_construction {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono d ∧ ∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ε ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0) ∧ ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n
problems.humanStatement:
For any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an infinite sequence $2 \le d_0 < d_1 < \dots$ such
that all sufficiently large integer can be written as $\sum_{i \in I} a_i$ where $a_i$ has only
the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$,
but $\sum_{i \in I} \frac 1{d_i - 1} \le \varepsilon$.

Proved by Melfi [Me04]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 124 (erdos124.ne_zero)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos124.ne_zero : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → D.gcd id = 1 → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d k
problems.humanStatement:
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 124 (erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers 3 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 4 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 7 1
problems.humanStatement:
All sufficiently large integers can be written as $a + b + c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are
divisible by $3$, $4$, and $7$ respectively, and after division by that base have only the
digits $0, 1$ in that base.

Proved by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 124 (erdos124.zero)
problems.statementText: lemma erdos124.zero : answer(True) ↔ ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0
problems.humanStatement:
Let  $3 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_r$ be integers such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Erdős [Er97], solved by Boris Alexeev using Aristotle.

problems.statementText: lemma erdos170 : Filter.Tendsto (fun N => F N / √N) Filter.atTop (𝓝 answer(sorry))
